comments.body:
## Research findings — LIN-1892 (beats 1–4, grounding `7a43ef25`)

Scope: research only. This comment records the evidence; a sibling description section keeps the compact version.

### Flow map (sign-in → account → workspace → token)
Every sign-in path converges on `establishAccount` (`lib/account-session.js:111`) — the single seam. Production call sites (11, 6 files):
- Linear OAuth — `routes/auth.js:258` (add-source) / `:378` (mode:new), scope `viewer.id`
- Linear PAT auto-login — `lib/pat-session.js:89`, scope `viewer.id`
- GitHub App/OAuth — `lib/github-install-flow.js:551/605/684`, scope `humanId`, creds `{login}`
- GitHub Projects — same flow, same `github` identity (`account-session.js:17-19` Q3)
- Jira OAuth/API-token — `routes/jira-auth.js:266/549/687/771`, scope `myself.accountId`
- Local — `routes/workspace.js:114`, scope random `urlKey` (`POST /workspace/new:69`)

`establishAccount` → `findAccountByIdentity` (`account-store.js:91`) → reuse/mint/link (`:139-169`) → `linkIdentity` (`:107`, **strict, no auto-merge**) → `bindAccountToWorkspace` (`account-session.js:219`) → `session.accountId` + `identityAuthenticatedAt` (`:220-224`). Session resolves workspaces via `session.workspaces[]` (`server.js:1975`). Token resolution: `resolveWorkspaceAccess` (`server.js:2160`) canonicalizes owner (`:2182-2189`), scans sessions (`:2223`) via `selectOwnerWorkspaceToken` (`workspace-token-resolver.js:113`).

### LIN-2231 — fully done, not a prerequisite
The credential/ownership migration is complete. Children all `Done`: LIN-2233 (`0c3dfd1e`), LIN-2234 (`2a95b7bb`), LIN-2235 (`80b35088`), LIN-2236 (`edbe5e7e`), LIN-2237 (`28ddf05`); one-time production repair executed 2026-08-23. `mergeAccounts` (`account-store.js:225`) and `resolveCanonicalAccountId` (`:304`) are live. The **durable workspace document** is a different, *parked* line (LIN-1354 Canceled, LIN-1368 Done "park pre-launch") — `WorkspaceStore` constructed (`server.js:565`) but wired to no route; workspaces live only in the session blob. This has **no bearing** on the email door.

### LIN-2149 / LIN-2883 boundaries
- LIN-2149 (`Connection` noun) moves credentials from `workspace.bindings[]` to a per-connection record — orthogonal to the email door (which touches no workspace credential); functionally independent either side (Ruling #4).
- LIN-2883 (machines): `ownerAccountId` = a single stable Harbour account UUID carried on the machine/workspace **from day one** so later sharing is additive grants, never a re-key.

### Import-cycle placement rule (binds the new route)
Four `lib/providers/*/index.js → routes/*-auth.js` upward edges (`linear:34`, `github:67`, `github-projects:60`, `jira:103`) all sit inside static cycles through the `lib/providers/index.js` barrel (2026-09-26 Drift & Coherence, LIN-675). **Email is an identity type, not a provider**: a `lib/` factory (e.g. `lib/email-auth-router.js`) + thin `routes/` mount, injected from `server.js` (as `createWorkspaceRoutes`/`createAccountMergeRoutes` are), importing `lib/` downward only — no new `lib/→routes/` edge, never a 5th provider module.

### Motivation — the promised cold-start door
`docs/v1.md:43-50` promises "log in with email" as step 1; the 2026-09-26 Onboarding Review (R2-7) records it as not advertised and not reachable. This ticket is the home of that gap.

### Magic-link security contract (each with a source)
Single-use, short-expiry token stored **hashed** at rest; no account enumeration (send returns an identical response whether or not the email exists — precedent: conflict copy never discloses the other id, `account-conflict.js:59`); send-rate limiting via the existing `express-rate-limit` convention (`routes/proxy.js:250`, `routes/dispatch.js:136`); link-scanner prefetch safe (**GET must not consume; confirm by POST/click**); session fixation handled by regenerating on sign-in (`routes/auth.js:342`); CSRF per the codebase convention (`SameSite=Lax` cookie `server.js:826` + opaque session nonce — there is no csurf/token middleware).

### Transactional email provider — recommend Resend
Plain HTTPS `POST /emails` + `Bearer` key (no SDK; the project has no build step and no mail lib today). Alternates: Brevo (free tier), SES (sandbox-approval friction), Postmark/Mailgun (trial-only). **Operator-only steps**: create account + API key (env), verify sending-domain DNS (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), set `EMAIL_FROM`. Transport must be an **injectable `fetch` seam defaulting to a console logger** when unconfigured or `NODE_ENV=test`, so local dev and the hermetic unit suite (`tests/fixtures/network-guard.js`) never open a non-loopback socket.

### Provider email today (verified-email join)
| Provider | Email available? | Gets verified email | Owner-only change needed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linear | yes — `viewer()` has `{id,name,email}` (`linear/index.js:1349-1357`); auth currently uses `fetchViewer` (id-only, `:222-227`) | same OAuth scope, wider field selection | **no** |
| GitHub App/OAuth | no — `fetchViewer` returns `{id,login,name}` (`github/index.js:652-655`); authorize sends no scope (`app-auth.js:436-438`); install path yields `login/userId` only | needs "Email addresses" App permission (`user:email`) | **yes** → **avoided**: Decision 2's type-your-email fallback covers GitHub with zero App change |
| GitHub Projects | same as GitHub | same | same |
| Jira | `emailAddress` optional/privacy-nullable (`jira/index.js:1422-1435`); `read:jira-user` already in scope | none guaranteed | **no** — fallback covers null |

### Linking rules
(a) verified provider email matching an existing account's `email` identity → auto-link: resolve `findAccountByIdentity('email', normalized)` *above* `establishAccount` and link the arriving provider identity onto that account (strict `linkIdentity` untouched); (b) no/unverified email → "type your email" + magic link, hold provider identity+workspace in session (`oauthIntent`/`pendingMerge` pattern, `account-conflict.js:76`), link on confirm; (c) unmatched verified email → mint fresh account and attach **both** `email` + provider identities; (d) existing local-path accounts (random `urlKey` identity) → attach an `'email'` identity in-session via the same verification — additive, no migration, becomes re-enterable.

### `ownerAccountId` placement — the edge, not the session
Rejected: (i) session-entry field (per-session copy — the LIN-2231-retired pattern, `server.js:2223`); (iii) deriving from the owner-credential key (incomplete — no record for local/PAT/github-family). **Chosen**: the `account-workspace-store` edge — the universal durable record every path writes via `bindAccountToWorkspace`; owner = canonicalized sole bound account; add an explicit owner mark at creation. Not a parallel representation (it *is* the membership record) and does not pre-decide credential placement or LIN-2149. Un-parking WorkspaceStore is **not** required.

**Backfill (Decision 3 recorded faithfully):** new workspaces get the owner mark at creation; existing single-owner workspaces backfill by **pure derivation** (canonicalized sole bound account). Two populations **cannot** be bounded from source: (a) workspaces bound to more than one distinct canonical account, and (b) workspaces with **no edge at all** (pre-LIN-1329 or otherwise missing). Recommended first implementation step: a **read-only dry-run count** of (a) and (b). If both zero the question is moot; if non-zero, assigning those owners is **a data decision that is John's** — an open question for the plan, not settled here.

**One-time merge of John's existing accounts (Ruling #4):** uses `mergeAccounts` (`account-store.js:225`; alias-only — never touches `identities[]`, so it does not unify emails/content). It is **not a prerequisite** of the email door and is **out of this ticket's implementation scope** — John's data decision, not to be performed by this work.

### Class inventory (queries at `7a43ef25`)
- `establishAccount(` over `routes lib server.js` → 11 production sites (listed above).
- `findAccountByIdentity|linkIdentity(|createAccount(|mergeAccounts(|resolveCanonicalAccountId(` → `account-store.js`, `account-session.js`, `account-merge.js:106`, `openrouter-key-resolver.js:189`, `credential-invariant-sweep.js:149`, `server.js:2184`.
- `resolveWorkspaceAccess(` → `routes/proxy.js:672` (+ `getWorkspaceAccessToken` `server.js:2394`).
- Sign-in entry rendering: `render-pages.js:78-85`, `landing-hero.js:56-61`, `navbar.js:80-90/483-492`; `entryCta` at `linear:2334`/`github:509`/`jira:1380` (github-projects/local none). No email CTA exists.
- **Not sweepable from source**: production account populations (provider-only / local-`urlKey` / merged-aliased), email deliverability + a sending domain that must be created, provider free-tier limits.

### Runtime witness (criterion: "a new person can sign in by email")
Unit-hermetic `node --test` route test with the injectable console-transport capturing the magic link. Assert: submit email → transport emits link → **POST confirm consumes it** → `session.accountId` equals a **fresh** account whose `identities[]` contains `{provider:'email', scope}` → lands on a signed-in screen; **re-entry**: a second empty session + same email resolves the **same** account (no second mint). Fails at HEAD (no `/auth/email` route → 404; no `email` identity ever written; no transport) and asserts the sign-in *outcome*, not a 200-from-send proxy.

### Adversarial findings
Siblings covered (GitHub Projects shares `github-install-flow`; Jira basic+OAuth in `jira-auth.js`; PAT in `pat-session.js`; local in `workspace.js`); `openrouter-auth.js` is a credential surface keyed off `session.accountId`, not an identity — must not regress, out of the identity class. ## Gating findings (the revision must address these)

### G1 — S2 `POST /auth/email/confirm` is open to login CSRF
**What's wrong.** The plan's CSRF story is "`sameSite:'lax'` + POST-only consumption" (§Cross-cutting invariants), and its `requestNonceHash` only drives a GET-page notice. Neither stops a *login* CSRF, because that attack doesn't need the victim's existing cookie.

**Evidence.**
- Session cookie is `sameSite:'lax'` with `saveUninitialized:false` (`server.js:827-837`).
- There is no CSRF or Origin/`Sec-Fetch-Site` middleware anywhere in `server.js`, `lib/` or `routes/` (grep for `csrf|origin|sec-fetch` finds only the OAuth `state` comments).
- The provider flows are protected only because the OAuth `state` nonce is bound to the initiating session (`routes/auth.js:66-74, :135`; consumed per LIN-2499 at `routes/auth.js:312`). The email flow has no equivalent.

**Failure scenario.**
1. The attacker requests a magic link for their own address and receives token T.
2. The attacker gets the victim's browser to auto-submit a cross-site form: `POST https://harbour.cat/auth/email/confirm` with `t=T`.
3. Under Lax the victim's cookie isn't sent, so a fresh session is created. The consume succeeds, the session is saved, and the cookie is set on the top-level navigation. The victim is now signed in as the attacker.
4. The victim then connects Linear. `establishAccount`'s existing `else if (session.accountId)` branch (`lib/account-session.js` ~:160, "linking a NEW identity onto the current account") attaches the victim's Linear identity to the attacker's account. `persistOwnerCredential` (`routes/auth.js` ~:397) stores the victim's durable credential under the attacker's accountId.
5. The victim's future Linear sign-ins resolve to the attacker's account.

**What the revision must address.** State a defence that makes the consuming POST unforgeable cross-site while still allowing a legitimate open-in-another-browser confirm. Add an adversarial test: a POST without a session cookie, or without the defence's proof, is refused and **nothing is consumed**. The confirm page showing the email address stays as the mitigation for a user who is simply sent a link and clicks it.

### G2 — S2's navbar "Continue with email" CTA can never render
**What's wrong.** Surface List / S2 item 7 says to thread `emailEnabled` into `navbar.js` (isLanding :86-105) "like `githubEnabled`/`jiraEnabled`", passed only via the two `renderLandingPage` calls (`server.js:1462, :1781`). That can't reach the navbar CTA.

**Evidence.**
- `renderLandingPage` renders the navbar with `minimalNav: true` (`lib/render-landing.js:276`), and the navbar returns `''` for `isLanding && minimalNav` (`lib/components/navbar.js:61-63`).
- The `isLanding` bar renders **only** on the unauthenticated `/swipe`, `/swim` and `/ship` previews (`server.js:1805, :1827, :1846`). There it is the *sole* sign-in path (comment at `navbar.js:58-60, :67-68`), pinned by `tests/e2e/landing-swipe.spec.js:20-31` and `tests/e2e/landing-swim.spec.js:21-27`.
- The navbar does **not** take threaded provider flags. LIN-1890 E4 (`navbar.js:70-77`) deliberately calls the provider predicate instead of threading through ~7 renderers. Email isn't in the registry (by design), so no such predicate exists for it.

**Failure scenario.** The unit test "email CTA renders iff `emailEnabled`" passes, but in production no navbar anywhere ever shows the email CTA. Visitors on the preview pages have no email door.

**What the revision must address.** Give a mechanism by which the landing navbar knows email is configured, consistent with the LIN-1890 E4 rule and N6's import constraint. Name the preview routes as surfaces, and extend the preview e2e specs to assert the CTA.

### G3 — S3's step middleware has no configuration or test-mode gate
**What's wrong.** S3 item 1 ("Step middleware") fires whenever `session.accountId` is set and `session.emailPrompt === undefined`. Nothing gates it on email sign-in being available.

**Evidence and failure scenarios.**
- **Production unconfigured** (the stated default until the Operator Prerequisites are done): `transport` is `null` and `/auth/email*` returns 503 (S2). Every provider user is still redirected once to `/auth/email/register`, whose Send can't work.
- **Test mode**: `NODE_ENV=test` constructs the capture transport, so email counts as configured. The test login fixture establishes a real `accountId` (`routes/test.js:217`). **44 of 83** e2e specs `goto('/workspace/…')`, and each would be redirected once to the register page. The plan only says `account-merge.spec.js` "stays green".

**What the revision must address.** Specify the step's gate: it must not fire when email sign-in is unavailable. Specify the test-mode behaviour so the existing e2e fleet is unaffected unless a spec opts in, with a test for each.

## Revision closure: gating findings from `4e29a086`

### G1: login CSRF on `POST /auth/email/confirm` → **PASS**

The verdict's attack, walked step by step against revision 1:

1. *The attacker mints token T for their own address.* Still possible in their own browser, and not meant to be blocked.
2. *A cross-site auto-submitted `POST /auth/email/confirm t=T` runs in the victim's browser.* It's refused at S2 item 4 (a), because `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` → 403. It's also refused independently at (b). The session cookie is explicitly `sameSite:'lax'` (`server.js:835`), so a cross-site POST carries no cookie. express-session then gives the handler a fresh empty session with no `emailConfirm`, so `verifyAndClearConfirmNonce` fails → 403. Chrome's 2-minute Lax-POST allowance applies only to cookies with **no** SameSite attribute, so the plan's claim is correct. With `saveUninitialized:false` (`server.js:831`), that refused, unmodified session is never saved: no `Set-Cookie`, and the victim's own session is untouched.
3. *The consume succeeds and the victim is signed in as the attacker.* Unreachable. (a)/(b) run before (b′), which is only a DB **read** (peek + owner lookup), and before (c) `consume`, the first write. **A refusal consumes nothing.**
4. *The victim connects Linear, and `establishAccount`'s `else if (session.accountId)` branch (`lib/account-session.js:161-164`) attaches the victim's Linear identity to the attacker's account.* That requires `session.accountId` = the attacker's account in the victim's browser.
   - For email, the only writer is a successful POST confirm past (a)(b)(b′)(c), which a cross-site request can't reach.
   - The provider entries remain guarded by the session-bound OAuth `state` (`routes/auth.js:87` set, `:136` check, `:301/:320` clear; `consumeOAuthNonce`, `lib/github-install-flow.js:59-61`).
   - For a **signed-in** victim, the N2 guard (b′)/(c′) refuses any sign-in-mode confirm whose email isn't already on the live account. The GET page then shows no button.
   - So step 4 is **closed structurally**, not just made less likely.
5. Follows from step 4, so it's closed too.

**Legitimate cross-browser confirm.** The phone's top-level GET (Lax cookie allowed) mints the nonce into the phone's own session, shows the other-device notice, and its button is a same-origin POST (cookie + nonce + `t`). The laptop stays signed out. If the cookie is lost, the 403 page links back to the non-consuming GET.

#### F7: merge re-auth loop for an email-only account, reachable in S2 as shipped
- **Reproduction.** Harness plus the real `establishAccount` and `respondToAccountConflict`, mirroring the Linear callback's conflict arm at `routes/auth.js:373-391`:
  1. P signs up through the real email door. P has an `accountId`, zero workspaces, and only an email identity.
  2. Account A already owns Linear identity `lin-A`.
  3. P connects Linear (the `/account` "Connect Linear" button → `/auth/linear`) and gets a conflict.
- **Result:**
  - If P's email sign-in was **5 minutes ago**: 409 with a merge offer. Correct.
  - If it was **11 minutes ago** (past `MERGE_CONFIRM_FRESH_AUTH_WINDOW_MS`, `lib/account-session.js:46`): 409 with the re-auth page, whose only button goes to `/auth/linear`. Following it hits the same conflict and the same re-auth page.
  - Meanwhile `GET /auth/email` in P's session returns "You're signed in" with no form (`routes/email-auth.js:175`), and send refuses signed-in sessions (`:192`). P has no way to re-prove itself in-session, so it loops.
  - GitHub (`lib/github-install-flow.js:797`) and Jira (`routes/jira-auth.js:808`) take the same kind of branch.
- **Reachable in S2 without S3.** It's the S2 counterpart of G4/S3-1, but harder: an email-only P has **no provider sign-in** to re-prove with, so S3-1's "re-prove P via its provider sign-in" doesn't apply.
- **User impact:** no security effect. But it hits exactly the flow `/account`'s C6 line recommends: sign in by email on a new device, then reconnect a source the person already signed in with elsewhere (for them that source is on another account until S3). After 10 minutes they're stuck until they log out, sign in by email again, and reconnect within 10 minutes.
- **Why this doesn't block merging S2:** the email door is off everywhere until the operator activation prerequisites are set, so email-only accounts can't exist in production yet.
- **Class:** inside LIN-1892. The email-only account state is this ticket's creation, and so is the need to re-prove P shared with G4. LIN-2500 (pinning each surface's `reauthUrl`) is related but not a duplicate.

issue.title: The first screen: your backlog, the top task, Go, and the prompt underneath
issue.description:
**Child of milestone 3 in the v1 epic. Blocked until the sketches conversation is Done. *(cleared: LIN-2947 is Done, merged as*** `6e8bf424`***.)***

## What this is

The first screen a signed-in, connected person sees. They recognise their own backlog, see which task Harbour would take first and why in a line, and see Go. Under Go, the grounded prompt for that task, free, for the person who would rather do it by hand. The hands-on person and the handover person are both at home on it.

The shape comes from the sketches conversation. This ticket builds it.

## What Done looks like

The milestone's demo runs through this screen: a fresh account, its own backlog, the top task, Go and the prompt, with no help from the operator.

## Read first

`docs/v1.md`, steps 3 and 4 of the golden path. `lib/task-stack.js` for how the top task is chosen today. `lib/render-swipe.js` for the nearest existing surface.

## Update from the LIN-2947 sketches sitting (26 Sep 2026)

**Rescoped: this is now the opened task, not a new first screen.** Home stays the minimalist list and Swipe stays "just the top task". What gets built is what you see when you open a task: **one component shared by home and Swipe** (today they are two builds that have drifted: different names, order and fields, and Swipe ignores `aiRecommendations`/`promptButtons`).

* **Primary action ✦ next step:** the AI-generated, task-tailored prompt (the templates are generic). Its reasoning streams and **stays visible** (today it collapses behind "show reasoning"); a prominent copy; the last generated prompt remembered per task ("generated 2h ago · regenerate"). Target: three clicks from home to a copied prompt (today four).
* **The ladder beside it:** copy the prompt → run this step for me → run the whole task. Rungs not yet enabled are shown as "○ set up ›", never hidden; pressing one says what it needs. (The recording of that press belongs to LIN-2942.)
* **Proxy on by default,** labelled in plain words ("your agent can read & update your tasks · what's this? ›") with an FAQ; not a hidden global localStorage switch.
* **Templates under "other prompts".** Edit promoted to the header. Everything for understanding (brief, recap, runs, comments, images, blockers, chat) as one quiet row of links with counts; **nothing spends AI until asked** (Brief/Recap auto-generate on open today).

Inventory of today's surface (file:line) is in this sitting's record on LIN-2947.

## Research findings (LIN-2944, grounded at LinearViewer `507210ea`)

**Recommended approach.** Build /ONE/ shared opened-task component by **extending** `public/prompt-section.js:189` `PromptSection.init` (already a view-agnostic renderer for picker/reasoning/copy/dispatch), and have BOTH Home and Swipe consume it — retiring Home's parallel inline renderer (`lib/render.js` `renderPromptButtons`/`renderPromptContainer`/recommend/autopilot containers + `public/app.js` `initRecommendations`). Add on top: ✦ next-step primary framing with always-visible reasoning, the copy→run-this-step→run-whole-task ladder, proxy-on-by-default + plain-words FAQ, templates under "other prompts", Edit in the header, the quiet understanding row (brief/recap/runs/comments/images/blockers/chat with counts), and per-task prompt memory. No new page route; no second server representation of prompt data (consume the existing `promptCache` shape in localStorage).

**Witness (end-to-end, fails today).** GitHub-connected person (`seedGitHubWorkspace` + `page.route` on `/api/recommend/*/stream`) as the sign-in/connect case; local connected workspace (`seedLocal(…, { openRouterConnected:true })`, deterministic `shouldMockAi` mock) for the R2-5/no-spend case. Assert: own backlog, real (non-welcome) top task + one-line why, Go, tailored prompt with visible reasoning, copy ≤3 clicks, zero AI POST before an explicit click. All fail at HEAD.

**Boundaries / do-not-take.** R2-5 fix here = the *screen's top task* on opened-task/Swipe/Home only; roadmap/next-run sample filtering stays **LIN-3069** (relation added). Do not take: **LIN-3123** (F8 contrast owner — use `--green-dim`/`--amber-dim` only), **LIN-2942** (ladder press recording), **LIN-3079** (autopilot-proxy token), **LIN-1916**, email sign-in (LIN-1892), Connection model (LIN-2149). Stop Brief/Recap auto-POST (`brief.js:172`/`recap.js:205`) to satisfy "nothing spends AI until asked". Ladder "○ set up ›" uses flag-gates (`dispatch`/`proxy`), not a live runner probe.

**Surface Assessment.** `refactor required: minimal scoped change — consumer: public/prompt-section.js:189 PromptSection.init` (unify two drifted prompt surfaces, not add a second representation). Next action: `plan`.

## Implementation Plan (revised — grounded at LinearViewer `06c754a5`)

**Revised against Plan Review Verdict** `ad5e526c` **(F1–F12).**

### Strategy (unchanged, root contract gap: none identified)

Extend `public/prompt-section.js:189` `PromptSection.init` into the shared opened-task component; Swipe consumes it first (already does, `swipe.js:799`), Home migrates onto it in P1, retiring Home's parallel inline renderer. Rejected alternatives unchanged: a new shared module (duplicates hardened logic — LIN-2987/LIN-3079/LIN-2046 — and violates the "no second representation" constraint); migrating Swipe onto `render.js` (reopens three fixed bug classes, no streaming/state-machine there). Intra-repo renderer drift, not a cross-service contract break.

### Phase 0 — extend `PromptSection.init`; Swipe as in-task consumer. Blocks all other phases.

**Files:** `public/prompt-section.js`, `tests/e2e/opened-task-first-screen.spec.js` (new), `tests/unit/prompt-section-recommend-url.test.js`, `tests/e2e/swipe.spec.js`, Swipe-side cases of `tests/e2e/autopilot-proxy-force.spec.js`.

**Adds:**

* One-line "why" header sourced from `buildWhy()`; ✦ next-step primary framing; reasoning always visible (reverses LIN-70); ladder (copy → run-this-step → run-whole-task) with `○ set up ›` rungs keyed on `featureFlags.dispatch`/`proxy`; "other prompts" grouping; Edit slot; per-task memory extending `promptCache`.
* **F9 flag parity:** `hasAI = !!openRouterSource && aiRecommendations !== false` (today `render-swipe.js:590` ignores `aiRecommendations`); `promptButtons === false` hides templates under "other prompts". Applied at `render-swipe.js:590` and Home's future mount point (P1). AI off by user choice → primary action disabled, "AI suggestions are off · turn on in settings"; AI unconfigured/no BYOK → disabled, "needs OpenRouter"; free-tier exhausted (429) → disabled, quota message (ports `app.js:1889`). Test case per flag state.
* **F5 (moved here from "preserve readSSEStream" in app.js):** `PromptSection.handleStreamingResponse` adopts `window.readSSEStream` (`common.js:613`), replacing its own hand-rolled `getReader`/`TextDecoder` (`prompt-section.js:325-326`) — closes the fifth SSE-reader fork LIN-2969 missed, regains LIN-2980's exception propagation. Keeps rAF-batched rendering and LIN-2987 pinned-bottom sampling exactly as today. Guard: extend `prompt-section-recommend-url.test.js` (or a new unit test) to assert the shared reader is used.
* **F11 persisted prompt-memory shape:** replace the in-memory-only `Map` with a persisted record — same fields as today's cache entry (`{label, name, raw, reasoning}`) minus `html` (re-rendered from `raw` on hydrate), plus `generatedAt`. Keyed by `urlKey` **+** `issueId` (not global). Reads/writes wrapped in try/catch. The proxy-appended block is never persisted — tokens mint fresh per copy (LIN-1140).
* Must preserve: `state.result.proxyForce`-keyed toggle suppression (LIN-3079, Swipe cases of `autopilot-proxy-force.spec.js` \~`:178-246/410`); pinned-bottom-before-mutation sampling (LIN-2987); `URLSearchParams`-built recommend-stream URL for `source` (LIN-2046).

**Tests:** new `opened-task-first-screen.spec.js`, scoped to the Swipe-reachable witness subset (top task+why, Go, tailored prompt+visible reasoning), both GitHub-connected (`seedGitHubWorkspace` + `page.route` stub) and local-connected (`seedLocal(...,{openRouterConnected:true})`) cases. Red-first inside this PR (fails against pre-P0 Swipe UI), green by this phase's commits; also asserts the F4-correct no-request sub-assertion for the Swipe-reachable path. Update `prompt-section-recommend-url.test.js` and `swipe.spec.js` to the new ladder DOM (same truth condition, different selector). **Baseline evidence:** run the full witness skeleton against pre-P0 HEAD (`06c754a5`) and record the failure in the PR description.

### Phase 1 — Home migrates onto the shared component; retire Home's inline renderer. *(depends on P0)*

**Files:** `lib/render.js`, `public/app.js`, `server.js` (`renderDashboardAfterRefresh` — F3's top-task/why computation), `lib/render-swipe.js` (export reuse, no behavior change), `tests/e2e/opened-task-first-screen.spec.js` (Home-path additions), `tests/e2e/dispatch.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/autopilot-proxy-force.spec.js` (Home cases), `tests/e2e/streaming.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/detail-nonactive-binding.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/interactions.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/prompts.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/prompts-page.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/custom-prompts.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/free-tier.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/templates.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/proxy-toggle-copy.spec.js`.

**Removals — F1-bounded, opened-task call sites only:** `render.js:1053` (buttons row), `:1061` (container), `:1073` (recommend container), `:1088` (autopilot container); `app.js` `initRecommendations` + its reasoning-toggle/suggest-btn/prompt-copy/prompt-download handlers for the opened-task DOM only. `renderPromptContainer` **(**`render.js:127`**) and the page-wide** `.prompt-copy`**/**`.prompt-download` **handlers (**`app.js:1058,1103`**) stay** — still used by periodical Mint (`:498`), Mint+Autopilot (`:517`, `proxyForce:true`), and Setup Prompt (`:846`).

**Adds:**

When `why` is `[]`, the component renders no reason line. Empty-backlog state per F12 when only seed content remains.
* Behavior improvement: AI-unconfigured shows the primary action disabled with plain-words "needs OpenRouter" instead of vanishing (today's `renderPromptButtons` drops `.suggest-btn`); same for free-tier-exhausted.

**Tests:** extend `opened-task-first-screen.spec.js` with Home-path versions of every P0 assertion (land on Home → marked top row → same why/Go/prompt/reasoning) plus "copy ≤3 clicks from Home", plus "Home's marked top task equals Swipe's first card for the same seed" (new, F3) — red-first, green after. Retarget with stated truth conditions (F2): `dispatch.spec.js` (dispatch posts the right issue, 9 hits e.g. `:91`), Home cases of `autopilot-proxy-force.spec.js` (`:40,50,129` — Home Autopilot forces proxy), `streaming.spec.js` (a stream renders reasoning, now visible by default, replacing `.reasoning-toggle`), `detail-nonactive-binding.spec.js` (\~`:116`, a Jira-sourced opened task grounds on its own binding), `interactions.spec.js`, `prompts.spec.js`, `prompts-page.spec.js`, `custom-prompts.spec.js`, `free-tier.spec.js`, `templates.spec.js`, `proxy-toggle-copy.spec.js` (same click-gating/free-tier/proxy-copy truth conditions, different markup). ### Phase 2 — stop Brief/Recap AI-spend-on-open. *(depends on P1; may run concurrently with P3)*

**Tests:** `brief-recap-autogenerate.test.js` rewritten to assert the opposite (required behavior-change edit, reversing LIN-998/LIN-1016's auto-populate decision — not a weakened guard). ### Phase 3 — proxy default-on (server-side) + FAQ; R2-5 top-task fix; F8-safe markup. *(depends on P1; may run concurrently with P2)*

**Files (F6-complete):** `public/common.js`, `lib/user-preferences.js`, `lib/feature-defaults.js`, `server.js` (new preference route + login rehydration, mirroring `:3638`/`user-preferences.js:382`), `public/prompt-section.js` (plain-words label + FAQ), `lib/render.js`/`lib/render-swipe.js`/`lib/render-dispatch.js`/`lib/render-flight-companion.js` (`bodyAttrs` lines only — the 4 existing `data-proxy-feature` sites), `routes/workspace.js` (the F12 seed-id helper, additive export only), presentation-layer top-task pick in `render-swipe.js`/`server.js` for R2-5 (not `task-stack.js`), `tests/e2e/proxy-toggle-copy.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/autopilot-proxy-force.spec.js`, `tests/e2e/opened-task-first-screen.spec.js` (its own `test.describe` block).

Mirror the theme/LIN-785 precedent exactly: add `preferences.features.proxyDefault` to `UserPreferencesStore`, written via a read-merge-write route parallel to the theme route (`server.js:3638`), rehydrated into `req.session.proxyDefault` at login alongside `session.theme` (`user-preferences.js:382`). Each of the 4 renderer `bodyAttrs` sites additionally emits `data-proxy-active` from the session value. `isActive()` reads `document.body.dataset.proxyActive` (mirroring `isFeatureEnabled()`, `common.js:1543-1545`) instead of localStorage; `setActive()` becomes a fire-and-forget POST plus an optimistic dataset flip. `session.proxyDefault` **is the single source of truth — no** `localStorage` **key is kept for the default.** Existing `localStorage['proxy-toggle-active']='false'` values are ignored post-migration (dead data, never read by the new `isActive()`).

Retarget both to set the toggle explicitly through the new preference seam (e.g. `/test/set-session`-style `proxyDefault:false`/`true`); force assertions run with the toggle explicitly off.

Demotion applies the helper at the presentation layer only — after `render-swipe.js:563-564` for Swipe's front card, and in Home's top-task pick (P1's F3 wiring). **Tests:** extend/confirm `proxy-toggle-copy.spec.js` for default-on. `tests/e2e/opened-task-first-screen.spec.js` carries separate `test.describe` blocks per phase; whichever of P2/P3 merges second rebases onto the first's spec state (disjoint `describe` blocks in one shared file — no logical conflict). Full landing-path witness, both cases:

**Local-connected (R2-5):** `seedLocal(..., {openRouterConnected:true})`, `shouldMockAi` deterministic mock → same assertions, plus the two F12 seed-set cases above.

Fully green (all assertions, both cases) only at the end of P3 — no red e2e ever lands on `main`, per phase's red-first-in-PR / green-by-merge discipline.

### Cross-cutting interactions / sources of truth

* **Prompt rendering/memory:** single source `PromptSection` + persisted `promptCache` record (F11); Home and Swipe both read/write it identically post-P1.
* **Feature flags:** `hasAI`/`promptButtons` gating centralized in the shared component (F9); `FEATURES.PROXY` default flip (F7) fans out through the 4 `bodyAttrs` sites — Flight Companion, Passage Planner (force-only), Dispatch page are read-only consumers of `common.js`/`ProxyToggle`, unaffected at the interface level.
* **Proxy preference/tokens:** `UserPreferencesStore` becomes the one source of truth for the default (F7); `opts.force`/`proxyForce` (LIN-3079) bypasses it entirely, untouched.

* **Streaming:** `window.readSSEStream` becomes the one reader after P0 (F5) — Home inherits it for free via the shared component in P1.
* **Home/Swipe top-task presentation:** one pipeline (`computeGraphFeatures`→`sortIssuesForSwipe`→`applyBlockingOrder`) computed independently per-surface (existing precedent), same seed-skip helper (F12) applied at both front-card and Home-row presentation points.
* **Shared witness tests:** coordinated via separate `describe` blocks (above).

### History / behavior-preservation (high-churn files)

`prompt-section.js`: pinned-bottom sampling before mutation (LIN-2987); `proxyForce` not `kind` for suppression (LIN-3079); `URLSearchParams` for the recommend-stream URL (LIN-2046); now also adopts `window.readSSEStream` (LIN-2969/LIN-2980, moved here per F5). `render.js`: preserve `source`/`data-source` provenance when retiring only the opened-task containers (LIN-1910/LIN-2045) — `renderPromptContainer` itself is not retired (F1). `app.js`: the page-wide `.prompt-copy`/`.prompt-download` handlers stay live for periodical/Setup-Prompt containers. `render-swipe.js`: preserve `source` stamping in `issueToCard` and the unstarted-with-downstream-reach sort rule (LIN-1872) — this plan only consumes `sortIssuesForSwipe`, never alters ranking, and reuses (never duplicates) `buildWhy`/`computeOffPageBlockers`. `common.js`: proxy default now server-preference-backed (P3) — no bypass reader. `workspace-api.js`: `503 AI_NOT_CONFIGURED` contract (LIN-1016) and per-row-binding resolution for recap/brief/recommend (LIN-1910/LIN-2045) unchanged.

### Session fit

Does not fit one session. Dependency arrows: **P0 → P1 → {P2, P3 (parallel, disjoint** `describe` **blocks in one shared spec file, rebase-on-merge)}**. P0 (large, real engineering lift) → P1 (large, mechanical, wide blast radius, \~10 e2e specs touched) → P2 (small) ∥ P3 (medium). Each phase dispatchable as its own `implementation` session on LIN-2944, in order; P2/P3 genuinely concurrent-safe per the file lists above (F6).

**plan-review due: yes — (a) multiple sessions; (d) credential/token-exposure surface (F7's proxy-default flip, its fan-out, and the token-exposure FAQ text).** (c) does not apply: P2's Brief/Recap auto-spend removal and the dead `autoOpen` branch removal are a deliberate behaviour reversal explicitly mandated by the ticket (reversing LIN-998/LIN-1016's auto-populate decision), not a relaxation of any validation, contract, or guard — the `503 AI_NOT_CONFIGURED` contract and its manual-path error handling stay fully intact. (b) does not apply: no contract gap is being routed around.

**Finding from periodical: Onboarding & Cold-Start Review (LIN-3106), 2026-09-26.** Report: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/901934717dcd3fce66fd0367dc50e66486882a36/docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-09-26.md (merged in `90193471`, PR #1592)

## Research findings — LIN-2944 (research beat complete, grounded at LinearViewer `507210ea`)

**Scope:** code-grounded view of the opened-task surface + what the rescoped component must reuse. Research only — no plan yet. Next action: `plan`.

### Verdict on "existing component to unify vs create"
No shared opened-task component exists. Home (`lib/render.js` `renderDetailsContent` + `public/app.js` `initRecommendations`) and Swipe (`lib/render-swipe.js` + `public/swipe.js` `renderCard` + `public/prompt-section.js` `PromptSection`) are two drifted builds, exactly as the ticket states. issue.title: One agent credential: cover dispatch, proxy and the session-only routes (or proxy versions of them)
issue.description:
*From Lighthouse*, a project run on Harbour by agents, and its first outside user. It filed this feedback on 2026-09-26 after its driver script had to work around Harbour. Filed by the con; the full list is on the parent epic.

There are three auth surfaces today:

* the dispatch token, for consumers;
* the proxy token, for the workspace API;
* the session cookie, for history, next-run, roadmap, north-star writes and feature flags.

An agent needs **one credential that covers all three**, or proxy versions of the session-only routes. It is **priority 2**.

## On the v1 path (26 Sep 2026, John's decision)

LIN-3080 proved locally that a person's own Claude Code session can take dispatched work and run a whole Autopilot task through its subagents with no Simple Dispatcher. The one thing a copied prompt can't carry today is a credential that can **take** work and **post feedback**: only a browser session can mint a dispatch token. That makes this ticket what lets v1's "run this step / run the whole task" rungs be a single copied prompt, so it now blocks LIN-2942.

**The v1 slice is narrower than the Lighthouse ask.** v1 needs take + feedback reachable from a copied prompt. The session-only routes (history, next-run, roadmap, north-star writes, feature flags) are not needed for v1 and can split into a follow-up at planning.

**Two designs to choose between at planning** (LIN-3080's close-out compares them):

* take + feedback on the proxy, so the proxy token a copy already carries is the only credential;
* mint the runner credential at copy time, the way the +proxy block already mints a single-use bootstrap, e.g. a bootstrap that exchanges for a workspace-scoped, expiring take/feedback credential.

**Constraint from LIN-2884.** Taking work means running code on the person's machine. Whichever design lands must not let an ordinary `readWrite` token, or a worker's exchanged token, take work. Plan it with LIN-2884's dispatch scope in view, not against it.

**Done also includes** the [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) witness deferred here from LIN-3080: re-run its two runs (one step, one tiny Autopilot) against the hosted instance, using a copied prompt as the only credential.

## Research findings (2026-09-27)

Grounded at repo HEAD `06c754a51d6ddce32e31223af3257c9fa55f32af`. Research only; no design chosen. Next action: `design`.

**Credential inventory (today):** dispatch/consumer token (`lib/dispatch-tokens.js`), proxy token (`lib/proxy-tokens.js`, scopes `read`/`readWrite` only, kind `standard`/`bootstrap`), session cookie `connect.sid` (`server.js:827`), single-use bootstrap (48h, exchanged at `POST /api/proxy/token`), worker exchanged token (inherits scope+owner from bootstrap), Harbour OS single-use feedback token (`lib/harbour-feedback-tokens.js`). No `dispatch` scope exists today (LIN-2884).

**Auth surfaces:** enqueue = proxy (`POST /api/proxy/dispatch`, `/recommend-and-dispatch`, `/autopilot/kickoff`) + session (`/api/dispatch`, collective, flight-companion approve, feedback-triage) + internal wake. Take = dispatch-token bearer (`/api/dispatch/take/:id`) plus a Harbour OS `local`-target server-side self-take (`routes/dispatch.js:667`). Feedback = dispatch token + Harbour OS single-use token (ownership `takenByTokenLabel`, `lib/dispatch-store.js:2045`). No proxy take/feedback path exists.

**Two candidate shapes** (from LIN-3080's close-out, no third path): **(A)** take+feedback onto the proxy (proxy token becomes the only credential) — must ship with a take-authority scope or every `readWrite`/exchanged token takes; **(B)** copy-time bootstrap → workspace-scoped, expiring take/feedback runner credential — confines take authority to the copy path. Both meet the "one credential" criterion once the token model allows **one bearer carrying more than one authority** (multi-scope or composite scope); the real difference is where the bearer lives, not how many credentials exist.

**LIN-2884 seam:** `dispatch` = enqueue ("run code on my machine" = start a session); take = consumer side (run the item on your own machine). Distinct authorities. Tension to resolve: a copied prompt carries a bootstrap, but LIN-2884 says `dispatch` is "never by exchange from a bootstrap token" — reading (a) "exchange copies, never upgrades" vs reading (b) "no take/dispatch scope ever rides a bootstrap".

**Class bounds:** enqueue = 13 `createDispatchItem(` hits = 1 definition + 2 comments + 10 call sites, plus 2 internal `addItem` wake sites; mint = 7 `createToken(` sites; exchange = 1 route caller; auth gates = `authenticateProxyToken`, `requireWriteScope`, `authenticateDispatchToken`, `authenticateFeedbackToken`, `workspaceFromUrl`.

**Decisive prior safeguard (LIN-1576 → LIN-1582):** scope/ownerless restrictions must be **structural in the store + exchange**, never per-route (the "choke point" assumption failed — three sites escaped). Applies to any third scope.

**Inputs for the design decision:** (1) one-bearer-multi-scope vs composite scope; (2) whether take and enqueue share revocation/granularity; (3) risk trade (A widens paste blast radius, B adds a store surface but smaller blast radius + fine revocation); (4) LIN-2394 `expiresAt` misreport is inherited by either scoped token unless fixed; (5) the [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) witness needs an isolated workspace Simple Dispatcher does not poll.

**Security-boundary questions (for John, unresolved):** (i) may a copy-time bootstrap carry take authority; (ii) shared vs separate take/enqueue grant; (iii) TTL/revocation of the take-capable credential; (iv) can a non-owner member ever hold it.

## Shared credential + scope design (LIN-3059 + LIN-2884)

*Design written 2026-09-27 (design session* `9a7b0b86`*). Grounded at LinearViewer* `06c754a51d6ddce32e31223af3257c9fa55f32af` *(= origin/main at design time). This section is shared: LIN-2884 adopts it verbatim and adds only what "LIN-2884 adds" below says. Nothing here is built yet. The security-boundary choices J1–J4 are **ruled** (2026-09-28, John, accepted; comment* `643adf08`*); J5 is LIN-2884's.*

*Updated at planning 2026-09-28: J1–J4 ruled; the owner check keys on* `workspaceId` *(reusing #1601's* `getWorkspaceOwnerAccountId`*);* `dispatch` *is in* `GRANTS` *and stamped on the runner mint by LIN-3059 (recorded, not enforced until LIN-2884); ownership transfer → LIN-1892 follow-on; backfill → LIN-1892 decision 2; slicing refined to S1 / S2a / S2b (see* `## Implementation Plan (2026-09-28)` *below, which governs where it differs).*

*Revised after plan-review 2026-09-28 (F1–F3, comment* `c6f6cbec`*):* `requireGrant`*,* `req.proxyTokenGrants` *and the runner criterion test move into S1; LIN-2884 builds after S1 but must merge its enforcement after S2b + #1601; the runner mount shape and the feedback-ownership filter are corrected in the plan.*

### 1. Chosen shape: B's issuance on A's plumbing

**Take authority exists only on a bearer that the workspace owner's signed-in session mints at copy time.** That bearer is a single-use bootstrap, exchanged once for an expiring working token. Both are ordinary `ProxyTokenStore` documents; there is no new token store. Take, poll and feedback are served as proxy routes, gated once at their sub-router mount.

Rationale: (B) confines "run code on my machine" to one owner-minted, short-lived, single-use path. That gives it the smallest mis-paste blast radius and per-runner revocation. Building it on the proxy token model (A's plumbing) avoids a parallel token representation, keeps one base URL and one auth middleware for the runner, and lets the LIN-1582 structural guarantees live in the one store that already carries them.

| Constraint | (A) take+feedback on the proxy token, with a take scope | (B) copy-time owner bootstrap → expiring runner credential (**chosen**, on A's plumbing) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Enqueue vs take kept distinct (LIN-2884) | Only if take is its own authority; it could still attach to 90-day Settings tokens | Take exists only on runner bearers |
| Exchange never upgrades | Holds | Holds; needs J1 reading (a) |
| Structural enforcement (LIN-1582) | Harder: 7 `createToken` sites and the Settings mint could request take | One store method mints grants; `createToken` refuses them |
| Feedback ownership (F1) | Label ownership breaks; needs a token id | Same fix; the runner bearer id is the owner key |
| Expiry | Inherits 90d (Settings) or 48h (working) | Short bootstrap and bounded working TTL by construction |
| Revocation | Coarse: revoking also kills tracker access | Per runner bearer; tracker tokens untouched |
| Mis-paste blast radius | Widest: a leaked token runs code for its whole TTL | Spent after the first exchange; the owner's own exchange then fails loudly |
| LIN-2394 `expiresAt` skew | Inherited | Inherited; checked by the witness (§7) |
| Size | Smaller | Somewhat larger (one mint path, one grant-aware exchange) |

### 2. Authority model

* `scope` **+** `grants[]` **(multi-scope, not a composite scope).** `scope` stays `read` | `readWrite`, unchanged, as the base tier for tracker access. A new `grants: string[]` field holds privileged authorities, each independent:
  * `take`: poll, take and post consumer feedback on dispatch items (LIN-3059).
  * `dispatch`: enqueue, including abort and follow-up (LIN-2884, added later).

  A composite scope was rejected because every combination would need a name (`readWrite+dispatch`, `runner`, `runner+dispatch`, …), and LIN-2884 would have to reshape LIN-3059's value.
* **One source of truth:** `lib/proxy-scopes.js` exports `SCOPES`, `GRANTS` and `hasScope` / `hasGrant`. It replaces today's 10 `'readWrite'` literals across 6 files (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:129`, `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js:62`, `routes/proxy.js:589`, `lib/proxy-preamble.js`, `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `routes/dispatch.js`). This is the research Surface Assessment.
* **Structural refusal in the store (the LIN-1582 lesson):**
  * `ProxyTokenStore.createToken` **throws** on any non-empty `grants`. Every existing mint site (7) and any future one is therefore unable to mint a grant, and the worker bootstraps from `provisionBootstrapToken` and `broker-token` can never carry one.
  * A grant on a document with `createdBy: null` is treated as absent at validate time.
  * `DISPATCH_OWNERLESS_BROKER_COMPAT` does **not** apply to grants.
* **Owner-only mint:** `ProxyTokenStore.mintGrantBootstrap({ urlKey, workspaceId, ownerAccountId, grants })` is the only way to create a grant. It mints `kind: 'bootstrap'` (single-use) and refuses unless the injected owner check, `checkWorkspaceOwner({ workspaceId, accountId })`, reports `owner` (it reuses #1601's `getWorkspaceOwnerAccountId`, compared canonically; J4 ruled). `workspaceId` is stamped on the bootstrap so the exchange-time re-check needs no `urlKey` lookup. It also refuses with no owner. *(Updated at planning 2026-09-28: keyed on* `workspaceId`*, not* `urlKey`*.)*
* **Exchange copies grants and never adds them.** `exchangeBootstrapToken` copies `grants` verbatim, as it already copies `scope` (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:274`). For a grant-bearing bootstrap it re-checks the owner at exchange time and applies the runner working TTL. A test pins "exchange never adds a grant".
* **Mount-level gate:** `requireGrant(name)` (a pure middleware factory in `lib/require-grant.js`, importable by any sub-router) gates a path-scoped `router.use('/api/proxy/runner', proxyLimiter, authenticateProxyToken, requireGrant('take'))` that is the first statement of the runner factory, so it is applied at the runner **mount** and never inside long handlers (per the LIN-3103 finding on LIN-2884). The factory itself is mounted path-less as `router.use(createProxyRunnerRoutes({...}))` so the proxy DI witness accepts it. *(Revised at plan-review 2026-09-28.)*
* **Ownership by token id (F1).** Today take stamps `takenByTokenLabel` and feedback matches on it (`lib/dispatch-store.js:815`, `:2045`). Labels are not unique: every copied `+proxy` bootstrap is `prompt-proxy` (`public/common.js:1586`), every dispatched worker is `dispatch-bootstrap`, and dispatch tokens default to `default`.
  * Runner take stamps `takenByTokenId`, keeping the label for display, and runner feedback matches the token id.
  * The legacy dispatch-token path keeps label matching for legacy-taken items, unchanged, but its filter also requires `takenByTokenId: null`, so a dispatch token that carries the runner's label cannot post onto a runner-taken item; both branches are one atomic update. *(Revised at plan-review 2026-09-28.)*
* **The server resolves grants, never the client (F4).** The session mint `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/proxy/tokens` today takes `scope` from the request body. The runner copy sends `runner: true`; the server decides the grant list (J2) and checks ownership (J4). Clients can never name a grant.
* **Bootstrap delivery.** The copied runner prompt uses the prose lane: the single-use bootstrap sits in the prompt text, as the `+proxy` prose block does today. The MCP lane exists only for sessions Simple Dispatcher launches. Items the runner takes still carry their own `readWrite`, grant-less `bootstrapToken` for subagents, as in the LIN-3080 pattern. Grants are never inherited by a worker's children.

### 3. Refusal codes

| Case | Result | Enforced |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `read` / `readWrite` / worker-exchanged token on a runner route | 403 `TAKE_GRANT_REQUIRED` | Mount gate. Structurally, no ordinary mint can hold `take`. |
| Runner mint from a non-owner session | 403 `GRANT_OWNER_ONLY` | `mintGrantBootstrap` (store), re-checked at exchange |
| Runner mint from a session with no `accountId` | 503 `GRANT_OWNERLESS` | Store, with no compat lane |
| Grant present on a `createdBy: null` document | Grant ignored, so 403 `TAKE_GRANT_REQUIRED` | `validateToken` |
| `createToken` called with grants | Throws (internal; test-pinned) | Store |
| Expired or revoked runner bearer | 401 `PROXY_TOKEN_INVALID` plus `proxyTokenExpiredAt` (existing shape) | `authenticateProxyToken` |
| Second exchange of the same runner bootstrap (mis-paste signal) | 401 (existing "already-exchanged" text) | Exchange |
| Take of another workspace's item, or one already taken | 404 | `takeItem` (urlKey plus atomic `findOneAndDelete`) |
| Feedback from a bearer that did not take the item, including a dispatch token carrying the runner's label | 404 (same collapse as today) | `addFeedback` filter: `takenByTokenId` (runner) or label + `takenByTokenId: null` (legacy), one atomic update |
| Runner mint, workspace has no owner edge | 409 `WORKSPACE_OWNER_UNSET` | `mintGrantBootstrap` |
| Owner check unwired, erroring or corrupt merge chain | 503 `OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` (retryable) | Store, fail closed |
| Client sends `grants` in the mint body | 400 `GRANTS_NOT_CLIENT_SETTABLE` | Mint route |

*Updated at plan-review 2026-09-28: the plan's refusal table (*`## Implementation Plan (2026-09-28)`*, P5) is the complete list and governs.*

### 4. What LIN-3059 builds vs what LIN-2884 adds

* **LIN-3059 builds:**
  * the vocabulary module, with both `take` and `dispatch` in `GRANTS` and both stamped on the runner mint (J2; `dispatch` is recorded but not enforced until LIN-2884; updated at planning 2026-09-28);
  * the `grants` field and the store refusal;
  * `mintGrantBootstrap`;
  * the grant-copying exchange;
  * `requireGrant` and `req.proxyTokenGrants` (S1, behaviour-neutral until mounted; revised at plan-review 2026-09-28);
  * the `take` grant and the runner routes;
  * `takenByTokenId`;
  * the owner-checked runner copy mint;
  * the docs.
* **LIN-2884 adds, with no reshaping** *(updated at planning 2026-09-28:* `dispatch` *in* `GRANTS` *and on the runner mint moved to LIN-3059)*:
  * `requireGrant('dispatch')` on the enqueue mounts (`routes/proxy-dispatch.js`: `POST /api/proxy/dispatch`, which also carries abort and follow-up and so reaches `expandCascadeAborts`, and `/recommend-and-dispatch`; `routes/proxy-kickoff.js`), so `read`/`readWrite` stop passing them; the criterion test "runner working token → `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` 201" is created in LIN-3059's S1 and must stay green once gated. **Merge order: LIN-2884's enforcement must merge after S2b + #1601 are deployed AND LIN-1892's owner backfill (Open decision 2) has been applied in production** (declared worker mints need the S2b owner wiring and an owner edge: earlier, ordinary `readWrite` enqueues would 403 while worker mints return 503 `OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, and then 409 `WORKSPACE_OWNER_UNSET` on every workspace bound before #1601, breaking autopilot; or LIN-2884 ships a stated fallback for owner-less workspaces); LIN-2884 can build after S1. LIN-3059's own S1, S2a and S2b do not depend on the backfill. *(Revised at plan-review 2026-09-28, N1.)* After LIN-2884 the legacy member-mintable dispatch token can still take work until J5 is ruled;
  * declared worker mints ("gets the scope explicitly on its own mint, recorded as such") via `mintGrantBootstrap`;
  * carrying J5.
* **Why no reshaping:** `grants` is an open set of independent authorities. LIN-2884 gates different mounts (the `dispatch` member already exists, stamped by LIN-3059). The document shape, the exchange, the ownership and LIN-3059's refusals are untouched. LIN-2884's "a test pins that bootstrap exchange never yields `dispatch`" is the general "exchange never adds a grant" pin, with `dispatch` added (J1 reading (a)).

### 5. Simple Dispatcher coexistence

* **v1 is isolation.** A runner serves a workspace Simple Dispatcher does not poll; outside users have no Simple Dispatcher.
* `pollAvailable` does not filter by target, but take is atomic, so a race is safe though unattributable.
* The runner poll response adds `otherConsumerLastSeenAt` (the latest dispatch-token `lastUsedAt`) so a runner can warn and stop.
* LIN-2885's `consumerLastSeenAt` also counts take-granted bearers, so a runner-only workspace doesn't read "never polled".
* Claim or target markers are deferred: they would need a Simple Dispatcher change.
* The witness precondition is an isolated workspace.

### 6. Implementation outline (design-level)

Existing model extended: `ProxyTokenStore` documents and `dispatchQueueStore`.

 1. `lib/proxy-scopes.js`; replace the 10 literals. Pure refactor.
 2. Store: `grants: []`; `createToken` throws on grants; `validateToken` returns grants and ignores grants on ownerless documents.
 3. `mintGrantBootstrap` with the injected owner check keyed on `workspaceId` (J4 ruled; #1601's owner edge) and no ownerless lane. *(Updated at planning 2026-09-28.)*
 4. Exchange: copies grants and never adds any; re-checks the owner; applies `RUNNER_WORKING_TTL_SECONDS` (86400).
 5. `requireGrant(name)` (`lib/require-grant.js`) and `req.proxyTokenGrants` in `authenticateProxyToken` (S1; inert until mounted). *(Revised at plan-review 2026-09-28.)*
 6. `createProxyRunnerRoutes`, mounted path-less (`router.use(createProxyRunnerRoutes({...}))`) with a path-scoped `take` gate as the factory's first statement:
    * `GET /api/proxy/runner/poll` returns items including their `bootstrapToken`, plus `halt` and `otherConsumerLastSeenAt`. It is take-gated because it hands out item bootstraps.
    * `POST /api/proxy/runner/take/:id`
    * `POST /api/proxy/runner/feedback/:id`

    All three reuse `pollAvailable` / `takeItem` / `addFeedback`.
 7. `takenByTokenId` on take and matched on feedback, legacy label path unchanged. Wake provisioning uses `createdBy = proxyCreatedBy`. Poll-recency counts runner bearers.
 8. Copy-time mint: `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js` accepts `runner: true`, and the server resolves grants (J2) and owner (J4). `public/common.js` gains a runner copy block. `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TTL_SECONDS` (3600) / `RUNNER_WORKING_TTL_SECONDS` (86400) are named constants (J3).
 9. Runner prompt delivery on the prose lane (the prompt body itself is LIN-3098).
10. `GET /api/proxy/instructions` and `docs/proxy-integration.md`: a scopes-vs-grants table, the runner routes, the refusal codes, and a forward pointer to Bootstrap Tokens.

**Slicing:**

* **S1** = seams 1–4 plus `requireGrant`/`req.proxyTokenGrants` and the runner criterion test, with unit pins. Behaviour is unchanged apart from the new mint method; it is what LIN-2884 builds on, but LIN-2884's enforcement merges only after S2b, #1601 merged and deployed, and LIN-1892's owner backfill (Open decision 2) applied in production (or LIN-2884 ships a stated fallback for owner-less workspaces). *(Revised at plan-review 2026-09-28.)*
* **S2** = seams 6–10 plus the e2e test, split at plan into S2a (runner routes) and S2b (owner-checked copy mint, Settings, docs; waits on #1601).
* **Cut after S1.** Then deploy, then the witness.

### 7. Acceptance witness

* **Unit pins:**
  * `readWrite` → 403 and worker-exchanged → 403 on the runner routes;
  * ownerless mint refused; non-owner mint → 403;
  * `createToken` throws on grants;
  * exchange never adds a grant;
  * feedback from another bearer → 404;
  * a runner and a dispatch token racing for one item → exactly one wins.
* **E2e (local harness):** owner copy → exchange → poll → take → feedback → terminal, plus a wake.
* **LIN-2394 check:** the exchange response's `expiresAt` minus its `Date` header ≈ the TTL, and a clock-injected local expiry gives 401 with `proxyTokenExpiredAt` == `expiresAt`.
* **[harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) (after deploy):** re-run LIN-3080's two witnesses, one step and one tiny Autopilot (harness `claude-code`), with a copied prompt as the only credential. Record the dispatch ids and include hosted refusal probes.
* **Needs John:** an isolated [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) workspace Simple Dispatcher does not poll, an owner browser sign-in to copy from, (the J1–J4 rulings are recorded, comment `643adf08`).

### 8. Owner grounding (F2): membership exists, ownership does not

* `AccountWorkspaceStore` (`lib/account-workspace-store.js`) holds many-to-many `{accountId, workspaceId, createdAt}` edges with **no role**. They are written at every sign-in (`lib/account-session.js:219`) and on merges.
* A Linear workspace's `workspaceId` is the Linear `org.id` (`routes/auth.js:198`), so every account connected to that org is a member. A local workspace is random per create, so it has exactly one member.
* `WorkspaceStore` has no owner field and is still unwired (LIN-1330).
* Token "owner" everywhere means `createdBy`, i.e. whichever member minted.
* **Options:**
  * **O1** any member: no cost, but "owner-only" is vacuous on shared orgs.
  * **O2** earliest membership edge: no schema change, but unstable under merges and first-to-connect.
  * **O3** explicit owner role on the edge, backfilled from O2 and transferable: one field, a backfill and a Settings line.
  * **O4** operator allow-list: a stopgap only.

*Updated at planning 2026-09-28: O3 is ruled (J4(c)) and delivered by LIN-1892 S1 / PR #1601 (a* `role: 'owner'` *edge on a workspace's first binding; reused, no parallel field). The backfill for workspaces bound earlier is LIN-1892 Open decision 2 (J4(c)'s "earliest edge" names the rule it needs); ownership transfer is a LIN-1892 follow-on; delegation is LIN-3085.*

### 9. Security-boundary decisions: J1–J4 ruled 2026-09-28; J5 is LIN-2884's

* **(d) Four distinct mint outcomes** (P5). An owner-less **workspace** (every workspace bound before #1601 until LIN-1892 decision 2, plus any crash-gap) is `409 WORKSPACE_OWNER_UNSET`, distinct from `403 GRANT_OWNER_ONLY`, `503 GRANT_OWNERLESS` (session has no account) and `503 OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` (seam unwired/erroring; fail closed, retryable). **Exchange (A5):** a transient owner-check failure at exchange happens after the atomic consume, so the bootstrap is spent and the response is the generic 401; the person must copy again (deliberate: never leave a live bootstrap whose owner check could not be evaluated). Client copy (the helper returns `{ error: { code, message } }`, never swallowed to null like `getOrCreateToken`): OWNER_ONLY "Only this workspace's owner can copy a runner prompt. Workspaces made before ownership tracking need an operator to assign an owner; a workspace created now gets its owner automatically."; OWNERLESS "This session isn't linked to an account. ### P5. Refusal codes

| Case | Result | Enforced at |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `read`/`readWrite`/worker-exchanged token, or a grant on a `createdBy: null` document, on a runner route | 403 `TAKE_GRANT_REQUIRED` | path-scoped gate at the runner mount; structurally no ordinary mint can hold `take` |
| runner mint, session has no `accountId` | 503 `GRANT_OWNERLESS` | mint route + store (no compat lane) |
| runner mint, workspace has no owner edge | 409 `WORKSPACE_OWNER_UNSET` (`retryable: false`) | `mintGrantBootstrap` |
| runner mint, another account owns it | 403 `GRANT_OWNER_ONLY` (never names the owner) | `mintGrantBootstrap`; re-checked at exchange |
| owner seam unwired, erroring, or corrupt merge chain | 503 `OWNER_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` (`retryable: true`) | store, fail closed |
| client sends `grants` | 400 `GRANTS_NOT_CLIENT_SETTABLE` | mint route |
| `createToken` called with grants | throws | store |
| second exchange, or owner changed / owner check failed at exchange (bootstrap already spent; copy again) | 401 `PROXY_TOKEN_INVALID` | exchange (check runs after the atomic consume) |
| expired runner token | 401 + `proxyTokenExpiredAt` | `authenticateProxyToken` |
| revoked runner token (documents deleted) | 401 (no state) | `authenticateProxyToken` |
| take of another workspace's item, or already taken | 404 | `takeItem` (`urlKey` + atomic `findOneAndDelete`) |
| feedback by a bearer that did not take the item, **including a dispatch token carrying the runner's label** | 404 | `addFeedback`: runner branch `takenByTokenId`; legacy branch label + `takenByTokenId: null`; one atomic update. Legacy-taken items behave as today |
| dispatch-token bearer on a runner route | 401 | different store |

Known consequence: ownership is per token id, so an item taken by an expired or replaced runner credential gets 404 from its successor; an in-flight task must finish within one credential lifetime (24h), and LIN-3098's prompt should re-copy only between tasks.

* **Feedback ownership:** id-bound runner branch, label + `takenByTokenId: null` legacy branch, one atomic update. **Revocation lineage:** `parentTokenId`, structural in `revokeToken`, rows keyed on `parentTokenId || tokenId`.

* **North-star writes:** LIN-3066. **Feature flags:** LIN-3064. **Roadmap write verb:** LIN-3067 (the read is LIN-1810, Done).
* **Dispatch history + next-run proxy versions:** **LIN-3128** (filed under LIN-3057, related to LIN-3059). `GET /api/proxy/dispatch` already lists queue + recent history (capped at 100); the gap is offset paging and the next-run suggest verb.
* **LIN-2884:** `requireGrant('dispatch')` on `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` (also carries abort/follow-up and so `expandCascadeAborts`), `/recommend-and-dispatch`, `/autopilot/kickoff`; declared worker mints via `mintGrantBootstrap`; **J5** (the legacy member-mintable dispatch token, `routes/dispatch.js:1165`, which can still take work until J5 is ruled); **enforcement merges after S2b + #1601 deployed + the LIN-1892 owner backfill applied** (or a stated fallback for owner-less workspaces). After LIN-2884, a non-owner member's dispatched workers on a shared org would get `GRANT_OWNER_ONLY` from declared worker mints: LIN-2884's to design with J5 and LIN-3085.
* **LIN-1892:** the backfill (Open decision 2; J4(c)'s "earliest edge" names the rule it needs; it is also a prerequisite of LIN-2884's enforcement merge, not of any LIN-3059 slice); an ownership-transfer slice (must revoke the former owner's grant-bearing tokens); #1601's merge gate.
* **LIN-3098:** the prompt body (P7). **LIN-2394:** the expiry defect (checked, not fixed). **LIN-3116:** doc file pointers. **LIN-2246:** `workspace-api.js` decomposition. **LIN-3085:** non-owner delegation. **LIN-2883:** machine tokens replace the legacy dispatch token.

### P11. Scope assessment and session fit

* S1, S2a and S2b are each one focused implementation session; the witness W is parent-level and needs John. The slices are independently landable (S1 changes no behaviour and unblocks LIN-2884's build; S2a lands with no mint path, so nothing can take yet; S2b turns the feature on), so this is a **breakdown signal: decompose**, not "implement S1 and stop".
* **Recommendation: three sub-tickets under LIN-3059 — S1, S2a, S2b — created after plan-review passes** (their shape may change at review). Relations: S1 blocks S2a; S2a blocks S2b; #1601 / LIN-1892 blocks S2b; **S1 blocks LIN-2884** (build), with the explicit note "LIN-2884's enforcement merges after S2b, #1601 deployed and the LIN-1892 backfill (Open decision 2) applied" on LIN-2884 and on S2b, and a recommended relation **LIN-1892 (backfill) blocks LIN-2884's enforcement** created at breakdown (a note for the coordinator; this plan posts nothing on LIN-1892); S2b blocks LIN-3098. LIN-3059 keeps W, the doc closure and Done, and stays open until all three land. Why sub-tickets rather than sequential dispatches: the dependency edges are slice-specific (LIN-2884 needs S1 to build and S2b to merge; LIN-3098 needs S2b) and Linear relations can only express that between separate issues. Fallback if child tickets are refused (as on LIN-1892): the same slices as sequential implementation dispatches on LIN-3059, ticket **not** Done after S1.
* **Next dispatchable step after review:** S1, which can start immediately (independent of #1601). S2a follows S1's merge. S2b waits on S2a and on #1601 merged and deployed (`PENDING-EXTERNAL`).
* **Landing rules:** every slice lands through a PR with `ci-success` green, via review and close-out.

**Deferred here from LIN-3080 (John's ruling, 26 Sep; wording clarified at LIN-3080's close-out).** The harbour.cat end-to-end witness for "a person's own Claude Code session as their runner" now belongs to this ticket. It moves once a copied prompt can carry a take-capable credential.

LIN-3080 proved the flow on a local Harbour (comment `7f06d6ad` there): a driver session took items, ran each through its own subagents, and relayed Autopilot wakes back to the same orchestrator subagent. The one thing a copied prompt can't carry today is the consumer (dispatch) token, because only a browser session can mint one.

**Two distinct designs can carry the credential; this ticket is where they are chosen** (both are named in this ticket's description; LIN-3080's final note compares them and does not pick one here):

- **(b) take + feedback on the proxy** — the proxy token a copy already carries becomes the only credential. A small server change, but it must ship with LIN-2884's dispatch scope, or any ordinary `readWrite` proxy token (and a worker's exchanged token) could take work.
- **(c) mint the runner credential at copy time** — a single-use bootstrap that exchanges for a workspace-scoped, expiring take/feedback credential, the way the `+proxy` block already mints one. Smaller mis-paste blast radius and cheaper, finer-grained revocation.

The "copy-time" wording on this deferral refers to **(c)** and must not be read as already choosing it over (b).

When this lands, re-run LIN-3080's two witnesses (one step, one tiny Autopilot) against harbour.cat.
Also relevant: claude-code item prompts assume Simple Dispatcher's credential broker (`$HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE`), so a person-run driver has to supply its own.

A single agent credential means touching both surfaces. The report cross-links LIN-1249 (decompose `server.js`) and LIN-2246 (decompose `workspace-api.js`) as the owners of those shapes.

**Finding from periodical: Recent Headwinds Review (LIN-3104), 2026-09-26.** Report: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/eb228315255f734867ac6dd4d8b95e83dc00bc4f/docs/reviews/recent-headwinds-review-2026-09-26.md (merged in `eb228315`, PR #1590)

- **The family is large.** A title scan finds 47 credential, token or identity tickets at LIN ≥ 2384: 25 Backlog, 14 Done, 6 Todo, 2 Canceled.
