## Research findings — LIN-3059 credential-and-scope (research beat 4/4, grounded at `06c754a`)

This comment is the consolidated research record for LIN-3059 (authority research stops short of choosing a design; next action is `design`). Grounded against repo HEAD `06c754a51d6ddce32e31223af3257c9fa55f32af`. No code changed.

### Credential inventory (file:line @ 06c754a)
| # | Credential | Store | Mint | TTL | Revoke | Workspace scope | Authorizes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Dispatch/consumer token | `DispatchTokenStore` `lib/dispatch-tokens.js:30` | session-only `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch/tokens` `routes/dispatch.js:1165` | never | `:169`/`routes/dispatch.js:1210` | urlKey | poll `:1427`, take `:1547`, feedback `:1581`, broker-token `:1491` |
| 2 | Proxy token | `ProxyTokenStore` `lib/proxy-tokens.js:60` | session `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js:44`; dispatch preamble `lib/proxy-preamble.js:306`; broker-token `:1523` | 90d default / 48h working | `:469` | urlKey + owner `selectOwnerWorkspaceToken` `lib/workspace-token-resolver.js:113` | read routes; readWrite → writes + dispatch enqueue |
| 3 | Session cookie `connect.sid` | `MongoSessionStore` `server.js:827` | sign-in/`/workspace/new` | 30d `server.js:194` | logout | `accountId`+`workspaces[]` | session-only routes + token admin |
| 4 | Single-use bootstrap | `ProxyTokenStore` kind `bootstrap` | preamble `:306` / broker-token `:1491` / session mint | 48h | single-use consume | urlKey+owner | only `POST /api/proxy/token` |
| 5 | Worker exchanged token | `exchangeBootstrapToken` `lib/proxy-tokens.js:223` | exchange of (4) | 48h | as (2) | owner inherited; null-owner fails closed | readWrite (enqueue, not take) |
| 6 | Harbour OS feedback token | `HarbourFeedbackTokenStore` `lib/harbour-feedback-tokens.js:26` | Harbour OS `local` target | 1h single-use item-bound | `validateAndConsume:83` | itemId+urlKey | one feedback on one item |
| 7 | Local broker | Simple Dispatcher side (not in this repo) | `$HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE` `lib/proxy-preamble.js:156/226` | — | — | — | credential-injecting broker; `X-Harbour-Intent: write` |

Proxy scopes today are only `read`/`readWrite` (validation `lib/proxy-tokens.js:129`); there is no `dispatch` scope — that is LIN-2884's proposal.

### Create / take / feedback auth matrix
- **enqueue** (proxy, readWrite): `POST /api/proxy/dispatch` `routes/proxy-dispatch.js:218`; `POST /api/proxy/recommend-and-dispatch` `:660`; `POST /api/proxy/autopilot/kickoff` `routes/proxy-kickoff.js:124`.
- **enqueue** (session): `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch` `routes/dispatch.js:273`; `collective/start` `collective.js:148`; `flight-companion/approve-follow-up` `flight-companion.js:883`; feedback-triage `workspace-api.js:3588`; feedback-autopilot `workspace-api.js:3671`; `send_follow_up` tool `lib/chat-tools.js:2076` (propose-only by default).
- **enqueue** (internal): wake via `dispatchQueueStore.addItem` `lib/dispatch-store.js:1957`/`:2253`, triggered by `addFeedback`.
- **take**: (a) dispatch-token bearer `POST /api/dispatch/take/:itemId` `routes/dispatch.js:1547`; (b) **Harbour OS `local` target self-take** — session dispatch with `target:'local'` calls `takeItem(item._id, urlKey, 'harbour')` `routes/dispatch.js:667` after `spawnClaudeSession` (`lib/harbour-spawn.js`). No proxy take path exists.
- **feedback**: `POST /api/dispatch/feedback/:itemId` `routes/dispatch.js:1581` accepts dispatch token OR Harbour OS single-use token (`authenticateFeedbackToken:237`); ownership = `status:'taken' && takenByTokenLabel` `lib/dispatch-store.js:2045`. Separate session-auth `dispatchQueueStore.markDecisionAnswered` (`routes/workspace-api.js:265`, `routes/dashboard.js:1640`) writes `decision-answer` kind only.

### Class bounds (queries @ 06c754a)
- `grep -rn "createDispatchItem(" routes lib | grep -v test` = 13 = 1 definition (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:174`) + 2 comments (`lib/chat-tools.js:52/2026`) + 10 call sites (9 unconditional, 1 conditional `send_follow_up`). The internal wake enqueue bypasses the factory via `addItem`.
- Mint sites: `grep -rn ".createToken(" routes/ lib/` = 7 (dispatch token, broker bootstrap, session proxy-admin, exchange-internal, `provisionBootstrapToken` choke point + 2 test-only).
- Exchange: single route caller `routes/proxy-token-exchange.js:48` (scope-preserving, never upgrading).
- Auth gates: `authenticateProxyToken` (`routes/proxy.js:514`), `requireWriteScope` (`:588`), `authenticateDispatchToken` (`routes/dispatch.js:193`), `authenticateFeedbackToken` (`:237`), `workspaceFromUrl` (`server.js:1975`).

### Feasibility: A vs B
- **(A) take+feedback on the proxy**: reuses the existing proxy token; requires a take-authority scope otherwise every `readWrite` (and worker-exchanged) token takes. Entangles take with the proxy token's enqueue surface.
- **(B) copy-time bootstrap → workspace-scoped expiring runner credential**: new copy-time mint (owner session) + a distinct take/feedback credential. Confines take authority to the copy path; LIN-2884 `dispatch` (enqueue) stays orthogonal. Must extend `ProxyTokenStore` (new scope/kind), not mint a third parallel token store (a parallel store would be a second representation of the already-modelled proxy token).
- **One-credential criterion**: both designs satisfy "one credential" once the token model permits **one bearer carrying more than one authority** (a scope set / composite scope). My mid-research "two bearers, one prompt" for (B) was a framing artifact, not a property of the design. The real difference between A and B is *where the bearer lives* (proxy-token surface vs a copy-time runner credential), not how many credentials exist. Design input: if take and enqueue must remain separately revocable/granular, the token model needs multi-scope (or two scopes minted onto one token); if they may share revocation, a single composite scope may suffice.

### LIN-2884 seam
- LIN-2884's `dispatch` scope = **enqueue** authority ("start a Claude Code… session on the operator's machine"); LIN-3059's "take" is the **consumer side** (run the item on the runner's own machine). They are distinct authorities and should not be silently fused.
- Quoting LIN-2884: "Mintable only by a session whose `accountId` owns the workspace; **never by exchange from a bootstrap token, never inherited by a worker's children.**" (and "`read`/`readWrite` no longer pass those routes"; "A worker that needs to dispatch children… gets the scope explicitly on its own mint, recorded as such.")
- Tension: a copied prompt carries a **bootstrap**; `exchangeBootstrapToken` copies scope verbatim (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:276`) and every dispatched bootstrap is minted `scope:'readWrite'` (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:398`). Two textual readings: **(a)** "exchange copies, never upgrades" — restriction is that no worker bootstrap is ever *minted* with `dispatch`; the owner's copy-time mint may stamp it. **(b)** "no take/dispatch scope may ever ride a bootstrap" — then the copy-time credential cannot be single-use-bootstrap-delivered, contradicting the +proxy design. Both survive the text; (b) is the stricter reading and is the one a ruling must resolve.

### Risk table
| Concern | (A) | (B) |
|---|---|---|
| Expiry | inherits 48h working TTL | mint property; still inherits LIN-2394 unless that store reports `expiresAt` correctly |
| Revocation | coarse (proxy token carries every proxy power) | fine-grained (runner credential id) |
| Workspace scoping | proxy token urlKey+owner | must stamp urlKey+`createdBy` (ownerless = dead-on-arrival) |
| Single-use | copy bootstrap single-use; take rides exchanged working token | bootstrap single-use; runner credential expiring |
| Mis-paste blast radius | widened (pasted token can run code) | strictly smaller |
| LIN-2394 `expiresAt` ~7h misreport | **inherits** | **inherits unless fixed** |

### Witness prerequisites (harbour.cat)
The rerun can use a copied prompt as the only credential only after the chosen design ships. Deploy prerequisites: the take/feedback-via-copy change on harbour.cat; an **isolated workspace Simple Dispatcher does not poll** (SD polls `linearviewer`/`m14-industries`/`tangle` only — LIN-3080's stated precondition, or SD races the driver and the run can't be attributed); an owner browser sign-in to copy. Research cannot supply: the isolated workspace urlKey, a real owner sign-in.

### History + measurement validity
Decisive prior episode: LIN-1576 (2026-07-25) — ownerless bootstrap mints, inherited through exchange, halted four autopilot trees ~100 min; lengthened by signal collapse (`token_ownerless` → `WORKSPACE_NOT_CONNECTED`). Safeguard that landed: LIN-1447 → LIN-1448 → **LIN-1582** (structural refusal inside `ProxyTokenStore.createToken`, because the "choke point" assumption was false — three sites escaped). Applies directly: a `dispatch`/`take`-scope restriction must be structural in the store+exchange, never per-route, and must carry a distinct failure signal. Measurement is **valid iff** it asserts authority refusals (readWrite/exchanged → 403 on take/dispatch) + a real poll→take→feedback loop + SD-coexistence; a bare green proxy/coordination signal (local run, `/instructions` 200) would NOT track the criterion.

### Security-boundary questions for John (open — do not resolve here)
1. **May a copy-time bootstrap carry take authority at all?** Options: (a) owner-session only; (b) owner + explicit "runner" opt-in; (c) never (take cannot ride a bootstrap). Rec: (b). Cost of (c): v1 upper rungs unrunnable from a copy. Cost of doing nothing: criterion unmet.
2. **Do take and enqueue share one grant?** Options: (a) one `dispatch` scope for both; (b) separate `dispatch` (enqueue) + `runner`/`take`. Rec: (b). Cost of (a): a worker's enqueue authority becomes a take authority; LIN-2884 invariant unfixable.
3. **TTL and revocation of the take-capable credential.** Options: (a) 48h like working tokens; (b) shorter + explicit revoke; (c) per-run/per-item. Rec: (b)/(c). Cost of (a): standing take credential reopens paste blast radius.
4. **Can a non-owner member ever hold it?** Options: (a) owner only (LIN-2884); (b) owner-minted delegation, audit-recorded. Rec: (a) for v1, (b) deferred. Cost of (b)-defer: none near-term. Doing nothing: a worker/exchanged token could take.

### Settled engineering choices (by evidence, not boundary)
- take/feedback consumers must accept a dispatch-token-shaped (or new runner) bearer, never a bare `readWrite` proxy token.
- scope restriction must be **structural** (store + exchange), per LIN-1582.
- `exchangeBootstrapToken` must never *upgrade* scope (already copies).
- feedback ownership stays `takenByTokenLabel`; any proxy/runner take must stamp a label matching its feedback credential.

### Surface Assessment
`Surface Assessment: refactor required: centralize the proxy scope vocabulary into one source of truth before adding a take/dispatch scope — consumer: routes/proxy.js:589 (requireWriteScope)`

Who-pays (every affected consumer): `lib/proxy-tokens.js:129` (createToken scope validation), `lib/proxy-tokens.js:276` (exchange scope copy — must refuse dispatch from a bootstrap), `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js:62` (session mint validation), `routes/proxy.js:588` (`requireWriteScope` + new sibling gates). Rationale: the scope enum is today duplicated across store + route + gate, and LIN-1582 proved per-site scope checks escape; a third value added per-site would recreate that outage shape.

### Unanswered questions
- Reading (a) vs (b) of "never by exchange" (boundary Q1 above).
- Whether the token model becomes multi-scope or one composite scope (design input, not resolved).
- Session-only routes' proxy inclusion (explicitly deferred; will split cleanly per beat-2 bounds).
- LIN-2394 `expiresAt` fix ownership (Backlog defect a scoped token inherits).

### Recommended next action
**`design`** — choose deliberately between the two evidenced credential shapes; no architecture is selected here.

## Design — LIN-3059 + LIN-2884 shared credential and scope (grounded at `06c754a`)

The full, self-contained design is now in this issue's description under **`## Shared credential + scope design (LIN-3059 + LIN-2884)`**. LIN-2884 adopts that section verbatim. This comment is the summary. No code changed.

**Research re-checked at HEAD.** Every cited claim holds, with minor line drift (exchange scope-copy at `lib/proxy-tokens.js:274`; the `local` self-take at `routes/dispatch.js:674`). Four new findings shape the design:
- **F1:** feedback ownership matches on the token *label*, and labels are shared (`prompt-proxy`, `dispatch-bootstrap`, `default`).
- **F2:** workspace membership is recorded, ownership is not.
- **F3:** any member can mint a never-expiring dispatch token that can take.
- **F4:** the copy-time mint takes its scope from the client request body.

**Comparison.** (A) puts take and feedback on the proxy token behind a take scope. It is the smaller change, but its blast radius is the widest, its revocation is coarse, and seven existing mint sites could request take. (B) mints a copy-time, owner-only, single-use bootstrap that exchanges for an expiring runner credential. That gives a strictly smaller mis-paste radius, revocation per runner, and one mint path that can be enforced in the store.

**Recommendation: B's issuance on A's plumbing.**
- The runner credential is an ordinary `ProxyTokenStore` document with `scope` + `grants[]` (`take` now, `dispatch` from LIN-2884), defined once in `lib/proxy-scopes.js`.
- `createToken` refuses grants structurally. `mintGrantBootstrap` is the only, owner-only, grant mint. The exchange copies grants and never adds them.
- `requireGrant` sits at the sub-router mount. A new runner sub-router serves poll, take and feedback. Ownership is by `takenByTokenId`, and the server, never the client, resolves grants.
- LIN-2884 then only adds `dispatch` and gates the enqueue mounts, with no reshaping.
- Coexistence with Simple Dispatcher in v1 is by isolation; the runner poll reports `otherConsumerLastSeenAt`.

**Security-boundary decisions: pending John's ruling (none decided here).**

| | Question | Recommendation | Effect on the plan |
|---|---|---|---|
| J1 | May an owner-minted copy-time bootstrap carry grants that the exchange copies (LIN-2884 "never by exchange" read as "never obtained or widened by exchange")? | (a) yes | **Blocks the shape** |
| J2 | Does the runner credential also carry `dispatch`? | (a) take + dispatch | Parameter, defaults to (a) |
| J3 | Lifetimes of the runner credential | 1h bootstrap / 24h working, plus revoke in Settings | Parameter: `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TTL` / `RUNNER_WORKING_TTL` |
| J4 | Who is "owner": O1 any member / O2 earliest membership edge / O3 explicit owner role / O4 allow-list | O3; delegation deferred to LIN-3085 | **Blocks the owner check's body** |
| J5 | Make the legacy member dispatch-token mint owner-only? | (b), under LIN-2884 after J4 | Routes to LIN-2884; does not block |

**Implementation outline.**
- **S1** (seams 1–4, plus unit pins):
  - the vocabulary module;
  - the `grants` field and the store refusal;
  - `mintGrantBootstrap`;
  - the grant-copying exchange.
  
  It changes no behaviour and is LIN-2884's prerequisite too. **Cut after S1.**
- **S2** (seams 5–10, plus e2e):
  - `requireGrant`;
  - the runner routes;
  - `takenByTokenId`;
  - the owner-checked runner copy mint (`routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js` / `public/common.js`);
  - prose-lane delivery (the prompt body is LIN-3098);
  - the instructions and docs.
- **Witness:**
  - unit pins for every refusal code;
  - an e2e loop;
  - the LIN-2394 `expiresAt`-vs-401 check;
  - after deploy, LIN-3080's two copied-prompt runs on harbour.cat. These need John for an isolated workspace Simple Dispatcher doesn't poll, and an owner sign-in.

**Deferred.**
- North-star writes: LIN-3066.
- Feature flags: LIN-3064.
- Roadmap write verb: LIN-3067.
- Dispatch history and next-run proxy versions: to file as a follow-up at planning.
- F3: J5, carried by LIN-2884 (LIN-1598 / LIN-2883).
- Delegation: LIN-3085.

**Recommended next action: `plan`.** Planning is gated on the **J1** and **J4** rulings; J2 and J3 can be planned as named defaults.

**Autopilot (stepper) status: parked for John's security-boundary ruling. Research and design are done; plan is next.**

The credential design needs a security-boundary decision that is John's to make.

**Done and verified:**
- **Research (4 beats)** is grounded at `06c754a`. See comment `bfa80a99` and the "Research findings (2026-09-27)" section.
- **Design (3 beats)** is in the description under **`## Shared credential + scope design (LIN-3059 + LIN-2884)`**. The design comment is `da2b9c7d`, and LIN-2884 links to it in comment `3344eb08`.
- **Chosen shape: B's issuance on A's plumbing.**
  - The owner's session mints a single-use bootstrap when the prompt is copied.
  - The bootstrap exchanges for a working token that expires.
  - Both are `ProxyTokenStore` docs carrying `grants[]`: `take` now, `dispatch` from LIN-2884.
  - Ordinary `createToken` structurally refuses grants.
  - Grants are enforced by `requireGrant` at the sub-router mount.

**Why it's parked:** J1 decides the plan's shape, and J4 is the body of the owner check. Both set who may run code on a person's machine, so both are John's. J2 and J3 only set values with named defaults. J5 is LIN-2884's to carry. The full options and costs are in §J of the shared section.

**One reply unblocks it.** Accept the recommended set, or answer J1–J4 individually:
- **J1 (a):** a bootstrap minted by the owner at copy time may carry grants. The exchange copies them and never adds any.
- **J2 (a):** the runner credential carries both `take` and `dispatch`.
- **J3 (b):** a 1h bootstrap and a 24h working token, with list-and-revoke in Settings.
- **J4 (c):** an explicit `role: owner` on the membership edge, backfilled once from the earliest membership edge. Delegation to other members is deferred to LIN-3085.

**Cost of waiting:** LIN-3059's plan, and so LIN-2884, LIN-3098 and LIN-2942, stay unstarted. No code lands until the ruling.

**Flight Companion note for the LIN-3059 plan (advice, not a ruling).**

J4 (c) in §J, "an explicit `role: owner` on the membership edge, backfilled once from the earliest membership edge", looks like the same rule that LIN-1892 slice S1 already builds. S1 is PR #1601, "workspace owner edge + read-only ownership dry-run", and it marks the first account to link a workspace as its owner.

- **Before designing the owner check's body, read PR #1601.** If S1's mark fits, reuse it instead of adding a second owner field and a second backfill. That saves a slice of work and keeps one definition of 'owner'.
- **S1's merge is held on John's ruling `lin1892-s1-edgeless-owner`.** The ruling needs a pre-deploy dry run on prod, which John will run the next time he's at the machine. issue.title: The runner prompt: Harbour serves the prompt that turns a person's Claude Code session into their runner
issue.description:
**Filed 26 Sep 2026 at John's request, from LIN-3080's findings.**

## What this is

The prompt that "○ set up ›" on the opened task points at. A person copies it into their own Claude Code session, and that session becomes the runner for their workspace: it takes their dispatched work and runs each item through its own subagents, including a whole Autopilot task, with no Simple Dispatcher. Harbour serves it, the way it already serves the Passage Runner prompt (`/passage-runner/prompt`).

LIN-3080 proved the shape on a local Harbour (see its witness comment and close-out): take → confirm → subagent → feedback → terminal; follow-ups continuing the same subagent (3/3); a full Autopilot task to Done. Start from the spike's driver template (`driver-prompt.md`, `driver.mjs`, `broker.mjs`, attached to or recorded on LIN-3080).

## What the served prompt must do

* **Poll and take** for the workspace, using the credential LIN-3059 lets a copied prompt carry.
* **Confirm** every taken item against `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/:id/prompt` and refuse on a mismatch.
* **One subagent per item.** A `followUpTo` item continues the same subagent instead of starting a new one.
* **Keep tokens away from subagents.** Today's claude-code item prompts assume Simple Dispatcher's local credential broker (`$HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE`, no auth header; `lib/proxy-preamble.js`), so they fail as written in a person's session. Choose one fix: the runner ships its own small broker (the spike's was about 40 lines), or claude-code prompts gain a no-broker variant. Record which, and why.
* **Report execution, not only coordination**, so the run page (LIN-2948) has something to show:
  * a `[handoff]` entry per subagent;
  * `[usage]` stamped with the realised `harness` and `model` (`lib/task-cost.js` reads the harness from the usage line, not the item);
  * terminal markers `[done]`/`[failed]`/`[blocked]`.
* **Run its own watchdog.** There is no Simple Dispatcher reaper. A stalled subagent posts `[blocked] stalled`, and the runner notices when its own poll loop dies (it died once in the spike, unnoticed by anything else).
* **Be honest about who it works for.** Claude Code only: opencode has no subagents. Say what happens when the laptop closes mid-run.

## Done looks like

* The prompt is served by Harbour and linked from "○ set up ›".
* A recorded run from a copied prompt against [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>), not localhost: one single step and one tiny Autopilot task, with dispatch ids and the run's record. This can be the same witness LIN-3059 owes.

## Related

LIN-3080 (the spike), LIN-3059 (the credential; blocks this), LIN-2884 (the "run code on my machine" scope), LIN-2942 (the ladder), LIN-2948 (the run page), LIN-3094 (Opus 5.5 pricing, so the runner's cost reads priced).

## Implementation Plan

**Revision 2 (beat 3/3).** This answers plan review `3a2e5ada` (Verdict: Revise). B1–B5 and N1–N5 are each addressed below, and the changelog is at the end. The plan is grounded at `5f25b4a0`, which is still `origin/main`.

**Direction:** E1–E7 from research `5861ce25`. **Slices:** 6 PRs. S1–S5 depend on no unfinished LIN-2884 work. S6 goes last and waits on LIN-3136 (T3).

**Boundaries.**

* No change to Simple Dispatcher or host configuration.
* No edits to LIN-3059 files (`routes/proxy-runner.js`, `routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js`, `lib/proxy-tokens.js`, `lib/proxy-scopes.js`, `public/proxy.js`, `lib/render-proxy.js`), to LIN-2884 code, to LIN-2942 (press recording) or to LIN-3099.
* The runner kit only *calls* LIN-3059's routes and `getRunnerBootstrap`.

### Decisions

* **Q1: orphaned items.**
  * No successor-lineage rule and no human-close path; those would be new rules, and they are John's.
  * The copy says what actually happens (B4): rows a lost runner took stay `taken` until history expires (30 days, `lib/dispatch-store.js:248`). A parent Autopilot waiting on them hangs. The owner re-dispatches the task; the duplicate guard only spans 5 minutes (`lib/dispatch-factory.js:62`).
  * The one in-lineage remedy is the ids-only ledger in S2. A restarted runner that still holds the **same** working token posts `[failed] runner restarted: subagent lost` on its own rows. It is the same token and lineage (`ownershipFilter`, `lib/dispatch-store.js:2199-2206`), so no new rule.
* **Q2 and the credential at rest: pending John's ruling** `lin3098-same-user-boundary`**.** The plan proceeds on the default:
  * **Broker:** a **same-user-restricted** broker. It is a Unix domain socket, mode 600, in a mode-700 directory, so the kernel refuses other OS users. See S1.
  * **Runner's own credential:** a mode-600 file in a mode-700 directory.
  * Token storage (`credentialStore` in `lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`) and broker transport (`brokerTransport` in `lib/runner-kit/broker.mjs`) each sit behind **one function**, so either can change before S1/S2 merge if John rules otherwise.
  * The remaining exposure is the same-user boundary only: another process running as the same user, subagents included. That is the same class for both.
* **Q3: items without API access.**
  * The runner never derives a subagent credential from its own token; such items run with no API access.
  * `proxyForce` is scoped (N3). Only the ladder's run-step rung, and only in a browser where this workspace's runner was set up, forces `attachProxy`. The shared `handleDispatch`, the dispatch disclosure and the +proxy toggle are unchanged for everyone else.
* **Q4: enqueue trust before T3.** Attribution is decided on the **poll** result, before any take (B1). A refused item is **never taken**: it stays queued, the owner can delete it (`DELETE /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch/:itemId`, `routes/dispatch.js:1053`), and otherwise it expires at 24h. `attributeItem(pollItem, {ownerAccountId, readRoot})`:
  * **pass** if `dispatchedBy === ownerAccountId`. This covers owner UI dispatches (`routes/dispatch.js:403,576`) and everything enqueued through owner-created proxy tokens (`routes/proxy-dispatch.js:365,580,1015,1303`, `routes/proxy-kickoff.js:395`). The chain is: bootstrap `createdBy` from the session (`routes/dispatch.js:509,552`), copied on exchange (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:547,672`), then `req.proxyCreatedBy` (`routes/proxy.js:580`).
  * **pass** a wake if `kind === 'wake'`, `dispatchedBy == null`, and `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/{followUpTo}` reads `dispatchedBy === ownerAccountId`. Wakes carry `followUpTo = child.sessionId` and no attribution (`lib/dispatch-wake.js:196-208`); the watch exposes `dispatchedBy` (`routes/proxy-dispatch.js:98`).
  * **otherwise leave it queued.** The check is not widened.
  * `ownerAccountId` arrives in the credential block that `/runner` composes from the minting session's `accountId`. Only the owner can mint (`mintGrantBootstrap`), so it is the owner's id by construction.
  * *Why:* this is stricter than `lin3059-credential-boundary-j1-j4` (`rec`), so it grants nothing new.
* **Harness (N2).** Items whose explicit `harness` is set and is not `claude-code` (poll carries it, `lib/dispatch-store.js:2707`) are **skipped at poll time** and left queued, the same way as B1. The copy says: "this runner is Claude Code only; items asked for another harness are left for a runner of that harness." `null` passes: wakes store `null` and inherit the parent's harness.
* **Rulings respected.**
  * `lin3059-credential-boundary-j1-j4` = `rec`: the owner-minted copy-time bootstrap carries take+dispatch, lives 1h, exchanges to 24h, with Settings revoke.
  * `lin2884-orchestrator-dispatch-grant` = `declared-kinds`: provisional; the T2c and T3 merges are held.

### S1: the broker (`lib/runner-kit/broker.mjs`)

**Behaviour:**

* **Transport** (behind `brokerTransport`):
  * It listens on a Unix domain socket at `~/.harbour-runner/s/<itemId8>.sock`. The directory is mode 700; the socket is created under `umask(0o177)` so it is mode 600.
  * The path is kept under macOS's **104-byte** `sun_path` **limit**. That is verified: a long scratch path fails with `EINVAL`, while `~/.harbour-runner/s/<id8>.sock` is about 43 bytes.
  * The subagent's base is `HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE=http://harbour-runner.invalid` plus `--unix-socket <path>` on every curl. A curl without the flag fails closed on name resolution (curl exit 6, verified), and the `.invalid` name never resolves.
  * The broker also refuses any `Host` other than `harbour-runner.invalid`.
  * *Verified locally (curl 8.7.1, Node 25):* the socket is created `srw-------` inside a `drwx------` directory, and `curl --unix-socket` round-trips.
* **Forwarding:**
  * It forwards only `/api/proxy/*` to the configured Harbour base.
  * Write verbs require `X-Harbour-Intent: write`.
  * It logs `method path status` only.
* **Credential:** the item's bootstrap arrives on **stdin**. The broker exchanges it itself (`POST /api/proxy/token`) and keeps the working token **only in memory**, never on disk, argv, env or logs.
* **Lifetime (B3):** it self-exits when any of these holds:
  1. The runner heartbeat file (`~/.harbour-runner/<urlKey>/runner.heartbeat`) is older than `BROKER_STALE_MS` (10 min) on **two consecutive checks that each follow a normal-length tick**. A tick gap much longer than the check interval means the machine slept, and restarts the grace window, so waking from sleep doesn't kill a live item.
  2. The maximum lifetime of 48h (the worker token's lifetime, `LIFETIME_PROFILES.worker`) has passed.
  3. It receives SIGTERM.

  *An idle timeout is declined:* a subagent can legitimately go a long time without an API call, and a broker that exits can't be re-armed, because the bootstrap is spent.
* **Discovery:** `~/.harbour-runner/<urlKey>/brokers/<itemId>.json` holds `{pid, socket, itemId, startedAt}` and **no token**. `stop-broker` reads it, checks the pid still owns that socket, sends SIGTERM, then removes the file and the socket.

**Tests (written first):** `tests/unit/runner-kit-broker.test.js`, using a fake upstream on `127.0.0.1` and the socket in a short `mkdtemp` directory. It checks that:

* the socket mode is 600 and the directory mode is 700, by `fs.stat`. This pins the same-user restriction; the kernel enforces it.
* a wrong `Host` gets 403;
* a non-`/api/proxy/` path gets 404;
* a write without intent gets 403;
* a GET is forwarded with a bearer the client never sent;
* the token is not in logs, not in argv (spawned with stdin) and not in any file under the kit directory;
* **a stale heartbeat closes the socket**;
* a simulated sleep gap does **not** close it;
* the maximum lifetime closes it;
* `stop-broker` using the pid file closes it and removes the pid file and the socket.

**Verification:** `npm run test:hermetic` green; PR CI `ci-success` green; review Approve; close-out.

### S2: the runner helper (`lib/runner-kit/runner.mjs`), its decisions and the local loop

**Commands:**

* `recover`
* `login`, which reads the bootstrap from stdin
* `poll`
* `wait`, a background long-poll
* `take <id>`
* `feedback <id> <kind> <msg>`
* `usage <agentId>`
* `stop-broker <id>`
* `ledger`

The runner's own token sits behind `credentialStore` in `~/.harbour-runner/<urlKey>/runner.token` (mode 600, directory 700). The **ids-only** ledger (B4) is `~/.harbour-runner/<urlKey>/ledger.json`, mapping `itemId → {agentId, rootItemId, state: running|stopped|done, tokenId}`. `poll`, `take` and `wait` never print a `bootstrapToken`.

**Pure functions, exported and table-tested:**

* `pollDecision(item, ctx)` returns `take`, `leave:<reason>` or `abort`. It runs, in order:
  1. harness (N2);
  2. `attributeItem` (Q4);
  3. `haltAction`;
  4. `confirmItem` against `/dispatch/:id/prompt`. The poll item already carries `prompt`, so confirmation also happens **before** take.
* `postTakeCheck(pollItem, takenItem)` requires byte-equality. A mismatch, which is unreachable in practice, is closed with `[skipped] refused: <reason>`. That marker is terminal but not a wake (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:20-26,48-53`), and **never** `[failed]` (B1).
* `haltAction(halt, item, ledger)`, with Simple Dispatcher's meaning (`simple-dispatcher/README.md` Halts):
  * `pause` takes only follow-ups and wakes for ledger subagents, and aborts;
  * `stop` takes nothing, stops every running subagent, posts `[aborted] Cancelled running session <id8> (stopped by operator).` on each row, and **keeps them in the ledger as** `stopped` (N4).
* `resolveFollowUp(item, ledger)`:
  * on a ledger hit that is `running` or `stopped`, it continues that subagent (N4);
  * on a miss, it posts `[failed] No live subagent to resume for follow-up (original dispatch <id> not found).`, following `simple-dispatcher/followup.js:40`.
  * It keys on every item id handed to that subagent (`followup.js:22-32`).
* `abortAction(item, ledger)` (B5), for an abort row (`abort:true`, `abortTo`, no prompt; `lib/proxy-instructions.js:773-774`):
  * **target running:** stop its subagent, post `[aborted] Cancelled running session <abortTo8> (running).` on the target row (the runner owns it), and post the same line on the abort row as its ack. This is Simple Dispatcher's ack-plus-child-post pair (`simple-dispatcher/dispatcher.js:541-567`).
  * **target already terminal:** post only the ack, `[aborted] Closed finished session <abortTo8> (done).`, on the abort row. Overwriting a real completion would be dishonest.
  * **target unknown:** post `[failed] No session to abort (<abortTo>).` on the abort row.
  * **Cascade:** Harbour expands `cascade:true` server-side into one plain abort per session (`lib/dispatch-store.js:1728-1741`). The runner handles each abort row the same way; it does no walk of its own.
  * Abort rows pass attribution the same way: `dispatchedBy` is the enqueuer.
* `recoverAction(ledger, currentTokenId)` (B4) runs on startup before `login` replaces anything:
  * for rows that are `running` or `stopped` with `tokenId === currentTokenId`, it posts `[failed] runner restarted: subagent lost` and marks them done;
  * rows from another `tokenId` are listed to the human as orphans, with the honest Q1 copy.
* `sumTranscriptUsage(jsonlLines)` returns `{harness:'claude-code', model, inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheCreation1hInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens}`. The model is the one with the most output tokens. With no readable transcript it returns `{harness:'claude-code', model?}` only, which reads unpriced, never a false $0.
* `watchdogAction(inflight, now, {stallMin, failMin, transcriptMtime})` returns `[blocked] stalled: subagent <id> silent for <n> min`, then `[failed] stalled: …` and a stop.
* `isHeartbeatStale(mtimeMs, nowMs, maxAgeMs, lastTickGapMs)` (N1) is shared with the broker.

**Keeping an idle session polling (N1).** The prompt tells the runner to run `node runner.mjs wait` as a **background Bash command** (`run_in_background`). It long-polls and refreshes `runner.heartbeat` every 30s, and it **exits** on work, a halt change, a stall or a 25-minute cap. Claude Code re-invokes the session when a background command exits, and the runner then re-arms `wait` before handling anything. On every turn the runner checks `isHeartbeatStale`; a stale heartbeat with no `wait` running means the poller died, so it re-arms. The fallback where background commands aren't available is `/loop 2m`. *This is Claude Code harness behaviour, stated as assumed; it is covered by the witness, not by CI.*

**Tests (written first):**

* `tests/unit/runner-kit-helper.test.js`, table rows for every function, including:
  * **B1:** a non-owner child with `sessionId` set to the owner's kickoff id gives `pollDecision → leave`, **no take**.
  * A wake whose root's `dispatchedBy` is foreign or null gives `leave`.
  * A non-wake with null `dispatchedBy` gives `leave`.
  * `postTakeCheck` mismatch gives `[skipped] refused: …`, and `findWakeEvent` of that line is null while `findTerminalFeedback` is `skipped`.
  * **N2:** `harness:'opencode'` gives `leave`; `null` and `'claude-code'` pass.
  * **B5:** `abortAction`'s three target states, and an ack line that `findTerminalFeedback` reads as `aborted`.
  * **N4:** `stop`, then a follow-up after the stop clears, gives `continue` on the stopped subagent.
  * **B4:** `recoverAction` with same-token and other-token rows.
  * **N1:** `isHeartbeatStale` (fresh, stale, sleep gap).
  * `sumTranscriptUsage` on `tests/fixtures/runner-kit/subagent.jsonl`, round-tripped through `parseUsage`.
  * No command's stdout contains a `bootstrapToken`.
* `tests/e2e/runner-kit-loop.spec.js`: local harness with `append:true` (the owner). It:
  1. mints the runner credential;
  2. runs `recover` (a no-op) and then `login`;
  3. takes an owner item through `poll → take`, with confirmation inside `pollDecision`;
  4. sends `feedback [done]` and asserts `done`;
  5. checks that a subscribed child's `[done]` wake passes;
  6. **B1:** enqueues an item attributed to a **different account** with `sessionId` set to the owner's kickoff id, then asserts that `poll` leaves it queued, that it is never taken, and that **no** `kind:'wake'` **row is minted** for the kickoff.

  The second account comes from a second local-harness session bound to the same workspace. If the harness can't bind one, add a test-only `/test/enqueue-dispatch-as` in `routes/test.js`. The spec also covers:
  * an abort row closing a live item (its `[aborted]` lines on both rows);
  * a `stop` halt that leaves fresh items queued.

**Verification:** as S1.

### S3: the served prompt, its endpoint and marker pins

**Files:**

* `docs/runner-prompt.md`: a preamble, then `---`, then the body. The body has one step per must-do:
   1. **Setup:** Claude Code only, Node 18+, macOS or Linux (Unix sockets); write the kit to `~/.harbour-runner/`; `recover`, then `login`.
   2. **The** `wait` **loop** (N1).
   3. **Poll-time decisions:** harness, then owner attribution, then halt, then confirmation. **Leave refused items queued; never take-then-**`[failed]` (B1).
   4. **Take**, then the post-take check.
   5. **One subagent per item.** The item prompt goes in verbatim, plus an environment preamble giving `HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE=http://harbour-runner.invalid` and "add `--unix-socket <path>` to every curl". A `followUpTo` item continues the same subagent. No token ever goes to a subagent.
   6. **Items with no** `bootstrapToken` run without API access (Q3).
   7. **Abort rows** (B5).
   8. **Markers**, in exactly the parser forms:
      * `[handoff] item <id> → subagent <agentId> (new|continued from <itemId>)`, `kind:'status'`;
      * a `recap`;
      * `[usage] {json}`, `kind:'usage'`, cumulative per subagent;
      * `[done]` / `[failed]` / `[aborted]` / `[skipped] refused:`;
      * `[blocked] …`, which is non-terminal, wakes the parent and reads as waiting on a human.
   9. **The watchdog.**
  10. **Halts:** binding. The prompt says `/api/proxy/instructions` still calls them advisory (LIN-3074) and must not be followed on this.
  11. **Laptop sleep and close, the 24h expiry, orphans and** `recover` (B4 copy).
  12. **The pre-T3 owner-only rule.**
  13. **The end summary.**
* `lib/prompts/runner-kickoff.js` exports `buildRunnerKickoff({ baseUrl })`, following the passage-runner pattern: it reads at HEAD, cuts at `---`, caches, and uses an uncached FALLBACK. It:
  * interpolates `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TTL_SECONDS` and `RUNNER_WORKING_TTL_SECONDS`, `HALT_MODES` and `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`;
  * inlines `lib/runner-kit/*.mjs` as fenced blocks.
* `routes/proxy-runner-prompt.js` serves `GET /api/proxy/runner/prompt` as `text/plain`, with its own chain (`proxyLimiter → authenticateProxyToken → requireGrant('take')`). It is mounted in `routes/proxy.js` **before** `createProxyRunnerRoutes` (`:1591`). `proxy-runner.js` is not edited.
* Docs: one line in the `lib/proxy-instructions.js` Runner Endpoints section (`:887-915`); `docs/proxy-integration.md`; `docs/architecture/source-map.md`. The prompt-template count is unaffected, since it counts `PROMPT_TEMPLATES`.

**Tests (written first):**

* `tests/unit/runner-prompt-markers.test.js` takes the literal lines from the prompt's fenced `markers` block and checks them against the parsers:
  * `findTerminalFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:109`) returns:
    * done for `[done]`;
    * failed for `[failed] …`, `[failed] runner restarted: subagent lost` and `[failed] No live subagent …`;
    * aborted for `[aborted] Cancelled running session …`;
    * skipped for `[skipped] refused: …`.
  * `findWakeEvent` (`:363`) returns:
    * `blocked` for `[blocked] stalled: …`, which is not terminal;
    * **null** for `[skipped] refused: …`.
  * `[handoff] …` matches neither.
  * `parseUsage([{kind:'usage', message}])` gives `harness:'claude-code'` and the example model.
* `tests/unit/runner-kickoff.test.js` checks that:
  * an anchor phrase is present for each must-do, B1's "leave queued", B4's honest orphan copy, B5's abort step and N2's harness copy;
  * every `HALT_MODES` value is present;
  * the TTLs are interpolated;
  * the kit is inlined byte-for-byte;
  * no token-shaped string appears;
  * the FALLBACK is not cached.
* `tests/unit/runner-prompt-route.test.js` checks that:
  * a take-grant token gets 200, equal to the builder output;
  * `readWrite` gets 403 `TAKE_GRANT_REQUIRED`;
  * no bearer gets 401;
  * the limiter and auth each run once (a counting fake).
* `tests/unit/proxy-endpoint-inventory-witness.test.js` gets a group-L row. The count goes 74 → 75, updating both the header and the `:583-584` assertion **and its per-file breakdown message to include** `routes/proxy-runner-prompt.js` (N5).
* The DI witness covers the new mount through its filesystem census, with a reach probe if the census requires one.

**Verification:** as S1.

### S4: the entry points and the phone-usable setup page (the UI mint)

**Entry points (B2).** John on [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) has **both** flags on, so no `○ set up ›` renders for him (`public/prompt-section.js:223-232`; flags default off, `lib/feature-defaults.js`). The entry points are:

1. `public/prompt-section.js`: a link **beside** the ladder, not a rung: `<a data-testid="opened-task-runner-link" href="/workspace/:urlKey/runner">run on my machine ›</a>`. It renders whenever `proxyEnabled` is true, whatever the dispatch flag. It carries no `data-rung`, so existing ladder parsing is untouched (`tests/unit/prompt-section-p0.test.js:494`).
2. The `○ set up ›` notices for `dispatch` and `proxy` gain the same link. Only the notice slot is written (N4 of LIN-2944), the old text is unchanged, and the press is not recorded (LIN-2942).
3. `lib/render-dispatch.js` (the Dispatch page, shown when the dispatch flag is on): one line in the Tokens section, "Run on your own machine instead: set up a runner ›". This is not a LIN-3059 file.

`routes/runner-setup.js` serves `GET /workspace/:urlKey/runner` (`workspaceFromUrl`), mounted in `server.js`. It **never redirects**. Its states:

* **proxy off:** a notice with a Settings link and no mint button.
* **not owner:** from the `getWorkspaceOwnerAccountId` read (`lib/workspace-owner.js`), a notice and no button. The server mint stays authoritative.
* **owner, dispatch off (B2):** the mint button, plus "to use **run this step**, turn on the Dispatch queue in Settings" with a link. S4 verifies which rungs work with dispatch off and states it exactly.
* **owner, both on:** the mint button.

`lib/render-runner-setup.js`**:**

* intro copy: Claude Code only, Node 18+, macOS or Linux, the 1h and 24h lifetimes, the pre-T3 owner-only rule, **B4's orphan copy**, and what happens when the laptop sleeps or closes;
* the served prompt in a disclosure;
* `data-url-key`, and `data-account-id` in the owner states only;
* links to Settings › Runner credentials (revoke) and the witness runbook;
* a mobile-first layout.

`public/runner-setup.js`, a two-tap flow:

* **Tap 1:** `getRunnerBootstrap(urlKey)`. It composes a `## Your runner credential` block (`baseUrl`, `urlKey`, `ownerAccountId`, the bootstrap, `expiresAt`, and "pipe into `runner.mjs login`; never echo it") into a readonly, pre-selected `<textarea>`.
* **Tap 2:** a synchronous `clipboard.writeText`. If that fails, the text stays selected for a long-press copy, and it includes the credential.
* Errors render from `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_ERROR_COPY`.
* After a successful mint it sets `localStorage['harbour-runner:<urlKey>']=1`, wrapped in try/catch. This marker is the N3 scope.
* The token is never logged, never stored and never server-rendered.

**N3.** `renderLadder` stamps `data-proxy-force="runner"` on the enabled run-step rung only when `proxyEnabled` is true **and** the marker is present. `handleDispatch` reads it: `proxyForce: existing || btn.dataset.proxyForce === 'runner'`. The disclosure buttons, the toggle and every other caller are unchanged. The PR description and the `/runner` copy state that "run this step" from this browser always carries workspace API access once a runner has been set up here.

**Tests (written first):**

* `tests/unit/runner-setup-render.test.js`: the four states. The button and `data-account-id` appear only in the owner states, and there is no token anywhere.
* `tests/unit/prompt-section-runner-link.test.js`, a new file:
  * the link renders with the proxy flag on, and not with it off;
  * the notices keep their old text plus the link;
  * `generate a prompt first` is byte-identical (`prompt-section-p0.test.js:821`);
  * `data-proxy-force` appears only with the marker, the dispatch payload carries `proxyForce:true` only then, and the disclosure path is unchanged.
* `tests/e2e/runner-setup.spec.js`: an iPhone-sized viewport with `hasTouch` and clipboard permissions. States:
  * **(a) owner, both on:** tap 1 gives a textarea holding the prompt, the bootstrap, `expiresAt` and the owner id; tap 2 fills the clipboard; the bootstrap exchanges to grants `take,dispatch`.
  * **(b) non-owner** (`/test/set-workspace-ownership?state=foreign`): no button.
  * **(c) proxy off:** a notice and **no mint request**, checked by interception.
  * **(d)** `○ set up ›` (dispatch off) reaches `/runner`.
  * **(e) both flags on:** `opened-task-runner-link` is visible on the opened task and reaches `/runner`.
  * **(f) proxy on, dispatch off:** `/runner` shows the dispatch-off note and the mint works.
* The existing `tests/e2e/opened-task-first-screen.spec.js:340-362` (`toContainText`) must stay green unchanged.

**Verification:** as S1, plus a manual check at 390px width in the PR.

### S5: the witness runbook for John (doc only)

**File:** `docs/runbooks/runner-hosted-witness.md`, linked from `/runner` and posted on LIN-3098 at close-out. It is short and phone-friendly:

1. On [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>), as the owner, use a **fresh** workspace that Simple Dispatcher does not poll, and create no dispatch token for it. In Settings, turn on **workspace API access** and the **Dispatch queue**.
2. Open any task and tap **"run on my machine ›"** beside the ladder. The Dispatch page also links to it. Tap **create runner prompt**, then **copy**. Within 1h, paste it into Claude Code (laptop, or [claude.ai/code](<http://claude.ai/code>) from the phone).
3. **Run 1:** on a task, tap **run this step**.
4. **Run 2:** tap **run the whole task** on a tiny throwaway task.
5. **Capture:**
   * every dispatch id: the root, each child and each wake;
   * `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/:id` for each (status, plus `[handoff]`, `[usage]` and the terminals);
   * `/issues/:id/cost`;
   * the runner's end summary.
6. **Optional probes:**
   * a `readWrite` token on `/api/proxy/runner/*` gets 403;
   * a second exchange gets 401;
   * a revoke makes the next poll 401;
   * an item from another account stays queued, with no wake.
7. **If the runner dies:** its taken rows stay `taken`. Re-dispatch the task (B4). Post the captures on LIN-3098.

**Nobody in this run performs the witness.**

**Verification:** a docs-only PR; CI green (secret scan included); review.

### S6 (last, dependent): post-T3 alignment

**Waits on:** **LIN-3136 (T3)** merged and deployed. T3 itself waits on **T2c PR #1616** (`lin3135-r2-sd-refire-ruling`). Nothing waits on **T4 PR #1617**, which gates the legacy dispatch-token mint the runner never uses.

**Re-check for revision 2:** the Unix-socket broker, the entry points, abort handling, the ledger and the poll-time attribution all use endpoints on `main` today (the poll/take/feedback surface, `/dispatch/:id` watch, `expandCascadeAborts`). None depends on unfinished LIN-2884 work.

**Changes:**

* `docs/runner-prompt.md`: a `403 DISPATCH_GRANT_REQUIRED` on an enqueue is reported as `[failed] …` and stops that item. The "until T3" copy is updated.
* `lib/render-runner-setup.js`: the same copy.
* `docs/runbooks/runner-hosted-witness.md`: a post-T3 Autopilot re-witness step.
* The owner-only `attributeItem` check **stays after T3**: ruled `lin3098-owner-check-after-t3` = **keep** (John, 29 Sep, comment `9490ba7f`). S6 therefore changes no attribution logic; its copy says the owner-only rule is permanent, not "until T3".

**Tests:** marker and kickoff anchors, plus a helper row for the 403.

**Verification:** as S1.

### Risks

* **R1: wake attribution (corrected).**
  * Poll-time attribution means the runner **never takes** a non-owner item. So its own refusals mint no wakes, and the review's B1 path is closed. The e2e asserts that no wake row is minted.
  * Residual: `producingItemId` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:2089`) isn't exposed. So if some **other** consumer took a non-owner child whose `sessionId` is the owner's root and posted a marker, the resulting wake would pass on its root.
  * Mitigation: the runner stops when `otherConsumerLastSeenAt` is recent, and the witness uses a workspace no other consumer polls. The real fix, exposing `producingItemId`, is a later ticket and not widened here.
* **R2: server rows refused.** Other server-enqueued non-wake rows with a null `dispatchedBy` stay queued before T3 (for example periodicals or triage). This is stated in the copy.
* **R3: merged accounts.** A raw `dispatchedBy` against a canonical owner could refuse a merged-account owner's items. Add a test if a fixture exists; otherwise it is copy only.
* **R4: Claude Code internals.** The transcript path, `run_in_background` re-invocation and continuing a stopped subagent are all assumed. They degrade to unpriced usage, `/loop`, and "fresh subagent plus recap" respectively. The witness observes them; CI can't.
* **R5: platform.** Node 18+ and a Unix-socket curl are needed (macOS and Linux). Windows is out of scope for v1 and stated on `/runner`.
* **R6: iOS clipboard** behaviour is assumed. The fallback is a pre-selected textarea that holds the credential.
* **R7: the same-user boundary.** A subagent running as the same user could read `runner.token` or connect to a broker socket. This is pending `lin3098-same-user-boundary`, and both sit behind one function.
* **R8: route order.** The mount order of the new prompt route is pinned by the inventory witness and the counting-fake test.
* **R9: pricing.** `claude-opus-5-5` stays unpriced until LIN-3094.
* **R10: 48h worker tokens.** A crashed broker is bounded by the stale-heartbeat exit (about 10 minutes after the runner dies, not counting sleep) and the 48h cap, and it is same-user only.

### Open for John

1. `lin3098-same-user-boundary` (being put to John as one ruling): is the same-user boundary acceptable for both the broker (a mode-600 Unix socket) and the runner credential (a mode-600 file)? The plan proceeds on that default, and both are swappable behind one function before S1/S2 merge.
2. ~~After LIN-3136 (T3) is live: keep or drop the owner-only ~~`~~dispatchedBy~~`~~ check?~~ **Ruled:** `lin3098-owner-check-after-t3` = **keep** (comment `9490ba7f`).
3. *(Not needed by this plan.)* Any successor-lineage or human path to close a lost runner's `taken` rows would be a new who-may-use rule, and only John can make it.

### Changelog (revision 2, review `3a2e5ada`)

B1 poll-time attribution and `[skipped]`; B2 entry points and states (e)/(f); B3 broker self-exit, pid file and Unix socket; B4 honest orphan copy and the same-token ledger; B5 `abortAction`; N1 the `wait` loop and heartbeat test; N2 harness skip; N3 rung-scoped `proxyForce`; N4 stop parity; N5 the inventory per-file message. Q2 is now cited as `lin3098-same-user-boundary`. Slices went from 5 to 6: the kit was split into broker (S1) and helper (S2).

**Finding from periodical: Drift & Coherence Review (LIN-3100), 2026-09-26.** Report: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/main/docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-09-26.md (merged in `08257bd3`, PR #1591)

This bears on the runner prompt. Today the shared vocabulary between the two sides is kept in two separate copies: Simple Dispatcher produces it, and Harbour consumes it. There is no shared source and no cross-repo test.
- **Sentinel, DECISION and marker words** (findings 11 and 10). `simple-dispatcher/hook.js:508` emits `[decision] `, and `LinearViewer/lib/session-telemetry.js:674` parses it.
  - The sentinel words live in `meta-prompt-template.js:204,303,306` and `prompt-formatters.js:918`.
  - The `[done]`/`[pending]`/`[blocked]`/`[failed]`/`[usage]`/`[evidence]` prefixes are matched in `render-session.js:158-220` and `kpi-stats.js`.
  - The halt modes `pause`/`stop` are copied in `lib/workspace-halt.js:28` and `simple-dispatcher/halt.js` (tracked by LIN-3074).
- **`target`** (contract table, Low-medium). SD owns the runner set in `simple-dispatcher/targets.js:17-18` (`cli`, `web`). LinearViewer has no single canonical definition. It has three lists that disagree (`routes/dispatch.js:295`, `routes/proxy.js:304`, `routes/collective.js:40`) plus 16 inline literal sites.

**Why it matters here.** A runner prompt served by Harbour would become a third producer of this vocabulary. The words it tells the session to emit have to match what `session-telemetry.js` and `render-session.js` parse exactly. It would be worth sourcing them from one place, not copying them a third time.

**Finding from periodical: Onboarding & Cold-Start Review (LIN-3106), 2026-09-26.** Report: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/901934717dcd3fce66fd0367dc50e66486882a36/docs/reviews/onboarding-cold-start-review-2026-09-26.md (merged in `90193471`, PR #1592)

**A scope note for the next run (§2, point 2).** No own-session runner product exists yet, so none was walked cold. The report names the runner prompt, this ticket, as the thing the next edition must decide whether to add to the cold-start journey set once it ships.

A related current fact, R2-13 (J5a): the access instructions today depend on the harness, and the two sets are mutually exclusive.
- claude-code sessions get `HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE` and an MCP token.
- opencode sessions get only a bootstrap embedded in the prompt.
- The source is `simple-dispatcher/dispatcher.js:1112-1258`.

A runner prompt that Harbour serves will need to cover whichever harness the person runs.

**Finding from periodical: Documentation Review (LIN-3102), 2026-09-26.** Report: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/blob/27aaf08a18a181f664fbeb311f52c0b6fff02668/docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-09-26.md (merged in `27aaf08a`, PR #1594)

Two findings bear on writing the runner prompt from Harbour's docs.
- **H13 (HIGH, owned by LIN-3074): the halt docs are wrong.** About 26 places in LinearViewer still say the runner does not honour a halt ("pending LIN-2995"). LIN-2995 is Done, and `simple-dispatcher` does enforce `pause` and `stop`:
  - the logic is `halt.js` `resolveEffectiveHalt`, precedence `stop > pause`, source `harbour > local > auto`;
  - it is documented in `simple-dispatcher/README.md:231`.
  - Stale places include `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md`, `docs/dispatch-integration.md:129-130`, `docs/proxy-integration.md:2402,2441` and `docs/runbooks/harbour-degraded.md`.
  - A runner prompt written from those docs would wrongly tell the session that halts are advisory.
- **DC-dispatch-fields (MED, new ticket LIN-3116): three proxy dispatch fields are undocumented.** `queueIfBusy`, `waitForFollowUps` and `subscription` are accepted by `routes/proxy-dispatch.js:225` but appear nowhere in `docs/proxy-integration.md`. `queueIfBusy` is also missing from `lib/proxy-instructions.js`. A runner that drives Autopilot needs `subscription` at the very least.

## Research findings (LIN-3098, beat 1/2)

**Grounded at** LinearViewer `main` `5f25b4a0`, which contains LIN-3059 S1 `b0751689`, S2a `fd528742`, S1b `e9c8b3f1` and S2b `40f53dbe` (each checked with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`). Simple Dispatcher is at `3b1e734` (== origin/main) and was only read. No code changed.

**Read first:**
- LIN-3080's spike template: `driver-prompt.md`, `driver.mjs` and `broker.mjs`, all in comment `5565753c`, plus final note `6f185601`.
- LIN-3059 runbook `5f66116a` and ruling `643adf08`: J1a, J2a take+dispatch, J3b 1h/24h, J4c owner role.
- The hosted-witness ruling `a743e53a`: **after-3098**, with the UI mint phone-friendly.
- LIN-2884's rulings and its T2c/T3/T4 state.
- LIN-3098 has **no rulings**. John's 29 Sep "UI mint, phone-friendly" requirement lives in `lin3059-hosted-witness` (suggested answer `after-3098`), not in a LIN-3098 row.

**Correction to the task text:** there is no `GET /api/proxy/halt`. The proxy halt read is `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/halt` (`routes/proxy-halt.js:25,44`).

---

### 1. "○ set up ›": where it renders, where it leads, what a phone flow needs

**Where it renders.** `public/prompt-section.js` `renderLadder`, the opened-task ladder, mounted only from `public/swipe.js:804`:
- **"run this step"** shows `○ set up ›` when `dispatchEnabled` is false (`:223`, `data-setup-needs="dispatch"`).
- **"run the whole task"** shows it when `!(proxyEnabled && hasAutopilot)` (`:228`, `data-setup-needs="proxy"`).
- The flags come from `lib/render-swipe.js:613-615` (`featureFlags.dispatch` and `featureFlags.proxy`).

**Where it leads now: nowhere.** A press only writes a one-line notice into the notice slot (`public/prompt-section.js:729-744`), for example "running this step needs the dispatch runner set up". There is no link, route or mint behind it.

**The runner mint exists, but no UI calls it (console only today).**
- Server route: `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/proxy/tokens {"runner":true}` (`routes/proxy-tokens-admin.js:93-139`).
  - Owner-checked `mintGrantBootstrap` (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:365-395`), with `RUNNER_GRANTS = ['take','dispatch']` (`lib/proxy-scopes.js:28`) and the `runner` profile: 1h bootstrap, 24h working (`lib/proxy-scopes.js:52-59`).
  - Client `grants` are refused (`:87-91`).
  - It is gated on the **proxy** flag (`:76`) and the per-IP `proxyTokenCreationLimiter`.
- Client helper: `window.ProxyToggle.getRunnerBootstrap(urlKey)` (`public/common.js:1627-1668`) returns `{token, expiresAt, grants}` or `{error:{code,message}}`, with the copy map `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_ERROR_COPY` (`:1603-1611`). Its own docstring says the caller is LIN-3098.
- `git grep getRunnerBootstrap` finds **only its definition and export** (`public/common.js:1627,1747`). No page calls it, so today the only way to mint is from the browser console or a hand-made session `fetch`. That is exactly what runbook step 3 has John do.
- Settings has **list and revoke only**: the "Runner credentials" group on the Proxy page (`lib/render-proxy.js:86-89`, `public/proxy.js:317-400`). The Proxy page redirects to Settings when the proxy flag is off (`server.js:3367-3376`).

**The closest existing pattern is a session page with a server-built prompt and a mint on copy.** Flight Companion (`routes/flight-companion.js:482-493`, `public/flight-companion.js:68-91`) and Passage Planner (`routes/passage-planner.js:45`, `public/passage-planner.js:34-40`) both follow it:
1. The route renders the builder's prompt into a `<pre>`.
2. On "copy", the client awaits `ProxyToggle.maybeAppend(..., {force:true})`, which mints.
3. It then calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText`.

**What a phone-usable flow needs**, built on that pattern:
- **A destination.** `○ set up ›` becomes a link (or opens a panel) to a session page, for example `/workspace/:urlKey/runner`. The page renders the served runner prompt and a **"create runner prompt"** button that calls `getRunnerBootstrap(urlKey)` and composes prompt plus credential block client-side. The bootstrap must never be server-rendered into HTML; it is minted only on an explicit POST press.
- **A two-tap copy on mobile.** Existing pages mint and then write to the clipboard after an `await`. On iOS Safari a clipboard write after an awaited network call commonly loses the user gesture (*assumed from platform behaviour, not tested here*). Also, the existing error fallback ("select the text and copy manually", `public/flight-companion.js:89`) would copy a prompt **without** the token, because the `<pre>` holds only the bare prompt.
  - So: tap 1 mints and renders the composed prompt into a selectable, wrapped field that shows `expiresAt` (1h).
  - Tap 2 copies synchronously in a fresh gesture.
  - Failure codes render from `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_ERROR_COPY`: `GRANT_OWNER_ONLY`, `WORKSPACE_OWNER_UNSET` and so on.
- **Flag and role honesty on the page.**
  - With the proxy flag off, the mint 403s (`proxy-tokens-admin.js:76`), so the page must say so rather than offer a dead button.
  - A non-owner gets `GRANT_OWNER_ONLY`.
  - The page should link to Settings › Runner credentials for revoke.
- **Pressing `○ set up ›` must not be recorded.** That belongs to LIN-2942 (`prompt-section.js:730-731`), which this ticket must not touch. LIN-3098 changes only where the press leads.
- **Cross-dependency.** LIN-2884 T3's 403 guidance already tells callers to "use the runner copy from Settings" (LIN-3136 description, R3). Nothing in the UI mints one until this lands.

### 2. Where and how the prompt is served

**The pattern to follow is the Passage Runner prompt.**
- `lib/prompts/passage-runner-kickoff.js` reads `docs/passage-runner-prompt.md` **at HEAD**, cuts at the first `---`, and caches the result. A read failure returns an uncached FALLBACK.
- It is served as `text/plain` at `GET /api/proxy/passage-runner/prompt` behind `proxyLimiter` and `authenticateProxyToken` (`routes/proxy-kickoff.js:541-549`).
- The same body feeds a session page. Passage Planner does the same thing (`routes/passage-planner.js:45`).
- Templated builders exist too, for example `buildFlightCompanionKickoff({ baseUrl })` (`routes/flight-companion.js:493`).

**Recommendation: a builder over a doc, not bare static markdown.** The prompt needs values that already have a single source in code:
- `RUNNER_BOOTSTRAP_TTL_SECONDS` and `RUNNER_WORKING_TTL_SECONDS` (`lib/proxy-scopes.js:58-59`, already interpolated this way in `lib/proxy-instructions.js:908-909,964-967`);
- `HALT_MODES` (`lib/workspace-halt.js:28`);
- `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:121`);
- `baseUrl`.

So: `docs/runner-prompt.md` holds the prose (reviewable, like passage-runner), and `lib/prompts/runner-kickoff.js` holds `buildRunnerKickoff({ baseUrl })`, which interpolates those constants. It is exposed on two surfaces:
1. The session page from §1, where the human copies it.
2. `GET /api/proxy/runner/prompt` for re-reading mid-run. Mounted inside the `/api/proxy/runner` sub-router, it inherits `requireGrant('take')` from the path-scoped gate (`routes/proxy-runner.js:76`), so only a runner credential can read it.

**Housekeeping the plan must carry:**
- The prompt-template count and source-map rows are checked against source at test time (CLAUDE.md invariant; `docs/architecture/source-map.md`).
- `lib/proxy-instructions.js`'s Runner Endpoints section (`:887-915`) should point to the new endpoint.

### 3. Take, confirm, refuse

**Endpoints the runner credential uses.** All three are behind `proxyLimiter`, `authenticateProxyToken` and `requireGrant('take')` (`routes/proxy-runner.js:76`; mounted at `routes/proxy.js:1591`):
- **`GET /api/proxy/runner/poll`** returns `{ items, halt?, otherConsumerLastSeenAt }` (`:92-112`). Items are `_formatItem` shapes that include each item's grant-less `bootstrapToken` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:2734`).
  - `otherConsumerLastSeenAt` is dispatch-token-only on purpose. Served instructions say: if it's recent, warn and stop rather than race Simple Dispatcher (`lib/proxy-instructions.js:893-895`).
- **`POST /api/proxy/runner/take/:id`** is an atomic `findOneAndDelete` plus an archive as `taken`, stamping `takenByTokenLabel` and `takenByTokenId` (`routes/proxy-runner.js:119-142`; `lib/dispatch-store.js:907-933`). A 404 means someone else took it.
- **`POST /api/proxy/runner/feedback/:id`** has the same body as `/api/dispatch/feedback` (`validateFeedbackBody`).
  - Ownership is by **`takenByTokenId`** inside the atomic update (`routes/proxy-runner.js:178-185`; `lib/dispatch-store.js:2199-2201`). Only the exact token that took an item can post on it.
  - It provisions wake credentials (`routes/proxy-runner.js:161-168`).
- The runner credential also has `readWrite`, so it can call `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/:id/prompt` and every other proxy read.

**`GET /api/proxy/dispatch/:id/prompt` returns enough to confirm** (`routes/proxy-dispatch.js:1779-1815`). It is workspace-scoped through `req.proxyUrlKey` and returns `{ id, promptName, kind, prompt, issueIdentifier, issueUrl, target, followUpTo, sessionId, dispatchedAt }`. It does **not** return `harness`, `model`, `dispatchedBy`, `subscription` or `bootstrapToken`.

**Proposed definition of a mismatch.** Refuse (post `[failed] refused: <reason>` and don't run) when any of these holds:
1. The confirm returns 404 or a non-200.
2. `prompt` is not byte-equal to the taken item's `prompt`.
3. Any of `id`, `kind`, `followUpTo`, `sessionId`, `issueIdentifier` or `target` differs between the take and the confirm.
4. For a `followUpTo` item, the target is neither an item this runner handed to a subagent nor resolvable.

   This is the fallback policy in §7. Simple Dispatcher itself posts `[failed] No live session to resume …` (`simple-dispatcher/followup.js:22-40`).

**What confirmation does not do.** Both reads hit the same store over the same credential. Confirmation catches a prompt that reached the session some other way, such as pasted, injected or altered in transit (LIN-1128's purpose). It does **not** stop a hostile enqueuer: until LIN-2884 T3 enforces `dispatch`, any `readWrite` proxy holder can enqueue (LIN-3080 Q8; CLAUDE.md "`dispatch` not yet enforced"). See open question Q4.

| wake (`[blocked]`, `[pending]` and terminals) | `WAKE_FEEDBACK_REGEX` `:53`; checked on **each newly appended entry** in `addFeedback` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:2262`) | `/^\s*\[(done\|complete\|failed\|aborted\|blocked\|pending)\]/i`. **`[blocked]` is not terminal**: it wakes a subscribed parent and leaves the item open. |
| blocked / waiting | `BLOCKED_MARKER_REGEX` `lib/render-session.js:163`; `WAITING_WAKE_MARKERS = {'blocked'}` `:177` (mirrored in `routes/dashboard.js` and `lib/pipeline-loops.js` per `:173-176`) | `[blocked] …` renders as **waiting on a human**. `[pending]` does not. |
| `[usage]` | `parseUsage` `lib/session-telemetry.js:490-500` (**`kind === 'usage'` required**, last parseable entry wins); `parseUsagePayload` `:420-477` | `[usage] {json}`. The JSON is parsed from the first `{`. Recognised fields: `harness`, `model`, `effort` (strings, passed through), `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheCreationInputTokens`, `cacheCreation1hInputTokens`, `cacheReadInputTokens` (finite numbers), `lane` (`subscription\|api\|openrouter`, else null), and `costUsd` (a number; otherwise derived). Simple Dispatcher's producer is `hook.js:311,324` (`harness:'claude-code'`). |
| harness in cost | `lib/task-cost.js:147-158` | `harness: usage.harness`: the **realised** harness from the `[usage]` payload, never the item's `harness` field. Same for `model` and `effort`. |
| `[handoff]` | **None.** `grep` over `lib/`, `routes/` and `public/` finds no parser. | Inert today. As a `kind:'status'` line it matches no regex, so it never terminates or wakes anything. LIN-2948's run page would add the reader. |
| `[decision]` (FYI) | `lib/session-telemetry.js:667` | `[decision] {json}`. Not needed by the runner. |

**Cost consequences, for the `[usage]` line:**
- `computeUsageCostUsd` returns **null** when there are no token counts (`lib/model-pricing.js:302-371`, `tokenTotal === 0 → null`). So a `[usage]` carrying only `harness` and `model` is honest ("unpriced"), never a false $0.
- Putting a subagent's *total* tokens into `outputTokens` or `inputTokens` would misprice it, and must not be done.
- `claude-opus-5-5` resolves to `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, which has no row at HEAD (`lib/model-pricing.js:126-129`), so it stays unpriced until LIN-3094 lands.
- The runner **can** get the full split. On this host, Claude Code writes subagent transcripts to `~/.claude/projects/<proj>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, with a per-message `message.model` and `message.usage` (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`). One sample had 35 usage-bearing messages on `claude-opus-5-5`. Summing those would give a priced `[usage]` with the realised model. *This is a Claude Code internal layout, observed locally and not a stable API.*
- Usage is a cumulative snapshot, last-wins per lineage. So for a continued subagent (the orchestrator across wakes), post the subagent's cumulative totals on each item it handles.

**Is there a shared constant? Only partly.**
- `FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:121`) and `HALT_MODES` (`lib/workspace-halt.js:28`) are exported.
- The marker **words** exist only inside regex literals (`dispatch-terminal.js:26,53`; `render-session.js:163,177`; plus the two mirrors). `TERMINAL_FEEDBACK_REGEX` is exposed only through `__internal` (`dispatch-terminal.js:374`).
- So a served prompt either duplicates the words or the builder imports new exported word lists. See engineering choice E4, which pins the copy with a round-trip test. This matches the drift review's warning in comment `55365477`.

### 5. Token handling: (a) runner-owned broker vs (b) no-broker claude-code prompt

**Why the problem exists.** The item prompt is **baked at enqueue**:
- `lib/dispatch-factory.js:687` defaults the harness to `claude-code` (`DEFAULT_DISPATCH_HARNESS`, `lib/proxy-preamble.js:103`).
- That selects `tokenDelivery:'mcp'`, which writes the `$HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE`, no-auth, `X-Harbour-Intent: write` block (`lib/proxy-preamble.js:212,283-292`) and puts the bootstrap only in the structured `bootstrapToken` field.
- Wakes get the same treatment (`lib/wake-credential.js:63-66`; `lib/dispatch-store.js:2399`).
- The block also says "Your runner reports back automatically when this session stops" (`:321`). That is true for a person-run runner only if the runner relays the report.

**(a) The runner ships a small broker** (the spike's `broker.mjs`, about 40 lines, the person-run analogue of `simple-dispatcher/harbour-token-mcp-server.js`).
- For each item, the runner exchanges the item's own `bootstrapToken` into a mode-600 file. A `127.0.0.1` listener forwards only `/api/proxy/*`, injects the bearer and requires `X-Harbour-Intent: write` on write verbs.
- The subagent gets the item prompt **verbatim**, plus an environment preamble that overrides `HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE` to that broker. The spike found an inherited value can point at a different workspace.
- **Tokens:** the subagent never sees or holds one (proven 7/7 locally in LIN-3080), and prompts stay byte-equal to `/prompt`, so confirmation still works.
- **Cost:**
  - Node (or another runtime) on the machine;
  - a port and process per item, or one multiplexing broker;
  - cleanup at the terminal marker;
  - rotating the orchestrator's broker credential to each wake's fresh bootstrap (as the spike did).
- **No Harbour or Simple Dispatcher change.**

**(b) A no-broker variant of the claude-code prompt.**
- The prompt is fixed at enqueue, before anyone knows who will take it, and `pollAvailable` doesn't filter by consumer (`lib/dispatch-store.js:947-949`). So a variant would need one of two things:
  - a new harness or target value to route runner items. That changes the shared `target` vocabulary Simple Dispatcher owns (`simple-dispatcher/targets.js:17-18`) and the enqueue paths, and is out of bounds here.
  - a runner-side prompt rewrite, which breaks byte-equal confirmation.
- A prompt that works without a broker must carry the credential in prose (the `'prose'` branch, `lib/proxy-preamble.js:299-306`). The subagent then holds the working token in its context and transcript. That is exactly what LIN-1155 and LIN-1375 removed, so it **fails "keep tokens away from subagents."**

**Recommendation: (a).** This is an engineering choice: the ticket itself delegates "choose one, record which and why". The broker holds only the item's own grant-less worker credential, which is the same holder class as Simple Dispatcher's broker on its host. No new who-may-mint or who-may-hold rule is created.

One residual needs John's confirmation (Q2): on a *person's* laptop, the broker is an unauthenticated localhost listener that any local process can use.

### 6. Watchdog, halts, laptop close

**Halts.**
- Every runner poll carries `halt: {mode, setAt, setBy}` when one is set (`routes/proxy-runner.js:100-106`). The read is bounded and degrades to the last-known cache (`lib/poll-halt.js:45-56`).
- The standalone read is `GET /api/proxy/dispatch/halt`, read scope (`routes/proxy-halt.js:25,44`; mounted at `routes/proxy.js:1565`). Modes are `HALT_MODES = ['pause','stop']` (`lib/workspace-halt.js:28`).
- **Simple Dispatcher enforces halts** (`simple-dispatcher/README.md:231-245`; `halt.js`). The runner should mirror that meaning:
  - `pause`: take no fresh items. Leave running subagents alone, but still take follow-ups and aborts for live subagents.
  - `stop`: take nothing new, stop every in-flight subagent, and post `[aborted] halted by operator (stop)` on each.
- **Stale docs the runner must not inherit.** "pending LIN-2995" (advisory) wording remains in **13 files**. The ones a runner would actually read are the *served* instructions, `lib/proxy-instructions.js:629,850`. Others include `routes/proxy-halt.js:9,104`, `lib/render-dispatch.js:151`, `public/dispatch.js:774,805` and `routes/dispatch.js:978`. The fix belongs to LIN-3074. The runner prompt must state its own binding rule and not defer to `/instructions` on halt semantics.

**Watchdog: the runner owns it all; Harbour has no reaper.** "Stalled" today comes from Simple Dispatcher's reapers (`[failed] … wedged …`; LIN-3080 finding 11). Harbour has no stale-taken detector.
- **Subagent stall.** After N minutes without the subagent returning, post `[blocked] stalled: subagent <id> silent for <n> min`, as the ticket asks. Per §4 it is **non-terminal**, it **wakes a subscribed parent**, and it **renders as "waiting on a human"**. Simple Dispatcher uses `[failed] … wedged` for a true wedge. Keep `[blocked] stalled` as a first signal and escalate to `[failed] stalled …` after a second threshold.
- **Poll-loop death.** The spike's background poll died unnoticed. The runner should poll in-turn, or check a heartbeat-file age on every turn. It can also post `kind:'heartbeat'` feedback on in-flight items (`FEEDBACK_ENTRY_KINDS`).

**What honestly happens if the laptop sleeps or closes.** There is **no lease**:
- `take` deletes the queue row and archives it as `taken` (`lib/dispatch-store.js:926-931`).
- Queued items expire after 24h (`:247`, `cleanup` `:957-990`).
- History lasts 30 days (`:248`).

So:
- **Sleep, then resume within 24h:** the process was only suspended. Subagents continue, though some tool calls may have timed out. Items may look silent meanwhile.
- **Session killed, or away more than 24h:**
  - In-flight items stay `taken` with no terminal indefinitely; nothing re-dispatches them.
  - A subscribed Autopilot parent never gets its wake, so the run hangs.
  - The 24h working token expires and polls return 401. Re-copying mints a **new lineage with a new `tokenId`**, and feedback ownership is by `takenByTokenId`, so **the new runner cannot post a terminal on its predecessor's items.** I found no other path at HEAD by which a different credential closes them (the plan should verify), so they are closed by hand. See Q1.
  - Queued items wait and expire at 24h.
- A cloud Claude Code session (claude.ai/code, the natural "from my phone" runner) has no laptop to close, but its container is reclaimed when idle. The same no-lease consequences apply.

### 7. followUpTo and subscription

**followUpTo → continue the same subagent.**
- The runner keeps a map from every item id it handed to a subagent (the root and each follow-up) to that subagent's id. Simple Dispatcher matches the same way, on `rootItemId` **or** the current `itemMetadata.itemId` (`simple-dispatcher/followup.js:22-32`).
- On a `followUpTo` hit, continue that subagent with the new item's prompt verbatim, and rotate its broker credential to the new item's `bootstrapToken`.
- On a miss (runner restarted, subagent gone), either post `[failed] no live subagent to resume` (Simple Dispatcher parity) or start a fresh subagent seeded with the parent's recap (the spike). Both are engineering choices; record which in the `[handoff]` line.
- Proven 3 of 3 in LIN-3080.
- `force` on a follow-up only overrides Simple Dispatcher's liveness guard, so the runner can ignore it.

**subscription: the runner needs no handling of its own.**
- The edge (`sessionId` plus `subscription`, default `terminal-only`, `lib/dispatch-store.js:37,474`) is set by the **enqueuer**, the orchestrator subagent.
- Harbour auto-enqueues the parent's `kind:'wake'` follow-up **server-side** when a wake marker lands on the child (`lib/dispatch-store.js:2217-2262`, resolved through `_resolveEdgeDoc`), and gives it a fresh bootstrap (`:2399`).
- So the runner must:
  1. post each child's markers verbatim, on the child's own item id, through the credential that took it;
  2. take the wake (`followUpTo` = the kickoff id; see LIN-3080 run 2) and continue the orchestrator subagent.
- The kickoff's `waitForFollowUps` "park" becomes "the subagent ends its turn and the runner resumes it on the wake."

### Open security-boundary questions for John

- **Q1. Orphaned items after the runner credential expires or is replaced.** Only the token that took an item may post on it (`takenByTokenId`). A re-copied runner, which is a new lineage, cannot close items its 24h-expired, revoked or killed predecessor took, so they stay `taken`. Options:
  - accept that and close by hand (no code; I recommend this for v1, with honest copy);
  - let a successor runner credential **of the same owner** post terminals on its predecessor's items. That is a new who-may-use rule.
- **Q2. The local broker on a person's machine.** Option (a) runs an unauthenticated `127.0.0.1` listener that injects the item's worker credential for any local process. This is the same shape Simple Dispatcher runs on its host, but it would now run on arbitrary owners' laptops. Is that acceptable?
  - I recommend yes, with a Host-header check, a per-item random port and teardown at the terminal marker.
  - If not, the alternative is subagents reading the token from a mode-600 file themselves, which means they hold it.
- **Q3. Items with no API access.** A "run this step" dispatch sent with the +proxy toggle off has no `bootstrapToken` and no access block (`public/common.js:704-727`). Should the runner ever give such a subagent a credential derived from **its own** (take+dispatch) token? I recommend **no**: run it without API access as Simple Dispatcher would, or have the runner flow force `attachProxy` on its rung (that part is UI and engineering). Allowing it would be a new who-may-use rule.
- **Q4. Enqueue trust before LIN-2884 T3.** Until `dispatch` is enforced, any `readWrite` proxy holder in the workspace can queue work that the runner executes on the owner's machine, and confirmation doesn't stop it. Options:
  - ship the UI mint and prompt before T3 (my recommendation, with this stated in the copy);
  - additionally have the runner refuse items whose `dispatchedBy` isn't the runner's owner. That is cheap, but it is a runner-side who-may-enqueue policy, and the server-enqueued wakes' `dispatchedBy` would need checking in the plan.
