### Findings

**B1 (blocking, security): the runner's own refusal delivers attacker-controlled text into the owner's orchestrator.** The plan's R1 mitigation says "the runner itself refuses such children, and its refusal text is runner-authored". At HEAD the refusal is what *causes* the injection:
- Pre-T3, any `readWrite` holder can enqueue an item with `sessionId` set to the owner's kickoff id. `validateSessionId` does no ownership check (`lib/dispatch-validation.js:114-129`), and `issueTitle`, `promptName` and `issueUrl` are taken from the client body (`routes/proxy-dispatch.js:575-590`).
- The runner takes the item, `attributeItem` refuses it, and the runner posts `[failed] refused: …`. `[failed]` is a wake marker (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:53`), and "terminals always bubble".
- With no `followUpTo`, `_resolveEdgeDoc` returns the child itself (`lib/dispatch-store.js:1978-1990`). `buildWakeFollowUp(edgeDoc, …)` (`:2311`) then mints a wake to the owner's kickoff whose prompt copies the child's `issueTitle`, `promptName` and `issueUrl` (`formatWakePrompt`, `lib/dispatch-wake.js:76-90`).
- That wake has `dispatchedBy == null`, and its root is the owner's, so `attributeItem` passes it. The owner's orchestrator subagent then reads the attacker's text on the owner's machine. No other consumer is needed.

*Fix, which the plan author can make:*
- Run `attribute` on the **poll** result, before `take`. `dispatchedBy` is already on poll items, and a wake's root can be read before taking. **N1 (non-blocking): the `wait` reasons in §2 (`docs/runner-prompt.md:80-85`) don't match what `waitLoop` returns.**

- `credential` is returned for *any* thrown poll (`:961`). That includes a plain network failure, such as waking from sleep with no Wi-Fi, not only the 401 message. The prompt maps `credential` to "expired or revoked: tell the person", and §8 then ends the runner. After a network blip this is a spurious stop, which contradicts §7's "wait re-arms when you wake".
- *Fix (copy only):* `error` means re-arm. For `credential`, read `message`: only the "rejected (expired or revoked)" text means the credential died; anything else means re-arm.

- *Fix:* the fallback runs `runner wait` in the foreground on each `/loop` tick. It returns by `WAIT_CAP_MIN` at the latest, and it keeps both the heartbeat and the watchdog.

issue.title: Re-evaluate Jev for step one of the meta prompt (choosing the task type), set up per its guides
issue.description:
**Filed by the Flight Companion on John's go, 2026-09-26.** Follow-up to LIN-3097. This is a research and evaluation task only: no production change.

## The question, in John's words

The AI meta prompt does two things. First it **chooses a type of task** (which template comes next). Then it **creates that task**, combining the template with the task information. The question is whether Jev can do the **first step** only. If it can, the functionality can usefully be separated, and Harbour can make use of Jev's high speed and low cost. The second step stays with the current model.

## Why LIN-3097's "no-go" does not settle it

LIN-3097 asked the right question, but it did not give Jev a fair setup:

* **The result was effectively a tie.** Jev scored 12/21 and the incumbent scored 13/21: one answer apart, on 7 fixtures.
* **The decision rule was harsh.** Jev also had to get LIN-510 and LIN-813 right, and the incumbent got both wrong in 3 of 3 runs.
* **The wording was not written for Jev.** The `choice` instructions and criteria were reused as they were: each template's `aiHint.situation`, written for the incumbent's prompt. `docs/papers/harbour/jev-decision-model.md` (Limits) says the wording "was written once and not iterated, and TypeSafe's docs say the wording moves the answer, so Jev's numbers are a floor". The LIN-3097 re-test capped tuning at one small change and changed only `defer`.
* **The state was the raw ticket.** It included the full description and every comment in order, and the instruction told the model to treat the latest comment as the current state. That is an indirect, multi-hop read over distracting context. Published guidance on Jev names exactly those as its weak spots, and recommends giving it relevant state and asking a direct typed question.

## What this task should do

1. **Read TypeSafe's own guidance on Jev before designing anything**, plus the practical guides that have been published. Record which practices you adopt and which you drop, and why. Starting points:
   * TypeSafe's introduction and API docs, as cited in the paper.
   * [https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/09/23/a-coding-guide-to-typesafe-ai-jev/amp/](<https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/09/23/a-coding-guide-to-typesafe-ai-jev/amp/>)
   * [https://dev.to/valyuai/how-to-use-jev-a-practical-guide-to-typesafes-system-one-model-g5e](<https://dev.to/valyuai/how-to-use-jev-a-practical-guide-to-typesafes-system-one-model-g5e>)
   * [https://huggingface.co/blog/sora-2/jev-ai-typesafe-ai-a-practical-guide-to-typed-deci](<https://huggingface.co/blog/sora-2/jev-ai-typesafe-ai-a-practical-guide-to-typed-deci>)
   * [https://www.datacamp.com/blog/system-one-models-jev](<https://www.datacamp.com/blog/system-one-models-jev>)
2. **Design the routing call for Jev.**
   * Write the question and the per-action criteria as Jev wants them: direct, mutually distinguishable situations.
   * Give it a distilled current state rather than the raw thread. One option is the kind of summary Harbour's brief already produces; this task decides what state is fair to give it.
   * Keep the vocabulary honest to the live recommender, including the leaf and node `defer` rule.
3. **Widen the evidence beyond 7 fixtures.** Seven fixtures give a direction, not a rate. If more labelled routing cases can be built from the tracker's history, build them. Say how they were labelled and by whom.
4. **Run Jev and the incumbent over the same set.** Report:
   * hit rates, with intervals;
   * latency;
   * cost per call;
   * calibration.

   Calibration means: can a confidence threshold hand the uncertain cases back to the incumbent, and at what hand-back rate and what combined accuracy?
5. **Record a go/no-go against this rule.** Jev is viable for step one if it is **statistically indistinguishable from or better than** the incumbent on the widened set, **or** if a confidence-threshold hand-off reaches incumbent-level accuracy while Jev handles most calls alone. A tie counts as a pass, because a tie at Jev's speed and cost is the whole case for the split.

## Out of scope

* Any production change to `lib/openrouter.js`, the dispatch path or the meta prompt.
* Building the router/writer split. If the result is a go, that becomes a separate follow-up decision for John.
* Editing the frozen fixtures under `scripts/eval/fixtures/`, or rewriting the existing paper's findings.

## Done when

* The evaluation has run, and its method, data and scripts have landed under `scripts/eval/`, alongside the existing Jev spike.
* A go/no-go conclusion is posted on this ticket, with the evidence behind it.
* If it is a go, the ticket says what the split would need, without building it.

## Close-out stub (LIN-3107)

**Landed:** the standalone Jev step-one routing evaluation harness under `scripts/eval/` — research-only, with no production routing, dispatch, meta-prompt or frozen-fixture change — in **PR #1598**, merged as `a1564830`.

**Outcome: NO-GO.** Jev is not viable for step one of the meta prompt under the evaluated design: it did not beat or match the incumbent on the widened 66-fixture set, and no confidence-threshold hand-off reached incumbent-level accuracy while Jev handled most calls alone. No production router/writer split was built.

**Committed session-fit:** the plan-review gate fired on criterion (a) — session-fit "Needs multiple sessions".

The full research, plan and implementation history remains in this task's snapshots (`GET /issues/LIN-3107/snapshots`) and in its comments.

comments.body:
## Research + evaluation design (LIN-3107) — Jev for step one, set up per its guides

Re-grounded at `LinearViewer` HEAD `b5c528c4` (merge of PR #1589). Staleness check: `git log --since="2026-09-26T19:36:19.996Z" -- scripts/eval scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs lib/openrouter.js lib/prompt-templates.js lib/prompts/meta-prompt-template.js docs/papers/harbour/jev-decision-model.md` returns nothing — the code the ticket references is unchanged. Working tree clean.

### 1. What "step one" actually is (the routing question we're re-testing)

The meta-AI step is **one** `chat/completions` call to `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` (`lib/openrouter.js:947` `getRecommendationStream`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` at `:26`) that returns a markdown completion whose `## Reasoning` carries the routing decision (`→ **action**`, parsed `parseRecommendedAction` `:1675`) and whose `## Prompt` carries the full body — both from the same generation. "Step one" = the `→ **action**` line, graded against the 17-action vocabulary `deriveDispatchKind` resolves (`lib/prompt-templates.js:228/457`). Jev cannot emit the `## Prompt` half (it is a `text->decisions` model); the re-test is whether it can own **the routing half** alone. The router/writer split stays out of scope.

### 2. Sources consulted (Jev guidance)

- TypeSafe: intro blog (2026-09-15), API reference (`POST /api/…/v1/systemone`), `concepts/state`, `confidence`, `how-to-build-with-system-one`, `primitives`/`choice`, and `model-jaggedness/jev-1.13`.
- Practical guides from the ticket: MarkTechPost coding guide; dev.to (Valyu) "How to Use Jev"; HF community guide (`sora-2`); DataCamp "System One Models". Note the HF guide is community-written and pointedly docs an *independently-operated* "Jev AI" site — content overlaps TypeSafe's, treated as corroborating, not authoritative.

### 3. Adopted / dropped Jev practices (recorded per the ticket)

**Adopted** (with reason):
1. **Literal, direct instruction; write the exact condition.** Jaggedness #1. LIN-3097's "read all comments, treat the latest as current state" was an indirect multi-hop read — the named anti-pattern.
2. **Distilled, field-named, filtered state.** Jaggedness #5 / state page: raw thread was "large state full of irrelevant detail" (context rot). Adopt a compact named-field schema; keep arithmetic/counting/dates in **code** (jaggedness #2/#3 — the state builder computes comment/subtask counts, "how many Request-Changes", divergence, not Jev).
3. **Contrastive, mutually-distinguishable criteria, aligned with the instruction.** Jaggedness #7 / choice "structured criteria" (`what`/`not_for`). LIN-3097 reused the incumbent's one-line `aiHint.situation`; this is the core fix — derive Jev criteria from the live `aiHint.situation + whenNot + chooseOver`.
4. **Confidence-gated hand-off; thresholds set from a labelled set, per-action.** Confidence page / route-on-uncertainty. Adopted as the calibration measurement.
5. **Speculative fan-out** (ask independent questions in one request — operator decision rides free, already in `jev-spike.mjs`).
6. **Pin the model version + log `model`, probabilities, confidence** for reproducibility.

**Dropped** (with reason):
1. **"Add an `other`/catch-all option."** *Rejected deliberately:* the live recommender vocabulary is a fixed dispatch contract with **no** catch-all — seeding one would diverge Jev's answer space from `deriveDispatchKind` and production can't act on it. Uncertainty must be expressed through **confidence**, not a new action.
2. **"Keep counting/arithmetic in code"** — not a model practice; applied to the state builder instead (moved-to-code, listed under adopted #2).
3. **Score primitive / composite-scoring / cascade patterns** — not applicable to a single pick-one route.
4. **TypeSafe SDK** — the repo's existing lane is OpenRouter's alpha `decisions` endpoint (`jev-spike.mjs` already calls it); a research script needs no SDK dependency.

### 4. Bounded classes (enumerated)

- **Task-type vocabulary (17).** `getAIRecommendationActionNames()` = `blocked, bug, plan, look into, triage, breakdown, research, scoping, design, spike, context, plan-review, implement, review, close-out, retrospective-audit, defer` (reproduced via `node -e` against `lib/prompt-templates.js:457`). `defer` is the only one without `aiHint` (`RECOMMEND_META_ACTIONS` `:170`) — must be hand-described in Jev criteria.
- **defer rule.** Leaf → never offered (Step 4 only when `hasSubtasks`, `meta-prompt-template.js:229`); node → `defer` only with `DeferTo` to a **real, non-terminal child** (`recommend-recurse.js:165-186`; `parseDeferTo` `openrouter.js:1694`). Consistency obligation: Jev's offered set must track this/leaf distinction or any hit-rate move is a vocabulary artifact (the LIN-571 case).
- **Eval scripts + fixtures.** `scripts/eval/fixtures/*.json` = 7 frozen real cases (HAR-697, LIN-420, LIN-510, LIN-537, LIN-571, LIN-748, LIN-813; `expect`/`avoid` sidecars enumerated). `scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs` adds 24 synthetic `CASES[]`. `jev-spike.mjs` = Jev arm. `fixtures/recommend/` subdir is out of population (harness reads top-level `*.json`). Frozen → read-only.
- **Candidate state representations.** (a) raw fixture JSON (`jev-spike` `fixtureState`); (b) live meta-prompt `formatIssueContext` (`openrouter.js:633`); (c) Harbour brief distilled summary (`/brief`, `lib/brief.js`). This task must settle on a distilled schema; none of the three is itself the Jev-fair state.
- **Model result records.** `jev-spike-out/results.json` (choice/probabilities/confidence/usage/latency). Incumbent arm has **no** results file and **no** usage/latency plumbing (`eval-research-routing.mjs` `call()` — established in LIN-3097 review); must be added, not assumed.

### 5. Measurement — validate before optimize

- **Labels.** `expect`/`avoid` sidecars were frozen by a human at the "known failure moment" (`build-routing-fixtures.mjs`/`build-har697-red.mjs`). They encode the *intended* next action, not what the live recommender actually emitted. Some are **sets** (LIN-510 `expect=[implement,blocked,plan,bug]`, LIN-571 `expect=[breakdown,implementation,implement]`) — "hit" = ∈ set. This genuinely tracks the intended outcome, **but** a set-label can record a "hit" while masking a sub-acceptable choice → report per-fixture **distributions**, not only hit counts.
- **Hit rate + intervals.** Binomial; 7×K gives direction not a rate (the ticket's point). Widening gives a rate → report Wilson/Clopper-Pearson intervals.
- **Latency.** Jev measured (`performance.now` around fetch, median 148–411 ms). Incumbent latency is **LIN-263's figure (4–5 s), not measured in-harness** → add per-call timing to the incumbent arm.
- **Cost.** Jev measured from `usage.cost` (spike tallies). Incumbent has **no** cost plumbing → do NOT report incumbent cost from Jev `results.totals`; capture the arm's own usage (or read OpenRouter activity).
- **Confidence/calibration.** Jev `confidence = (n·peak − 1)/(n − 1)` — a distribution statistic, **not** probability-of-correctness. Prior result: wrong answers 0.24–0.84, right 0.23–0.94 → **no** separating threshold on 7 cases. The gate must be *tested*, never trusted. On widened set: sweep thresholds, report hand-back rate + combined accuracy = (Jev-correct + incumbent-correct-on-handback)/N.
- **Two measures that can look favourable while hiding a wrong route (explicitly qualified):**
  1. **Vocabulary asymmetry in grading.** Jev arm normalizes `implementation → implement` (`jev-spike.mjs:62`); the incumbent harness does **not**, so LIN-510's `implementation`×2 grade as off-vocabulary misses (≈2/21, LIN-3097 review F1). Report both arms **normalized the same way**, else the incumbent is systematically under-scored.
  2. **Narrowing Jev's offered set** (withholding `defer` on leaves) can flip a miss→hit as a pure vocabulary artifact (LIN-571 `defer`→`breakdown`). Any hit-rate gain must be attributed, not just counted.

### 6. Recommended evaluation design (for the next `plan`)

1. **Direct routing question** — one `choice` over the live 17 actions (16 on leaves, 17 on nodes), criteria rewritten for Jev from the live `aiHint.situation + whenNot + chooseOver` per action (`defer` described by hand, faithfully to the leaf/node rule). Instruction is literal and references named state fields by backtick path.
2. **Distilled current-state** (new, code-built): `{ identifier, title, state{name,type}, labels, isTerminal, hasSubtasks, nodeFacts{ …counts, frontierNextChild, sessionFit }, trailSummary (per-comment digest + code-computed divergence/convergence marker), descriptionDigest }`. Counts/dates/divergence computed in code. Fairness control: feed the **same** distilled state to the incumbent arm, and keep a raw-state incumbent arm to quantify whether distillation itself drops information.
3. **Widen the labelled set from tracker history** — candidate sources with recorded ground truth: LIN-812 (close-out/review evals), LIN-555/LIN-587 (suite + real fixtures), LIN-586 (divergence), LIN-830 (breakdown under-fire), LIN-878 (richer kinds), LIN-596 (re-freeze), and known routing mis-fires LIN-3075 / LIN-1093 / LIN-838 / LIN-1702. Method: freeze each real issue at its recorded "red moment" via the existing `build-*.mjs` recipe; set `expect`/`avoid` **from the ticket's own history** (the comment/verdict that records the correct next step), not from the model. Labeller = the researcher (John/agent), citing the exact comment that establishes gold; issues without an unambiguous recorded outcome are **excluded and listed** (cannot be reliably labelled).
4. **Same set for both arms**, K≥3, report intervals; per-call timing + usage captured on the incumbent arm; vocabulary normalization applied both ways.
5. **Calibration/hand-off sweep** over Jev confidence; report hand-back rate and combined accuracy at multiple thresholds.
6. **Decision rule:** go if Jev is statistically indistinguishable-from-or-better, **or** a threshold hand-off reaches incumbent-level accuracy while Jev handles most calls alone — **tie counts as pass** (speed/cost is the whole case). If go: price the router/writer split as a *separate* follow-up, not here.

### 7. Adversarial self-review (layer set claimed complete)

Searches that would have surfaced missed siblings (all run; results recorded):
- `grep -rn "getRecommendation|getRecommendationStream|buildMetaPrompt" lib routes server.js` → template-selection call sites (proxy/workspace-api/fused dispatch); no production `decisions` lane (`grep -rn "api/alpha|/decisions" lib routes` → only an unrelated `collective-preset-defs.js` prose hit).
- `grep -rln "jev|decisions" lib routes scripts` → the only "jev" hit is `scripts/eval/jev-spike.mjs`; `task-decisions-store.js`/`unanswered-decisions.js` are unrelated ("decisions" ≠ Jev). No prior distilled-state Jev router exists (`phase4-distillation-probe.mjs` is an INF-1 prompt-inflation probe, not Jev).
- `docs/papers/harbour/` + `scripts/eval/*.md` → prior diverging-routing evidence (`har-697-divergence-findings.md`, `lin-263-findings.md`) reconciled; no alternate task-state representation beyond the four in §4.
- Tracker `search` (`meta prompt`, `recommender routing`, `prompt experiment`, `Jev`) → the widening sources in §6 (LIN-812/555/586/587/830/878/596/3075/1093/838/1702); no prior routing eval that already runs the distilled-state + Jev design. Residual open classification: whether enough tracker cases carry an unambiguous recorded gold is the *content* of the next phase's labelling, not resolvable here — stated honestly rather than implied covered.

```
Surface Assessment: lands cleanly
```
The evaluation is a standalone research artifact: it writes/extended `scripts/eval/` state, reads (never edits) the 17-action vocabulary and the `defer` leaf/node rule, and touches no production routing, dispatch, meta-prompt, fixture, or paper. No production seam change is required — nothing to refactor.

Recommended next action: **`plan`**.

## Plan (LIN-3107) — execution plan posted to the description

Re-grounded at `LinearViewer` HEAD `b5c528c4` (unchanged; staleness check clean). Turned the grounded evaluation design into an executable plan — no prior plan-review verdict existed to revise against.

**Design:** three new standalone scripts under `scripts/eval/` (`jev-routing-criteria.mjs`, `jev-routing-state.mjs`, `jev-routing-eval.mjs`) plus a widened frozen fixture set under a new `scripts/eval/fixtures-widened/` directory (the existing `scripts/eval/fixtures/` stays untouched). Three comparison arms on the same fixture set: Jev+distilled-state (the candidate), incumbent+distilled-state (attribution control — isolates model vs. representation), incumbent+raw-state via the live meta-prompt snapshot (the actual production incumbent and the distillation-loss control). One addition to the prior research findings: `lib/recommendation-facts.js` (LIN-434) already exports the exact deterministic, unit-tested fact-assembly seam (`computeFrontierFacts`, `extractSessionFit`, etc.) the distilled-state builder should reuse rather than reimplement.

**Preserved:** research-only scope, no production/dispatch/meta-prompt change, frozen fixtures untouched, no router/writer split build, live 17-action vocabulary + leaf/node `defer` rule mirrored via the same helpers `recommend-recurse.js` uses (not re-derived from prose), `implementation`/`implement` normalization applied identically to every arm, confidence treated as a tested gate.

**Strategy framing:** full 3-arm + widened-set design recommended over reusing only the original 7 fixtures (would repeat LIN-3097's own diagnosed "direction not a rate" problem) or dropping the attribution arm (loses required win-attribution). No cheaper path routes around a tracked contract gap — `none identified`.

**Scope assessment:** needs multiple sessions — labelling ~11 tracker-history candidates, building the harness, running the 3-arm evaluation with new incumbent latency/cost instrumentation, and the calibration sweep + go/no-go write-up are each independently landable phases.

**Plan-review gate:** `plan-review due: yes` — criterion (a) fires (session-fit = needs multiple sessions). (b)/(c)/(d) do not fire: no routed-around gap, nothing relaxes a validation/contract/guard, and the plan reads (never writes) the dispatch-contract vocabulary/`defer` rule.

**Next action: `plan-review`.**

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict: Request Changes** — the design is sound and research-only. But the widened-set class misses a committed corpus that is already labelled. The primary comparator (arm 3) is a leaf-only, no-comment snapshot, not the live incumbent. And the `defer` offer rule is looser for Jev than for the incumbent, which tilts the comparison toward Jev.

Checked against `LinearViewer` HEAD `b5c528c4`. Staleness: `git log --since="2026-09-26T19:36:19.996Z"` over every referenced path is empty, and the tree is clean. `scripts/eval/meta-prompt.baseline.txt` regenerated from the live template is byte-identical to the committed file.

#### Findings to address

1. **Completeness: the widening class leaves out committed labelled corpora.** §6 bounds "labelled routing cases" to the 7 frozen fixtures plus Linear candidates, but the repo already holds two more members of that class:
   * `scripts/eval/fixtures/recommend/*.json`: 8 files, **30 gold-labelled targets**, each a full context bundle (`issue, parent, siblings, project, children, comments, focusedChild`). It is consumed by `scripts/eval-recommend-baseline.mjs`.
   * **24 inline cases** in `scripts/eval-research-routing.mjs`, including SYN-21 and SYN-22, which §9 itself cites.

   Several §6 candidates already have committed gold there: LIN-596 (`linearviewer.json` `LIN-596@implement`), LIN-830 (`breakdown-fork.json` FIX-830-pos/neg), LIN-812/823 (`closeout-review.json`), and LIN-555/587/878 (eval-research-routing cases). Reading these files doesn't break the no-edit rule for `scripts/eval/fixtures/`. The plan should enumerate this class first, include or exclude each case with a reason, and re-label from Linear only where no committed gold exists.
2. **Source of truth: arm 3 isn't the incumbent in "the strict production sense" (§5).** `meta-prompt.baseline.txt` is rendered with `hasSubtasks:false, hasComments:false` (`scripts/eval/regen-baseline.mjs:9-11,19-24`). The README says "cases must likewise have no children/comments to stay faithful". So it has no Step 4, no subtask-count NOTE, and no comment-count line, while §5 claims "today's full Step 1-4 heuristics". The primary source is directly available: `getRecommendation` → `buildMetaPrompt` over a context bundle, which is exactly what `scripts/eval-recommend-baseline.mjs` already runs, with gpt-5.4-mini as its default. The plan should either drive arm 3 through the live builder, or limit arm 3 to leaf fixtures and say so.
3. **Relaxation: the `defer` offer rule is stated as live but isn't, and it favours Jev.** §4 says withholding `defer` on leaves "matches `meta-prompt-template.js:229`". But the live vocabulary line lists `defer` on **every** call, leaves included (`lib/openrouter.js:818` → baseline line 332). Line 229 gates only Step 4's description. On nodes, live Step 4 appears whenever `hasSubtasks`, including all-terminal nodes, where it tells the model not to defer. `recommend-recurse.js:165-186` corrects a bad defer only after the fact. Arms 1 and 2 therefore choose from a strictly smaller vocabulary than arm 3, the comparator the decision rule is scored against, so one trap the incumbent faces is removed for Jev. The plan should:
   * describe the rule as an eval choice rather than the live contract;
   * grade arm 3's `defer` choices under the same rule (for example, count a leaf `defer` as a miss for every arm);
   * extend the §9 defer-withholding delta to leaves and arm 3, not just node fixtures.
4. **The node and `defer` machinery has no input.** The widened fixtures reuse the "graded-leaf shape" (`build-routing-fixtures.mjs:12-14`: comments trimmed, state forced to `started`, no `children`), and all 7 frozen fixtures have 0 children. That leaves the following with nothing to run on:
   * `nodeFacts` and `frontierChild`;
   * the node branch of the §4 `defer` rule;
   * the §9 node-fixture `defer` delta.

   The plan should add `children`, with their states at the red moment, to the widened shape, or adopt the context-bundle shape in finding 1. That shape already carries `children` and `focusedChild`, and 4 of its bundles are node-shaped.
5. **Reuse: the state builder re-implements an exported, tested helper.** §2 says `subtaskCount/completedCount/inProgressCount/remainingCount` "are NOT exported anywhere" and plans to recompute them. That's incorrect. `computeNodeStateCounts` and `assembleNodeFacts` are exported from `lib/recommendation-facts.js` (LIN-434, `c2cb16e4`) and unit-tested (`tests/unit/recommendation-facts.test.js:10-11,54`). `buildMetaPrompt` consumes `assembleNodeFacts` (`lib/openrouter.js:14,796-803`). Following the plan's own reuse principle, `jev-routing-state.mjs` should import `assembleNodeFacts` so its counts can't drift from the live meta-prompt.

#### Advisory (not blocking)
* **Gold vs. the live contract.** Several candidates predate routing changes: the plan-review gate (LIN-1603, 2026-07-26) and approved-plan breakdown children → implement (LIN-3049, 2026-09-25). A historical outcome should be checked against today's routing contract before it's used as gold.
* **Low power.** With about 25 paired fixtures, McNemar has little power, so an "indistinguishable" result is weak evidence. Report the interval of the paired difference next to the pass, so a tie is interpretable. This doesn't change the ticket's tie = pass rule.

#### Checks that held
* **Strategy framing:** §1 names the routed-around gap as `none identified`, and it closes the missing incumbent latency/usage plumbing inside the harness instead of routing around it.
* **History:** the commit summaries in §11 match `git log`. The recent meta-prompt churn (LIN-3056, 3038, 3049, 3033) doesn't touch the vocabulary or the `defer` text, and the recurse guard is unchanged since LIN-353/365.
* **Session fit:** "needs multiple sessions" holds up. Labelling, building 5 scripts, a costed 3-arm × K≥3 run, and the report are each separately landable.
* **Prerequisite refactor:** none is smuggled in, and no production surface is edited.
* **Other claims confirmed:**
  * the 17-action vocabulary via `getAIRecommendationActionNames()`, with `whenNot`/`chooseOver` on scoping, design, spike and retrospective-audit only;
  * `formatIssueContext` is exported and used by `lib/brief.js` and `lib/recap.js`;
  * the incumbent is `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, the `DEFAULT_MODEL`;
  * the anchor-resolver test denylists `scripts/eval`.

issue.title: Atomic read cutover: bindings become {connectionId, scope} and owner credentials are re-keyed on the connection
issue.description:
Sub-issue of **LIN-2149** (Account → Connection → Workspace), from its breakdown on 2026-09-27. This is a plain acceptance-criteria ticket: LIN-2149 carries no recorded `### Plan Review Verdict`, so no session fit or plan-review clearance is inherited. Line references are grounded at `7a43ef25` (LIN-2149's research SHA) and were confirmed unchanged on these paths at `2c00dee3`. **v1 slice = fresh-account path** (John's 2026-09-19 ruling): legacy operator-workspace migration (LIN-2150, LIN-1981) is out of scope, and so is **LIN-2819**.

## Bounded outcome

For every **connection-backed** workspace:

* credentials are read from the Connection
* the binding carries `{provider, connectionId, scope}` and **no** `credentials`
* the durable owner-credential record, the refresh single-flight and the invariant sweep are keyed on the connection, so **rotation and repair happen once per connection**.

This lands as **one atomic change with no user-visible difference** (LIN-1524's discipline).

## Scoping of "atomic" under the fresh-account v1 (ruled 2026-09-27)

The cutover is atomic **for connection-backed workspaces**. Legacy, connection-less operator bindings and 3-part owner-credential records keep today's read path, unchanged, until **LIN-2150** migrates them. This follows directly from John's 2026-09-19 fresh-account ruling. LIN-2149's DoD line "a workspace binding carries no credential of its own" therefore holds **for the v1 slice**, not across legacy records.

## In scope

* **Binding conversion**, with the converted shape written through the dual-write seams from the Connection store (LIN-3127).
* **Scalar-mirror credential consumers** (15 exact reads) resolve via the Connection:
  * `lib/workspace-token-resolver.js` 59/149/151/250/400/455/580
  * `lib/workspace.js` 395/481/649
  * `lib/token-refresh.js` 131
  * `lib/workspace-api.js` 401/3400
  * `server.js` 3122
  * `lib/diagnostics.js` 89
* The 38 `accessToken === 'test-token'` guards must keep working (not rewritten here).
* **Token selection and refresh re-keyed:**
  * `selectOwnerWorkspaceToken:113`
  * `selectExpiredOwnerRow:235`
  * `selectOwnerSessionRow:306`
  * `selectAllOwnerSessionRows:349`
  * `refreshOwnerCredential:287`: the single-flight key moves from `accountId::urlKey::provider` to the connection
  * `doOwnerRefresh:330`: keep spend-intent, CAS `putIfRefreshToken` and re-read-on-`invalid_grant`
  * `remintActiveCredential:478`
* `lib/owner-credential-store.js:89`: new records are keyed on the connection, not `${accountId}::${urlKey}::${provider}`.
* The `lib/credential-*` modules are re-keyed, including `lib/credential-invariant-sweep.js:135/157/162` (joins on the connection).
* `lib/suspect-credential-refresh.js:99-102`: adopt-before-exchange (`store.get(ownerAccountId, urlKey, provider)`) is re-keyed.
* **Decide and record the fate of the** `sessionsCollection` **copy** (`server.js:246`, a third serialized credential copy). At minimum, no connection-backed read may be served from it.

## Out of scope

* Migrating legacy/operator records (LIN-2150, LIN-1981).
* New UI or flow (the add-from-held-connection flow (LIN-3125)).
* **Multi-binding reads** on single-provider surfaces (LIN-3126, blocked by this ticket).
* LIN-2819.
* Absorbing the credential-defect cluster (LIN-2639, LIN-2642, LIN-2640, LIN-2530, LIN-2394). Cited only.

## Constraints

* Don't add a 5th upward `lib/providers/*/index → routes/*-auth` import edge. Today there are 4: `linear/index:34`, `github/index:67`, `jira/index:103`, `github-projects/index:60` (LIN-675).
* Don't add any new hand-rolled `w => w.urlKey === urlKey` lookup (LIN-2389).
* Reuse the existing GitHub App installation, permissions and callback URLs. No new owner-only App setting.
* Atomic and user-invisible.
* Don't make **LIN-2640** (owner-session rows not filtered by provider) worse; the `selectOwnerSessionRow` re-key touches exactly that surface.
* **Named regression risk: LIN-3105 R13 / LIN-2473.** LIN-2473 documented provider-lane 503/401 `LINEAR_AUTH` flapping on the `flow-account-connection-workspace-credential` surface. Its fix, adopt-before-exchange, reads the durable record by the very urlKey key this ticket re-keys. Its B1 defect was the durable record's `scope` leaking into `routes/proxy.js:733/744`'s `scope ?? token` credential substitution. The new record shape (`connectionId`, `scope`) must **not** reach that substitution.

## Acceptance witness (fails before, passes after)

Seed a fresh account with **one GitHub connection and two workspaces bound to it** (`repoA`, `repoB`). Expire the connection's credential and resolve both workspaces concurrently. Assert:

1. **exactly one** `mintInstallationToken` / refresh, single-flighted on the connection
2. both workspaces' `getWorkspaceCallScope` return the new token
3. exactly **1** durable owner-credential record, keyed on the connection
4. neither persisted binding has a `credentials` key
5. the invariant sweep reports no orphans.

Fails before: refresh is keyed per `urlKey`, so there are two mints and two records, and the bindings carry credentials.

**Non-regression arms:**

* A legacy connection-less binding resolves byte-identically.
* `tests/unit/lin-2473-adopt-before-exchange.test.js`, `credential-refusal-non-worsening.test.js`, `workspace-token-refresh.test.js` and `proxy-credential-health-route.test.js` stay green, with only key-fixture changes.
* A new adopt-before-exchange case finds the durable record by connection key.

Blocked by the Connection store (LIN-3127). Blocks the add-from-held-connection flow (LIN-3125) and multi-binding reads (LIN-3126).

### 5. Terms and design decisions

**Terms.** *Connection-backed binding* = `{provider, scope, connectionId}`, no `credentials` key, `typeof connectionId === 'string'`. `connectionId` = `ConnectionStore._id` = `${accountId}::${provider}::${unitId}` (research C1), carried explicitly. *Eligible providers*: linear, jira (OAuth only), github, github-projects; not eligible: local, Jira Basic (token omitted, ruling `04461f8f`), PAT (`isPAT`). *Refresh-token kinds*: linear, jira-OAuth. *Remint kinds*: github, github-projects. *Legacy* = any binding without `connectionId`. *Session-resident workspace* = the object inside `req.session.workspaces` (after `upsertWorkspace` on an existing id this is a new object, not the caller's local variable).

**D1. Hydration seam: per-request side-table.** Module-level WeakMaps, keyed per binding and per workspace, in the store-free `lib/connection-binding.js` (D15; written only from `lib/connection-credential.js`), filled by one global middleware after the session middleware (one batched read of the session's connection-backed Connections; none for legacy-only sessions). Sync accessors (`getWorkspaceToken`, `getWorkspaceCallScope`, `getWorkspaceMirrorToken`, `getWorkspaceTokenExpiry`, and the per-binding `getBindingCredentials` from D15) consult it and otherwise evaluate the verbatim legacy expression. The credential is never a property of a session object. Backstop: `sanitizeSessionForPersist` in both session write paths strips `accessToken`/`credentials`/`tokenExpiresAt` from any workspace or binding carrying `connectionId` (sanitize and log, never throw). An unhydrated connection-backed workspace fails closed. Pending pre-establish copies (§2) are outside its scope by design. *Rejected:* property hydration on `req.session.workspaces` (`resave:false` re-saves it); async read seams (37 signature changes, no structural guarantee); resolve-only-in-`resolveWorkspaceAccess` (leaves the browser lane on session copies).

**D2. Active-binding identity:** `activeBinding` **marker.** Legacy: token-equality, unchanged. Connection-backed: a session-resident `workspace.activeBinding = {provider, scope}` set by the converter (first link, or a link of the active provider, mirroring `linkProvider`'s `isActive` rule), `setActiveProvider` and `unlinkProvider`. Selection order: legacy mirror match, then the marker, then the unique connection-backed binding for the provider, else `AMBIGUOUS`. All 5 token-equality sites move behind one `isActiveBinding(workspace, binding)` whose legacy branch is the verbatim expression. *Why:* legacy "last-linked same-provider binding is active" (mirror overwrite) has no equivalent without a marker; plain `AMBIGUOUS` would break a second Jira site add-source, which is user-visible. *Rejected:* token equality (no token on the binding); array order (records first link, not recency).

**D2a. Creation, shape preservation and fallback.**

* A new binding is connection-backed iff the provider is eligible and no legacy binding exists for the same `(provider, scope)`; re-linking a legacy binding stays legacy, nothing converts. Mixed containers exist by design and are not a migration.
* **Two-phase conversion.** Phase A is today's `linkProvider`, in memory, legacy-shaped, no store write (no `accountId` exists yet at 4 seams). Phase B, `convertToConnectionBacked(session, workspaceId, provider, scope, credentials, {refreshToken})`, runs at exactly the existing post-`establishAccount` `writeConnection` positions (`auth.js:293/407`, `github-install-flow.js:648/704/802`, `jira-auth.js:302/626/719/824`, `account-merge.js:143` after its refusal returns), on the session-resident workspace. A refused, conflicted or limit-failed link never reaches phase B, so it persists nothing; the existing session-restore code is untouched.
* Phase B order (D18):
  1. For refresh-token kinds, `putByConnection`.
  2. `link()`: one atomic upsert of the credentials, `origin` and the referent.
  3. Rewrite the binding to `{provider, scope, connectionId}`, strip the scalar mirror (`accessToken`, `credentials`, `tokenExpiresAt`) if the binding is active, and set the marker.

  `removeReferent` is never part of the fallback. D18's table gives the end state after each failed step.

There is exactly one live copy whether finalize succeeds or fails, and every binding keeps a durable refresh path. This holds per session (the session-resident workspace and the session rows the converter can see), apart from residual (c) below, the accepted cross-device case.** A copy is *live* when some binding's refresh lane can read it: a legacy binding reads `acct::urlKey::jira`, a connection-backed binding reads `conn:${connectionId}`. A record no binding or referent *in the session-resident workspace* reaches is *inert for that session*: it is not a second lane there, and the next write to its key overwrites it. First writes come from the converter at the 6 writer seams (`auth.js:288/402`, `account-merge.js:154`, `jira-auth.js:462/681`, and the `routes/test.js:230` seed); `persistOwnerCredential` is not used for connection-backed bindings (it derives `token` from binding credentials and would write `undefined`). Jira OAuth add-source writes its record at `:462` before the site is picked, so that write stays a legacy-keyed **staging record** (`acct::urlKey::jira`), which is the only durable home of the refresh token on this path (`jiraPending.refreshToken` is set only for `mode === 'new'`, `:494`, comment at `:565`). The pick step (`:626`, phase B) therefore uses two methods, both inside `OwnerCredentialStore` (revision 3, replacing `promoteToConnection` wherever it is named: S1, S3, D6(f), T8): `copyToConnection(accountId, urlKey, 'jira', connectionId)` is step 1: read the staged record and `putByConnection`, leaving the staged record untouched (an absent staged record returns `false`, which is a step-1 failure). `finalizePromotion(accountId, urlKey, 'jira', {connectionId, copiedRefreshToken})` is the only place the staged record is deleted (revision 4). It is a compare-and-delete that runs only from the `finalize` thunk the route awaits after step 3 and after `saveSession` resolves, and it deletes only when the connection-keyed record exists and the staged record still holds the copied token (the D2a clause, parts 1-4, has the gate, the copy source, the thunk and the ambiguous-acknowledgement ordering). A step-0 gate means no conversion happens while a legacy OAuth `jira` binding in the session-resident workspace could read the staged record, so within a session the rotating token has exactly one live copy on every path (residual (c) is the accepted cross-device exception, in the D2a clause); the revision-3 rule that skipped finalize in that case is deleted because it left two live copies. A failed or no-op finalize leaves a duplicate that no binding in this session reads (a second live copy under residual (c)) and the next re-auth overwrites or re-finalizes. Both deletes and the copy are inside the store class, so the durable-delete census stays 7, and the D6(f) single-caller pin covers both methods (one caller each, `lib/connection-credential.js`). *Rejected:* keeping Jira add-source legacy (defeats LIN-3125's held connection); carrying the refresh token in `jiraPending` (a session copy of a rotating credential, repealed by LIN-1524).

**D8/D18 finalize seam, end states (revision 4).** Jira OAuth add-source, staged record `S` = `acct::urlKey::jira`, connection-keyed record `C` = `conn:${connectionId}` for the new site B, R1 = the new grant's rotating refresh token, A = another site of the container. "Live" is defined in the D2a clause. Every row is counted **per session** and keeps a durable refresh path for every binding in that session; residual (c), the accepted cross-device case (D2a clause, ruling `lin3124-pr5-gate-scope`), is the exception and is marked in rows 3 and 5-8.

| \# | Case (single- and multi-site alike) | `S` | `C` | Binding B | Live copies of R1 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| G | Legacy OAuth `jira` binding A co-resident (gate) | R1, shared by A and B | none | legacy; A and B refresh from `S` with CAS | 1 (`S`) |
| 1 | Step 1: copy fails, or `S` absent, or accountId mismatch | untouched | none (partial write released; inert if release fails) | legacy, reads `S` | 1 (`S`) |
| 2 | Step 2: `link()` false, re-read says absent | untouched | released; inert if the release fails | legacy, reads `S` | 1 (`S`) |
| 3 | Step 2: `link()` false, re-read says present (committed) | no reader in this session until finalize, then deleted (residual c: another session's legacy binding can read it) | kept | rolled forward to connection-backed | 1 (`C`) |
| 4 | Step 2: `link()` false, re-read fails (residual a) | untouched, live | kept | legacy, reads `S` | 2 until the store returns |
| 5 | `saveSession` rejects | untouched, no reader in this session (residual c: a second live copy if another session's legacy binding reads it) | kept | session unchanged | 1 (`C`); 2 under residual (c) |
| 6 | Finalize fails, or no-op (staged token differs, or `C` absent) | duplicate with no reader in this session (residual c: a second live copy if another session's legacy binding reads it), or a later flow's own grant | kept, live | connection-backed, reads `C` | 1 (`C`); 2 under residual (c) |
| 7 | Success | deleted | live | connection-backed, reads `C` | 1 (`C`); under residual (c), another session's legacy binding loses its only refresh token (re-link notice at its next expiry) |
| 8 | Existing connection-backed B re-auth (row 3), no legacy A | kept, no reader in this session (residual c: a second live copy if another session's legacy binding reads it) | new record kept | connection-backed, no downgrade, retryable error | 1 (`C`); 2 under residual (c) |
| 9 | Existing connection-backed B re-auth, legacy A co-resident (residual b) | R1, read by A | untouched, earlier grant | connection-backed, retryable error | 1 (`S`); `C` keeps its earlier grant |

Two sites on one grant exist only in the legacy shape: rows G and 7 never leave a connection-backed site and a legacy site on the same token. Two connection-backed sites come from two separate authorizations, so each has its own grant and its own record.

**D9. Rotation write order (refresh-token kinds).** Owner CAS first (authority: refresh token, spend-intent), then a monotonic Connection update. If the Connection write fails after a successful owner CAS, the next resolve enters `refreshConnection`, whose durable re-read reuses the rotated record instead of re-spending.

**D10. Durable** `referents`**,** `origin` **and a three-state rule.** `connections.referents = [{urlKey, provider, scope}]`, `$addToSet` on link, index `{'referents.urlKey': 1, 'referents.provider': 1}` (update `db-indexes.test.js`'s `EXCLUDED_COLLECTIONS`). LIN-3127 rows have no `referents` field (`lib/connection-store.js` `put` never sets it). **Absent** = a dual-write row never connection-managed; `[]` = referenced and now empty; **non-empty** = referenced. `link()` is one atomic upsert (`$addToSet` referent, `$set` credentials, `$setOnInsert: {origin:'connection'}`); deletion authority requires `origin:'connection'` and `referents` present with `$size:0`, so a LIN-3127-born row can never be deleted or reported, even after a connection-backed link shares it (retained for LIN-2150). Consumers: `deleteIfUnreferenced`, `onAccountMerged`, `connection_unreferenced` as D3/D4; `readConnectionsByReferent` and `readReferencedConnections` never return absent rows. Legacy `put` skips its credentials `$set` when the row is connection-managed (removes the shared-row race with monotonic `updateCredentials`; a tiny window remains, self-repairing on the next refresh). *Rejected:* counting referents by session scan (wrong after expiry/logout); treating absent as empty (would delete LIN-3127 rows on merge).

**D11.** `CONNECTION_BACKED_WRITES` **(default on) and rollback.** Default on: flag-off is the same code as the D2a fallback, one fallback path not two, and a default-off cutover would leave the new path unexercised. After a code revert, old code cannot read a connection-backed binding, so: (1) set the flag off before or with the revert; (2) list affected workspaces from `connections` with non-empty `referents`; (3) `scripts/revert-connection-backed.js` (dry-run by default, idempotent, tested) writes the Connection's credentials back into the session binding and scalar mirror and, for refresh-token kinds, copies the record to the legacy key; (4) anything skipped is re-linked by the user. Blast radius today is one user (LIN-3127 `04461f8f`).

**D12. Headless provider selection and authorization (finding 5).** `resolveWorkspaceAccess(urlKey, owner)` has no provider argument; the provider is an output. The arm takes it from the same source as today: the owner's session row's `workspace.provider` (`headlessRefreshProvider`, `lib/workspace-token-refresh.js:111`), falling back to `linear` when no row exists (today's post-logout behaviour, "honest rather than complete"). Provider is a mandatory filter on the durable lookup (`readConnectionsByReferent(urlKey, provider)`, `$elemMatch`), strictly narrower than `selectOwnerSessionRow`, so LIN-2640 is not recreated. If the owner's rows disagree on the active provider, candidates are ranked with the existing `isBetterCandidate` (LIN-1982) over each candidate's Connection expiry, because `selectOwnerSessionRow` ranks by a scalar expiry that is 0 on credential-free rows. Same-provider bindings use the D2 marker. Post-logout headless remains Linear-only. `UNSCOPED` callers never reach the arm (D16).

**D13. GitHub retention and cross-device: preserve today's behaviour (finding 11).** Today headless GitHub needs a live session row (`lib/workspace-token-refresh.js:117-131`) and each device's credential lives in its own session binding; `connections` rows are retained forever (LIN-3127) and never deleted. Design: for remint kinds the use authorization is the owner's session row (its binding carries `connectionId`; no `readConnectionsByReferent`); no row means `not_connected`. Referents are add-only and advisory (cache-eviction fan-out only, bounded by repos per installation), never pulled on unlink or removal and never a deletion authority. Consequently GitHub Connection retention is unchanged and device A's unlink or removal cannot affect device B's binding. Preserving this is possible, so no ruling is requested.

**D14 → D17 (revision 2, addendum** `c3f5b914`**).** The arm never returns a failure reason. When no authorized connection matches, it falls through to the unchanged legacy scan and passes a counts-only `connectionSummary {ownerLive, otherLive, storeError}` into an optional `classifyWorkspaceFailure` argument; without that argument the function is byte-identical. `owner_mismatch` holds when neither the owner's legacy rows nor the owner's connections are live, and another account's row or connection is. It is checked first (LIN-1506). A store error together with a failed scan gives `store_unreachable`. Logs carry counts only, never another account's id or any token bytes (LIN-1506, `0ff54c19`).

### 12. Residuals (explicit, with reasons)

* The stale `credentials.token` divergence and Jira's OLD-token call scope after a headless mirror are pre-existing and cited only (credential-defect cluster: LIN-2639, LIN-2642, LIN-2640, LIN-2530, LIN-2394).
* Refresh-token kinds: a removal on one device now fails another device's session immediately instead of after its mirrored token lapses.
* GitHub-family Connection rows are retained indefinitely (as today, LIN-3127); LIN-3127-born rows are never deleted by this ticket, including merge orphans, until LIN-2150.
* Guard limits: dynamic computed method access; regex-literal comment stripping (corpus-checked).
* Legacy `put` vs a concurrent `link()`: a small window, self-repairing on the next refresh.
* Jira add-source stage-and-promote: a crash between `putByConnection` and the legacy delete leaves a bounded duplicate until the next re-auth.
* D18 leaves two residuals:
  * A connection-keyed owner record orphaned when its best-effort delete fails. It is inert and is overwritten on the next conversion.
  * A dangling referent after a failed release. This matches today's failed legacy `deleteAll`: the owner's own grant keeps resolving for that urlKey.
* **D18 residual (c), cross-device legacy reader (accepted by ruling** `lin3124-pr5-gate-scope`**; user-visible; Flag C).** Another session row of the same owner can hold a legacy OAuth `jira` binding for the same `urlKey`, which reads the staged record `S` that the step-0 gate (scoped to the session-resident workspace) does not see. On success (row 7) finalize deletes that binding's only refresh token, so the other device shows a re-link notice at its next expiry; on rows 5, 6 and 8 `S` is a second live copy of R1; a concurrent add-source on another device can re-stage `S` between the callback and a multi-site pick. No legacy support and no cross-session checks are added; the invariant and `liveCopies` hold per session. Full statement and path:line evidence: the D2a clause, residual (c). (a) and (b) are also stated there.
* Legacy GitHub `missing` sweep noise until LIN-2150; cross-process duplicate GitHub mints (idempotent); GitHub mint-failure revocation taxonomy (retain); whole-account Connection deletion (no such path); Jira Basic omit lift (human ruling; a delete path now exists for refresh-token kinds only); multi-binding active resolution beyond the marker (LIN-3126); migration of legacy bindings (LIN-2150).
* Not touched: the credential-defect cluster above, cited only.

**Migration-trigger check:** nothing in this plan moves existing workspaces onto the connection model. Legacy bindings and legacy owner records keep their shape and read path; re-linking a legacy binding stays legacy; every new arm and guard keys on an explicit `connectionId`; the `upsertWorkspace`/`linkProvider` guards, the `put` skip and the `origin` marker are identity functions on legacy-only data; only bindings created after the cutover are connection-backed.

**Recommended next action:** `plan-review`, a confirmation pass limited to the revision-4a text (residual (c) in D2a/D18, D8's table and §12; the corrected wording; T20 scoping and T20(k); Flag C).

## LIN-3124 plan: revision 3 (narrow), grounded at `b0751689`

Against pass-3 Plan Review Verdict `3b83f17c`, under Con ruling `lin3124-pr3-revise` = authorize-revision (scope: only D18 row 2 and T20/T21). `origin/main` is still `b0751689bb2d1d01b65291182bea62b72202c570` (0 commits since); the blocking finding was re-verified against source there (`routes/jira-auth.js:461-467` staging write, `:494`/`:565` `jiraPending.refreshToken` for `mode === 'new'` only, `:626` phase B).

**What changed in `## Implementation Plan` (in place; nothing else touched)**
- **§0:** a revision-3 entry citing `3b83f17c` and the ruling.
- **D8:** `promoteToConnection` splits into `copyToConnection` (step 1: read the staged legacy record, `putByConnection`, staged record untouched) and `finalizePromotion` (the only legacy staging delete). Finalize runs only after step 3 and the session save succeed. Both are inside `OwnerCredentialStore`, so the durable-delete census stays 7 and the D6(f) single-caller pin covers both.
- **D18 row 2 (amendment under D2a):** on a step-2 failure for a new binding, release the connection-keyed copy via `releaseOrphanOwnerRecord` and leave the staged record as today's legacy record, so the fallback binding keeps refreshing. Also stated: step 1 failure, existing connection-backed re-auth (row 3: record kept, finalize skipped), session-save failure (finalize not run), finalize failure or skip.
- **T20:** cases (a)-(f) for the multi-site Jira add-source pick: `link()` false leaves a legacy binding that refreshes from the staged record after expiry; release failure; success ordering copy, link, save, finalize with one record left; save rejection; co-resident legacy Jira binding; finalize failure.
- **T21:** existing connection-backed `(jira, site)` re-auth with a failing `link()`, plus failure injection at each Jira pick step against the row-2 end states.

**Two details beyond the verdict's wording, both in the conservative direction (drop them if the reviewer objects)**
- Finalize runs after `saveSession`, not just after step 3, so a failed save leaves today's state exactly.
- Finalize is skipped while the workspace still holds a legacy Jira binding: the staged record is keyed per `(account, urlKey, provider)`, not per site, so a legacy binding for another site reads that same record.

**Not written (carried as implementation obligations / for the next reviewer)**, per the ruling:
1. D15 count is 22 not 24, plus the two unnamed readers (`lib/workspace-token-resolver.js:62`, `lib/workspace.js:782-785`).
2. D18 ambiguous acknowledgement (`link()` false after a committed write): re-read and roll forward, else a stated residual with a T21 case.
3. D18 row-2 residual wording: an orphaned connection-keyed record "may persist indefinitely; holds a copy of the same grant's refresh token" (`deleteAll` filters `{accountId, urlKey}`).
4. D17 edges: `store_unreachable` for legacy during a connections outage (with a legacy-only T25(e) case) and stale GitHub referents (T25 case).

Non-blocking 5-8 of `3b83f17c` are also unchanged and carried. The ticket's acceptance criteria are unedited.

**Next action: `plan-review`** (fresh-context reviewer).

### Plan Review Verdict

**Request Changes.** Revision 3 fixes the pass-3 blocker for the failure paths. But its own new "skip finalize while a legacy Jira binding remains" rule leaves two durable copies of one rotating Jira refresh token on a **normal success path**, so one of two Jira sites stops refreshing after the first rotation. The fix is a one-clause change at the same seam and needs no product call.

This is **pass 4**, a fresh-context, narrow review of revision 3 (comment `024e53f5`) against pass-3 verdict `3b83f17c`, under Con ruling `lin3124-pr3-revise` (`57d93579`/`f0ac9d4b`). Scope: D8's copy/finalize split, D18 row 2, and T20/T21. Blocking findings 1–3 of `71050cc5` are not re-litigated; revision 3 did not regress them.

**Grounding.** `origin/main` has moved from `b0751689` to `6430c620`: 9 commits (LIN-3130 S2a, LIN-3133 T1). None touches a credential read, write, refresh or delete path, `routes/jira-auth.js`, `lib/owner-credential-store.js`, `lib/workspace*.js`, `server.js`, `routes/test.js` or `account-merge.js`. The only drift in cited files is line shifts:
- `routes/proxy.js:733/744` → `:735/746`
- `lib/dispatch-factory.js:523` → `:528`
- `routes/dispatch.js:524` → `:485`

D16's claims still hold. `getWorkspaceAccessToken` is injected only at `server.js:2047` into the `workspaceFromUrl`-gated `POST /workspace/:urlKey/api/dispatch` (`routes/dispatch.js:234`), and the new `routes/proxy-runner.js` doesn't use it. **Not stale.**

#### Verified against source (`6430c620`)
- **Staging write.** `jira-auth.js:461-467` writes the refresh token only to `acct::urlKey::jira`. `jiraPending.refreshToken` is set only for `mode === 'new' && sites.length > 1` (`:494`). The multi-site pick passes `pending.refreshToken` (`undefined` on add-source, `:523`). Phase B is at `:626`, after `linkProvider` (`:616`) and before `saveSession` (`:633`).
- **Row by row, for a new binding with no co-resident legacy Jira binding:**
  - copy fails or the staged record is absent: staged record untouched, today's path.
  - `link()` returns false: copy released, staged record kept, legacy binding refreshes from it.
  - release fails: the copy is inert and the staged record still refreshes.
  - session save fails: `saveSession` rejects (`lib/workspace.js:263-267`), finalize doesn't run and the staged record is intact.
  - finalize fails: the connection-backed binding holds its own record, and the staged duplicate has no reader.

  **No step leaves that binding without a durable refresh token, and every fallback matches today.**
- **Row 3** (existing connection-backed re-auth): the new record is kept and the staged record stays. This is consistent with D9 (connection-keyed record is the authority; the `refreshConnection` re-read) and T8's "CAS loser converges and never deletes".
- **Durable-delete census stays 7.** The census scans only `server.js` and `routes/workspace.js` for `ownerCredentialStore.delete(All)?(` (`tests/unit/owner-credential-durable-delete-census.test.js:73-86`). The 7 sites are unchanged (`server.js:1124/1154/1457/1746/3763`, `routes/workspace.js:150/166`). Both new methods live in the store class and are called from `lib/connection-credential.js`.
- **D6(f).** D8 states a single-caller pin for `copyToConnection` and for `finalizePromotion`.
- **Consistency.** No inconsistency with D4, D9, D10 or the other D18 rows, apart from the finding below.

#### Blocking (correct before implementation)
1. **D8 finalize-skip × rotating refresh tokens: a co-resident legacy Jira OAuth binding and the new connection-backed binding each refresh from their own copy of one rotating grant.**
   - **Where both copies come from.** The owner-credential key is per `(account, urlKey, provider)`, not per site (`lib/owner-credential-store.js:89-90`). The add-source callback therefore overwrites the legacy site-A record with the new grant R1 (`jira-auth.js:462`). Today both Jira sites then refresh from that single record.
   - **What revision 3 does.** It copies R1 into the connection-keyed record for site B. It then skips finalize because site A is still legacy (D8, T20(e)). Two durable records now hold R1, refreshed by two independent lanes:
     - site A: legacy `doOwnerRefresh` plus `putIfRefreshToken` on `acct::urlKey::jira`;
     - site B: `refreshConnection` on key `conn:${connectionId}`, CAS on the connection-keyed record.

     Each lane's CAS protects only its own record.
   - **Why that breaks a site.** Atlassian refresh tokens rotate (`lib/providers/jira/oauth.js:8,32,271-277`). The repo already treats a spent token as dead past the reuse grace, with possible chain revocation (`lib/workspace-token-refresh.js:321-327`). So the first rotation by either lane leaves the other with a dead R1. Within about an hour that site stops refreshing, or is classified as a definitive revocation: D4 deletes the Connection for B, and `server.js:1124/1154` delete the record for A.
   - **Impact.** This happens on the **success path** for any workspace that already holds a legacy Jira OAuth site and adds a second site. It is user-visible, it isn't today's behaviour, and T20(e) as written would pass while site B breaks. Revision 2's promote-and-delete had the same class of problem in the opposite direction (A lost its record immediately), and pass 3 didn't flag it.
   - **Correction (plan text only, at the same seam):**
     - **D8 / D18 row 2:** at the Jira pick seam (`:626`), if the session-resident workspace holds any legacy (connection-less) **OAuth** `jira` binding, don't attempt conversion. The new site takes the legacy fallback exactly as today, so both sites share the single `acct::urlKey::jira` record. This extends D2a's "no legacy binding for the same `(provider, scope)`" rule to "no legacy OAuth binding for `jira`" at this seam, because the legacy key is per provider. A Basic binding reads no owner record and need not block.
     - The finalize-skip then can't be reached. Keep it only as a defensive assert.
     - **Rewrite T20(e):** with a co-resident legacy Jira OAuth binding, the new site's binding is legacy, there is exactly one owner record, and after a forced rotation by **either** binding the other still refreshes.

#### Non-blocking (implementation obligations)
1. **Where finalize is called.** `saveSession` is called by the route (`jira-auth.js:633`), not by the converter. Name the post-save hook, for example a `finalize` thunk that `convertToConnectionBacked` returns and the route awaits after `saveSession`, so the store call stays in `lib/connection-credential.js` and D6(f)'s single-caller pin holds. T20(c)'s spy order depends on this.
2. **Ambiguous acknowledgement × revision 3** (carried item 2).
   - When `link()` returns false, re-read with `readConnectionById` **before** releasing the copy. A roll-forward must keep the copy: releasing it and then finalizing deletes the only refresh token.
   - Make that impossible by construction: `finalizePromotion` deletes the staged record only if `getByConnection(connectionId)` returns a record.
3. **Fallback must not call `persistOwnerCredential`.** The addendum's generic row-1 fallback names `persistOwnerCredential`. At `:626` the refresh token is `undefined` for multi-site add-source, and `put` `$set`s it (`lib/owner-credential-store.js:220-231`), which would overwrite the staged token. Today this seam never calls it (`jira-auth.js:437-449`). State that; T20(a)'s byte-equal assertion already catches it.
4. **Single-site add-source.** It reaches the same seam with `tokenBag.refresh_token` as an argument (`jira-auth.js:499-500`). State whether the converter copies from the staged record or the argument (one source keeps one path), and run T20(a)/(c) for single-site too.
5. **Which accountId the copy reads.** The staging write uses the pre-`establishAccount` `req.session.accountId` (`:462`). `establishAccount` can canonicalize it (`lib/account-session.js:128`). A copy under `established.accountId` then finds nothing, which is a step-1 fallback: conservative and matching today. State it.
6. **Text drift and test labels.**
   - S1, S3, T8 and D6(f) still name `promoteToConnection`; D8's replacement clause covers them. T8 should assert that copy and finalize are idempotent, including finalize on an absent staged record being a no-op.
   - T20(a)/(b)/(d) are parity pins: they pass at the pre-change SHA by design and fail against revision 2's ordering. T20(c)/(f) and T21's row-3 case are new-code tests. The "new" label is fine.
7. **Same question outside this scope.** The new-login existing-container seam (`jira-auth.js:681/719`, second site for a container that already has a legacy Jira site) raises the same per-provider-key co-residence question. Apply the same rule there, or state why it's safe.

**Carried from `3b83f17c` as implementation obligations** (unchanged by revision 3, per `024e53f5`):
1. The D15 count is 22, not 24, and the omitted readers are `lib/workspace-token-resolver.js:62` and `lib/workspace.js:782-785`.
2. D18 ambiguous acknowledgement; see non-blocking 2 above for the ordering.
3. Reword the D18 row-2 orphan residual to "may persist indefinitely; holds a copy of the same grant's refresh token".
4. D17 edges: legacy `store_unreachable` during a connections outage (T25(e)) and stale GitHub referents (T25).
5. D17 naming and `diag` counts.
6. D6(a) allow-list for `releaseOrphanOwnerRecord`, and whether it counts toward `KNOWN_CONNECTION_RELEASE_COUNT`.
7. Description drift: S2, S4, §11 PR1/PR3 rows and §3 LIN-1885.
8. Align the session-fit stop-loss with the ~3.5-session PR3 price.

The carried items from `71050cc5` (3, 6–14) stand as well.

#### For the human (criteria unedited)
- **Flag A** (assertion 3 doesn't track for GitHub) and **Flag B** ("no orphans" isn't sweep vocabulary) remain open with their stated interpretations.
- **User-visible edge awaiting acceptance:** Jira Basic add-source over a connection-backed OAuth `(jira, site)` now shows a refusal page. The Jira Basic omit ruling is unchanged.
- **Convergence:** blocking findings went 11, then 4, then 1, and now 1. The new one is in revision 3's own added text and has an exact fix inside the ruling's scope (D8/D18 row 2 and T20).

Handoff: `plan` (narrow fix to blocking 1: the D8/D18 row-2 clause and T20(e)), then `plan-review`.

**Con ruling (Flight Companion, for John):** `lin3124-pr4-revise` = **authorize-revision**. A fourth narrow revision covers the D8/D18 finalize clause and T20/T21. The rule: exactly one live copy of a rotating refresh token on every path. The blockers went 11, 4, 1, 1, and the last is new but at the same seam. **Bound:** any further blocker at the D8/D18 seam on pass 5 parks it for John as a design question.

**The D8/D18 design, in brief.**
- When a Jira OAuth site is added as a source, today's code writes its rotating refresh token only to a legacy "staged" owner record keyed `account::urlKey::jira`.
- The cutover copies that token into a connection-keyed record (`copyToConnection`), links the Connection, rewrites the binding, saves the session, and then deletes the staged record (`finalizePromotion`).
- The invariant is that a rotating refresh token is never duplicated and never deleted: exactly one live copy.
- Revisions 3 and 4 made that hold **within one session**. For example, revision 4's step-0 gate keeps a new site legacy if this session already holds a legacy OAuth Jira binding.

**The open problem (pass 5).** Bindings live per device, in each session row, but the staged record is shared by the owner's legacy Jira bindings across **every** session row.
- On the success path, finalize can delete the only refresh token that a legacy Jira site on **another device** refreshes from.
- On the failure rows, the "inert" staged record can be a second live copy.
- Fixing this needs a cross-session reader check or a different ownership model for the staged record. That is a design choice at a credential boundary, not a one-clause edit.

The question: may a `dispatch`-holding token cause a new `dispatch` grant for an orchestrator-shaped child (child autopilot, passage-runner leg, SD refire of an orchestrator item)?

T2c may be designed and built against the provisional answer. It must **not merge** until John confirms on LIN-2884 or in Rulings. If John rules "no child dispatch grant", this slice is re-planned on LIN-2884, not adapted here.

## Scope (named)

* ~~**M3**~~ **DROPPED, not in scope** (LIN-2884 `95d748fa`; what is left belongs with LIN-3099's passage-runner/lane surfaces, and T3 LIN-3136 carries a source-sweep merge guard). Original text: **M3, proxy launch verbs** (`routes/proxy-dispatch.js`, launch `attachProxyContext` at `:495/:934/:1205` at `fd528742`). Children stay **leaf and grant-less** unless the launch is a **server-declared orchestrator launch verb** for passage-runner or lane.
  * That verb is not a client field and is not keyed on `kind` alone (D1).
  * It is owner-checked through `mintGrantBootstrap`, and only when the enqueuer holds `dispatch` (or is the owner's session).
  * Leaf workers never get it. Lanes are leaf by default (D3).
* **R2, refire broker** (`POST /api/dispatch/broker-token`, `routes/dispatch.js:1454`, mint `:1486` at `fd528742`).
  * Accept an item id from SD.
  * The server reads `getGrantDeclaration` and re-mints declared-or-plain through `provisionResumeCredential`, using the **recorded** owner, not `req.dispatchTokenOwner`.
* **Simple Dispatcher change (required).** SD's broker caller (`simple-dispatcher/feedback.js:98`, the `POST /api/dispatch/broker-token` fetch; related: `reapers.js` broker arm) sends the item id.
* **Interim behavior** until this lands: the refire stays grant-less and documented ("refire of an orchestrator needs a fresh launch").

## Constraints

* It uses only T2's artifacts (`getGrantDeclaration`, `provisionResumeCredential`, the `declaredGrants` preamble branch). No new mint path, no new grant vocabulary.
* The declaration is server-side. A client can never name a grant or an orchestrator verb that widens authority.
* The owner is the recorded owner on every re-mint, never the live owner and never the poster.
* An ordinary child of a `dispatch`-holding token is grant-less (acceptance 4: exchange never adds a grant).

- *(M3's two criteria are removed: M3 is dropped from LIN-2884 by decision* `95d748fa`*.)*

### Strategy framing

The strategy is unchanged and fixed by LIN-2884 rev 4 plus T2's artifacts (`getGrantDeclaration`, `provisionResumeCredential`, `mintGrantBootstrap`): the broker route reads the declaration itself, then branches (a record enters the helper; anything else takes today's inline `createToken`). Rationale unchanged: the helper's no-record path goes through `provisionBootstrapToken`, which returns a bare string (no `expiresAt`) and would not be byte-identical to today's grant-less mint.

* **Cost of doing it:** one route branch, one census row, one docs section, plus a credential-returning surface that the new caller bound (below) closes. LIN-3136 (T3) is blocked by this ticket.
* **Cost of not doing it:** after T3 a stall-failsafe refire of a declared orchestrator (M1/M2/M4 launches) comes back grant-less, so the refire cannot enqueue and needs a fresh launch. That is the documented interim, and it stays until S3 also lands.
* **Routed-around contract gap:** none identified. The revised caller-bound analysis resolves F1 inside this slice rather than routing around it. It does not conclude that "any workspace dispatch token" suffices, so nothing is raised as Needs Discussion on LIN-2884. One operator precondition follows from the bound and is documented, not a gap: a declared refire needs an owner-stamped runner token (same precondition as LIN-1448 part 1).

### Caller bound (F1, resolved here)

**What the route can hand out.** A declared re-mint returns, in the HTTP response itself, a 48h `worker`-profile bootstrap that exchanges for a 48h working token carrying `dispatch`, stamped `createdBy` = the recorded owner. Verified at `ac3ac010`: `authenticateDispatchToken` (`routes/dispatch.js:154`) only proves "a valid dispatch token for this urlKey"; dispatch tokens are minted by any workspace member (`routes/dispatch.js:1152`, `createdBy = req.session?.accountId || null`, label free text, default `'default'`) until T4; the route has no limiter. So without a bound, any such token could re-mint for any declared row in its workspace, active or history (history retention 30 days, `lib/dispatch-store.js:248`). The owner check in `mintGrantBootstrap` (`lib/proxy-tokens.js:375-399`) validates the RECORDED owner against the workspace owner; it says nothing about the caller, so it is not a caller bound.

**Rule.** The declared branch (lookup state `record`) is taken only when BOTH hold; otherwise the route refuses and mints nothing.

* **B1, authority (the "owner's session" limb):** the record's `ownerAccountId` is a non-empty string AND `req.dispatchTokenOwner === record.ownerAccountId`. The caller's dispatch token was created by the recorded owner's own signed-in session (`createdBy` is stamped from `req.session.accountId`), i.e. it is the owner's own credential. This is the only place the live owner is read; it gates, it never mints (the mint owner stays the recorded one, and `mintGrantBootstrap` still re-checks that the recorded owner is the current workspace owner).
* **B2, session binding (the taker):** `dispatchQueueStore.getItemStatus(req.dispatchUrlKey, itemId)` (existing read, `lib/dispatch-store.js:575`) returns a row with `status === 'taken'` AND `takenByTokenLabel === req.dispatchTokenLabel` AND `deriveTerminalStatus(item.feedback) === null` (`lib/dispatch-terminal.js:126`, the watch endpoint's own terminal predicate). This is the `addFeedback` ownership precedent (`lib/dispatch-store.js:2199-2201`, LIN-3130 S2a.2) applied as a read, on this row's own feedback (no lineage merge, so the id must be the current live row of the session; a row already terminal, expired, cancelled or still queued is refused).

**How this satisfies the ruling** (`lin2884-orchestrator-dispatch-grant` = `declared-kinds`: mint only "when the enqueuer holds `dispatch` or is the owner's session", owner-checked):

* The enqueue-time limb is discharged when the record is written: a record exists only because an owner-checked declared mint happened at a launch that T3 gates on `dispatch` (until T3 nothing writes one). The refire is not a new enqueue, so this route does not re-decide it.
* The refire-time limb is B1: the caller is the owner's own credential, not "any holder of a dispatch token". Members' tokens and ownerless tokens are refused.
* B2 adds "the runner that took this live session", which is the same authority `take` already conferred: `takeItem` returns the item to whoever takes it, with the declared bootstrap either as `bootstrapToken` (`_formatItem`, `lib/dispatch-store.js:2734`, claude-code harness) or inside the prompt prose (other harnesses), so a live taker already holds that authority. The re-mint restores it to the same session; it adds none. It also bounds the window to the session's lifetime instead of the 30-day history retention.

**On mismatch:** `403 { code: 'REFIRE_CALLER_NOT_PERMITTED', retryable: false }` via `jsonError` (same shape as the structural relay at `routes/dispatch.js:703`), never a grant-less mint. Server log `[dispatch] broker-declared-remint-refused` with `urlKey`, `itemId` and a reason (`owner-mismatch` | `not-taker` | `terminal` | `status-unreadable`), ids only. One generic body for all four reasons, so the response does not say which condition failed.

**Population handling (each pinned by a test below):**

| Caller / item state | Outcome |
| -- | -- |
| No `itemId` (old SD) | Today's inline grant-less `createToken`, byte-identical; no store read |
| `itemId`, lookup `none` / `row-missing` (leaf, or the T2 residual) | Today's inline grant-less mint for ANY caller. Same authority as the no-id call, and same response, so it leaks nothing about which ids carry a record |
| Ownerless compat-lane token (`req.dispatchTokenOwner === null`) + record with a usable owner | B1 fails → 403. Strict lane (`DISPATCH_OWNERLESS_BROKER_COMPAT=off`) still 503s first, as today, before any lookup |
| Member-owned dispatch token (`createdBy` ≠ recorded owner) + record | B1 fails → 403 even if its label matches the taker's |
| Owner-created token, different label, or item still queued | B2 fails → 403 |
| Owner-created token that took the item, live (also history-only rows: a taken row is normally history-only, this is the expected case) | Declared re-mint |
| Terminal / expired / cancelled row, even one this caller took | B2 fails → 403 |
| Ownerless RECORD (owner missing or empty) | B1 is skipped (there is no usable owner to compare); the helper refuses `GRANT_OWNERLESS` 503. Nothing is minted either way |
| Recorded owner no longer workspace owner (A→B) | B1/B2 pass, `mintGrantBootstrap` refuses `GRANT_OWNER_ONLY` 403, relayed; no plain mint |

**Named residuals (not widened, recorded):** (1) `takenByTokenId` is not exposed by `_formatHistoryItem`, so B2 cannot tell a dispatch-token take from a proxy-runner take carrying the same label; B1 confines that to owner-created tokens, which already hold the owner's authority. Not solved by adding a field to the read allow-list in this slice. (2) A dispatch-token holder racing the runner to `take` a queued declared item is pre-existing and T3/T4's; it already receives the declared bootstrap from `take`. (3) `getItemStatus` swallows read faults into `null`, so a fault at B2 refuses `403 status-unreadable` (closed) rather than `503`; SD treats any non-2xx as "mint failed" and falls back to today's token-less refire. (4) No limiter is added to the route; B1/B2 make it unnecessary, and limiter policy is T3/T4's.
